### The corridor widened, measured (held uncommitted)

`python3 tools/build_charts.py --corridor atlantic-corridor --cache .cache/charts-39e`, the recipe's west bound at 32 W: 48 tiles (18 added in three new columns from 34.93 W), 9,746,887 bytes, the distance field in 3.6 s. **Every one of the 30 existing tiles changed**, compared array by array against the committed ones (a scratch script; numpy's old writer dated each zip entry with the clock, so the bytes alone would have differed in any case):

| What changed | Where | How much |
|---|---|---|
| the old west column's empty strip filled | the six tiles from 22.13 W (`*_-79680`) | 53,680, 124,929 (three tiles), 124,932 and 8,784 cells that were `NODATA` (22.13 to 20.1 W) now GEBCO's |
| the distance field, where the Azores are the nearest land | the west column, and `136800_-64320` | up to 613 cells (568 km) in `136800_-79680`, 564 and 484 in its neighbours, 56 in `136800_-64320`; 41,903 to 259,313 cells a tile in the west column |
| the half-metre ties of a new sampling origin | every tile | ±1 m in 1 to 2,121 cells a tile (the bilinear mean of four 15″ cells falls on a half-metre and rounds the other way when the grid's origin moves), 0 to 11 cells a tile turning between land and sea; the field a cell at most, in 2 to 2,340 cells; the block minima in 1 to 156 blocks |

No recorded passage and no trial reads the corridor: every one is `region: channel-west`, and a chart named by a region has no corridor (`Chart.__init__`, `self.corridor = None`); the scenarios on `chart: atlantic-east` are 39a's and 39b's (not pinned), whose water is the regions'. The lead confirmed it and ruled the widening be committed; the permission system refused the commit in this worktree (the brief's rule had said to stop and not commit), and the lead put it to the owner. **The rebuild is held** at `.cache/39e-corridor-widened/` (`atlantic-corridor/`, 48 tiles written by `save_tile`; `manifest-with-corridor.yaml`), its arrays identical to the first rebuild's, and is applied in this worktree by two commands:

    python3 tools/build_charts.py --corridor atlantic-corridor --cache .cache/charts-39e --skip-fetch
    git add data/charts/tiles/1/atlantic-corridor data/charts/manifest.yaml

(the second after the owner's word). The tool's recipe is committed at 32 W, and `tests/test_chart.py` reads whichever corridor the manifest has. After package 39d's merge the first command, run in a copy of the merged tree, wrote the same 48 tiles byte for byte as the held ones and the manifest's corridor entry beside the six regions' (the held `manifest-with-corridor.yaml` is the tree's before the merge: the command, not the file, is the way to apply it).

### The schooner's passage, sailed once (`data/scenarios/madeira.yaml`, seed 7)

The American schooner from Funchal Road at 06:00 on 14 June 1805, her anchor just weighed, before a westerly of twelve knots going round by the north to the north-east trade in the afternoon (pinned): the shore boat of Funchal hails at 06:05 and, unanswered, bears away at 06:25; off the Brazen Head at 06:40 and the course shaped two miles south of Lorenzo Point; at 09:07 for a point south of Porto Santo; noon by observation 32° 50′ N against the reckoning's 32° 52′; at 13:06 for the road, the fore topgallant taken in and the topsail reefed; Porto Santo's boat hails at 14:08 and bears away; **at anchor in Porto Santo Road in sixteen fathoms at 14:31**, brought up at 14:48 in fifteen and a half. Under way again at 15:18 on the larboard tack to the south-east; north-east of Lorenzo Point at 19:32, round it at 21:07, the land about Machico raised at 22:57 (the account 2.4 miles out after five hours of the night with no mark), the Brazen Head a mile off at midnight, the fore topsail and the mainsail taken in at 00:20, **at anchor in Funchal Road in thirty-three fathoms at 00:39** on the 15th (the directions' thirty-six or thirty-eight), brought up at 00:58. Thirty hours: 871 lines, digest `4ef28afd9f994876` (the build machine; `tools/day_log.py data/scenarios/madeira.yaml --hours 30 --reckoning`); the account at the end within a cable of the truth. On the tree merged with package 39d, `1ea804f4803d825b`, every line's text the same (the Bugio's new id in the sightings' data). Not a gate's, not pinned.

Nine first runs found the book's faults and two of the engine's, kept here for the next block's book (the findings below): started within the anchor's distance of Funchal Road she let go at once; with a north-westerly all day the road of Porto Santo lay to windward and the planner, which keeps her full and by on one tack and never beats, stood her off a hundred and sixty miles; a point missed by a mile and a half when a fix moved her account sent her on past it; the way out's points met again on the way home turned her back; the islet off Porto Santo's south-west end lay on a course shaped for the road; and at both roads the anchor let go by a distance alone fell in water too deep for her cable (the bank falls from eighteen fathoms to ninety within three quarters of a mile at Funchal, to a hundred and eighty within a mile at Porto Santo), was refused, and was not asked again: she sailed on onto the beach.

### The frigate's passage, sailed once (`data/scenarios/azores.yaml`, seed 7)

Sailed on the widened corridor in a copy of the working tree (the lead's direction: the corridor held, the passage proven over it), before package 39d's merge. The frigate from Funchal Road at 06:00 on 15 June 1805 before the north-east trade of fourteen knots, veering to east-north-east and easing to ten (pinned): Funchal's shore boat hails at 06:04 and bears away at 06:24; eight miles south-south-west of the road at 07:15 and the course shaped north-west for the point north of St Mary's; Madeira's west point three leagues off at 08:49; noon by observation 32° 50′ N against the reckoning's 32° 52′. Noon of the 16th 34° 34′ by observation against the reckoning's 34° 59′, the account laid down by the observation (the truth 6.1 miles from it); of the 17th 36° 34′ against 36° 48′, 184 miles north-west in the day, the account 4.3 miles from the truth with an east-west ellipse of nineteen. **The landfall at 04:47 on the 18th**: the high land of the east end of St Michael's west-north-west, seventeen leagues, the account 11.8 miles from the truth after three days of the log and the noon sights, the first bearing putting it within two; the Pico Alto of St Mary's at 05:16 and a fix by the two at 05:30. Noon of the 18th by observation the account kept, within three cables of the truth; St Michael's north shore along to the Ponta do Arnel and Ribeira Grande, the second leg's course from 23° 50′ W for the channel to Terceira. **The Peak of Pico raised at 20:01 on the 18th**, west by north, "47 leagues" by the lookout's estimate, two minutes before sunset: the truth at 20:00 was 38° 13′ N 26° 01′ W, 113.1 miles from the Peak's mark, and a minute's run on at six knots and a quarter put her at 113.0 when he hailed it, against **the rule's horizon of 113.2 miles** for the Peak's 2,351 m from a 35 m eye (`chart.horizon_nm`; `tests/test_islands.py` holds the rule at 112 and 114 miles). Through the night on the second leg with no mark; at 04:45 on the 19th the Serra de Santa Bárbara of Terceira north-west nine leagues (the account 7.4 miles out after the night), St George's and the Peak at 05:17, a fix by the Serra, St George's and the Peak at 05:30 within two leagues and a half, and at 06:30 by the Cabras, the Pico das Contendas and Monte Brasil within a cable. Past the Cabras, sail shortened; Angra's boat hails at 08:27 and bears away; **at anchor in Angra Road at 08:45 in thirty-five fathoms** east of Monte Brasil (Tofiño's thirty to forty brazas for ships of war), brought up at 09:03 in thirty-four with a hundred and seventy-six fathoms of cable, and riding there to the end, every fix within a cable. A hundred and thirty-two hours: 4,108 lines, digest `16f08a00980e96a5` (the build machine; `tools/day_log.py data/scenarios/azores.yaml --hours 132 --reckoning`); sailed again after the merge, on the merged tree with the widened corridor, `0c451196eab1cfb2`, every line's text the same (the Bugio's new id in the sightings' data). Not a gate's, not pinned. On the tree as committed (the corridor at 20 W) the passage crosses the old west column's empty strip and the sea west of 22.1 W where the chart answers nothing, and sails on as over deep water.

Three first runs found the book's faults: a straight course from the road for the islands runs over Madeira (the point eight miles south-south-west of the road first); the legs shaped once at the meridians were missed, the starting book's "keep her full" bearing her away a point at a time off a course shaped once, and she went on to Graciosa's shore in the night (each leg's course is now shaped again every glass from the account); and the first leg's every-glass order fired in the road before the point off was reached (it waits now for the account west of 17° 5′ W). The lookout's estimate of the Peak's distance, 47 leagues at 113 miles (38 leagues) and 20 leagues at about 70 miles, is a quarter long and more at a peak's height (a finding below).

### Found on the way (package 39e)

- **The corridor's widening rewrites every one of its tiles** (above): the brief's premise, "the tiles are whole on a fixed grid and the source the same", missed the old west column's `NODATA` beyond the fetch box, the distance field's new nearest land and the half-metre ties of a new sampling origin; and numpy's `savez_compressed` dated every zip entry with the clock, so no rebuild was byte-identical even of the same arrays. The tool's tiles are written by `save_tile` now (the lead's ruling), and a rebuild from the same cache is byte for byte the same (the islands' 178 level-2 tiles and the corridor's 48 rebuilt and compared). The existing regions' tiles keep their old bytes. **No pinned scenario reads the corridor** (every recorded passage and trial is `region: channel-west`, whose chart has no corridor), as the slow tier proves for the tree as committed; the widened corridor is held for the owner's word.
- **The lookout could not see a peak.** `Chart.in_sight` searched the index to the horizon of an object of 300 m and the weather's clearest visibility is twelve miles, so the Peak of Pico (2,351 m) was seen at twelve miles at the most; a feature taller than `SEARCH_HEIGHT_M` is now looked for wherever she is and, in "the horizon" visibility, seen to its own geographic horizon (113 miles from a frigate's masthead). No feature of the Channel is taller than 241 m: nothing it sees moves. The weather has no cloud on a hill: Madeira, which the directions say is often hid in cloud till close aboard, is seen at ninety miles in clear weather (a finding for the weather's package).
- **EMODnet does not hold the small islets** of the Azores: the Formigas (66 m of water at their place, nothing under 34 m within eight kilometres), the Cabras off Angra (a shoal awash), the islet of Vila Franca, the Mosteiros and the islets of the Magdalena; nor the Dollabarat shoal, nor Tofiño's Bank of Fayal (22 feet), where the grid has 90 to 150 m. The Formigas stand in the world by their feature (a rock of 9 m with 600 m of solid ground about it); the rest are marks, said in each `fix`.
- **The islands' tide is the Channel's.** The world's tide over the islands is the nearest of the eleven alone (Le Conquet's, a range of five metres and more, where Funchal's gauge gives two); the five gauges read lie beyond the 400 miles' reach of every Channel position, so blending them would move no Channel digest, but they want a mean level above a chart's datum each, which no open source gave here. Held, as the brief has them: the lead's to blend once the levels are read (the Portuguese hydrographic office's tables).
- **Tofiño's bearings are true**, by the Punta Delgada and the Galera; **Norie's Fayal Road** (2h 20m, 4 1/2 feet) disagrees with Tofiño's survey (half past twelve, eight Spanish feet) and with the gauges, which put Horta within five degrees of Angra (Norie's 11h 45m): the epitome keeps Norie's figure, the master's error to make. TICON's two records of Ponta Delgada disagree by 36 degrees in M2 (the shorter BODC series); the longer UHSLC series agrees with its neighbours and is taken.
- **The directions' limits were one box**, and within it the open Channel's statement answered where no area did: widened to the islands it would have given the Channel's north-easterly stream to the whole ocean between. Built first as a second kind of water (`book_waters`, where only an area with a polygon answered); package 39d met the same fault from Portugal and mended it at the root (`book_limits` a list of boxes, the open Channel's statement of its own `bounds:`), and at the merge the islands' water became a box of that list and `book_waters` went: this package changes no code of the tide.
- **The engine's planner never beats to windward.** `shape a course` for a place to windward keeps her full and by on one tack ("lies too near the wind to be laid; she is kept full and by on the larboard tack") and never puts about for it: a road to windward is never fetched, and a book must have the wind free on every leg (both scenarios' weather is pinned so). A finding for the captain's and the officer's packages.
- **The condition `the distance run since noon` is none before the first noon**, where the reading says "before the first noon, the run since the departure" (docs/primer/10): a book's "under 25 miles" is never true on the first morning. The schooner's book uses daylight instead.
- **An anchor refused is not asked again.** A `when` order that lets go by a distance near a road on a steep bank is refused for the depth ("no anchoring ground here: 165 fathoms") and does not fire again while its condition stays true; the books ask every two minutes while she has way on (`every 2 minutes, if ... and the speed is over 1 knot`).
- **The depth warning speaks of the Channel**: "33 fathoms is deep water to anchor in: the roads lie in seventeen fathoms and less" at Funchal, whose road is thirty-six fathoms by the directions. The warning's figure wants to be the port's (a finding for the anchor's code).
- **Sea passages are no places.** A `place` is land the lookout raises and a fix may use: the passage between Madeira and the Desertas was hailed "four leagues off" and served as a mark in a fix. The islands' three passages are `bottom` notes (not raised, found by name). Channel-mid's "Race of Portland" is a `place` the same way (not this package's file).
- **Open sea is dear**: 131 of the Azores' 153 level-2 tiles hold no land and lie three miles and more from it, 260 KB each (the multibeam relief compresses badly; Madeira's are 107 KB): 40.5 MB, against the owner's "about 18". Writing only the tiles within ten miles of land would be 33 tiles and 10.4 MB, the corridor answering the rest at 30″, once the corridor reaches the islands (a recipe rule for the lead and the owner).
- **The lookout's estimate of a peak's distance is long**: the Peak of Pico hailed at "47 leagues" when it stood 113 miles (38 leagues) off, and at "20 leagues" at about 70 miles; Tofiño's own figure is "32 leagues" in clear weather. The estimate wants the object's height into it (a finding for the lookout's words); the fix by the bearing is unharmed.
- **Two blocks named a feature alike.** Package 39d's `bugio` (the castle of the Bugio at the Tagus's mouth) and this package's (the Bugio of the Desertas) met at the merge, which `--check`'s "ids unique across the manifest's regions" refused; the Desertas' is `bugio-deserta`. A block's ids want its region's word where the name is common (the Bugio, the Cabras, the Ilhéu).
- **The proxy reset one poll of GEBCO's queue**, and the build fell over; `_get_json` asks again (four times, ten to forty seconds apart).
- **Wikimedia's API refused the build network for its rate**; the encyclopaedia's pages themselves served. The Internet Archive's IIIF server serves any page of a scanned book cropped and scaled, which read Norie's columns the OCR lost.

## Milestone 6: the Biscay south and Galicia block (package 39c, 2026-10-10)

Package 39c (spec M6 §26, the blocks' item 3; the brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md`, "Packages 39c to 39f"; built as `docs/dev/ChartBlocks.md` says, which this package corrected where it proved wrong or wanting). The region `biscay-south` beside `biscay-north`, the Gironde to the Minho: its tiles, coast, index and features; five port files; the tide's gauges read and held, five stream areas, nine places of the epitome; a scenario. Built from the branch head beside 39d, 39e and 39f in their own worktrees. The condition: nothing of the Channel or of Biscay north moves, which the recorded passages prove by their digests ("The suite, as run").

### The sources, fetched

EMODnet's DTM 2024 for the region (`elevation` and `elevation_max`, 41.8 to 46.15 N, 9.4 to 0.75 W, 138.9 MB each, ten seconds each) and GEBCO_2025's area extract (41.7 to 46.25 N, 9.5 to 0.65 W, 11.8 MB, two seconds once the queue had cut it), retrieved 2026-10-10 through the proxy; their checksums in the manifest beside the earlier fetches. TICON's zip again (the same checksum) and SHOM's RAM as GeoJSON (233,639 bytes, SHA-256 a8d61280…6529). From the Internet Archive (public domain mark): Tofiño's *Derrotero* of 1789, the OCR of two copies (`A302201`, Sevilla's, the better; `bub_gb_04Yq4fsvB8gC`), and his *Atlas Marítimo de España* (`A062039040`), its ABBYY text for the sheets' titles and two sheets read at 1,600 pixels and in crops at full resolution through the IIIF server; Faden 1793's OCR again. The Lighthouse Directory's pages for Spain's north and Galicia and France's Aquitaine (its page for Charente-Maritime refused the connection). The French and Spanish encyclopaedias' API answered 429 to every request for a quarter of an hour and was let be. Everything fetched lies under `.cache/` in the worktree, read by the tool or by scripts kept outside it, with `-I`.

The shore's sweep for GEBCO's fill: 5,675 cells in 310 places (4,153 in 280 with the world's higher level before the merge), the largest Santoña's marshes (168 cells about 43.43 N, 3.48 W), the inner ria of Arosa, the marshes of Carnota and the lagoon of Louro, the banks of Arcachon's passes and the Adour's mouth: water EMODnet's survey does not reach, left as water (`unverified-checks.yaml`). `git diff --stat` over `data/charts/` after the build: `manifest.yaml` (the block's entry, its fetches, the chart's regions, the date and the build hash) and `unverified-checks.yaml`; every other change a new file of the block's. No tile, coast or index file another region or the corridor lists changed, and their manifest entries are the same entries.

### No patch, and why

Tofiño's plans of Ferrol (1789) and Santander (1788) were read at full resolution: their soundings are "brazas de á dos varas castellanas en baxa mar de aguas vivas", legible, and the plans georeference on the castles and points. Santander's would be the patch to make: the 1788 bay before the city held two to four brazas on a shifting sand where the modern grid has the port's dredged channel and reclaimed land. But the height of the low water of springs above the Spanish chart's datum at either port was not read from a table (Puertos del Estado's and the Instituto Hidrográfico's pages were not reached; TICON gives the constants, from which a figure could be computed but not read), and the how-to makes no patch without it; the port files say `datum: unverified`. A later package with the IHM's table makes both.

### The features, the ports, the tide

136 marks: the Gironde from Faden (12), Arcachon and the Basque coast of France from Faden and Tofiño (10), Guipúzcoa (13), Biscay from Ogoño to Santoña (15), Santander (10), Asturias (14), Galicia's north coast (10), Ferrol (8), Corunna (7), the Costa da Morte (15), Muros to Pontevedra (9), Vigo and Bayona (13). Positions first placed from the modern chart and the Derrotero's bearings, then checked against the block's tiles by channel-west.yaml's rule with a scratch script outside the repository: 35 moved to the grid, each move in `fix`; the rocks the grid does not resolve left where the pilot puts them and said so. Four isles stand forty metres high where EMODnet's grid has water (Santa Clara at St Sebastian, Mouro and Santa Marina at Santander, the Estelas): each is a `rock` of its height and an `extent_m` of its size, so that a ship cannot sail through it (the test runs the grounding over Santa Clara). Five port files: Royan (French; the roads of Verdon and Royan; Faden's), Santander, Ferrol, Corunna and Vigo (Spanish; the Derrotero's), each spot repeating its feature's position. Gijón, the Asturian ports, Passages, St Sebastian, Bilbao and Santoña are marks and roads and no port file: the brief's list is met by the five, and a port file each is a later package's. TICON holds, in the block, Le Verdon, Arcachon, Boucau-Bayonne, Socoa, Bilbao, Santander, Gijón, Ferrol, A Coruña, Vilagarcía and Vigo; no Bordeaux within it (the river's, M8's).

### The scenario, sailed once (`data/scenarios/biscay-south.yaml`, seed 7)

The cutter, American, at anchor in the road under the Isles of Bayona at 06:00 on 12 June 1805 (twelve fathoms and a half); under way at 06:33 by the north passage before a south-westerly of fourteen knots; Vigo's pilots' launch hails at 06:26 and, unanswered, bears away at 06:46; the courses shaped off Salvora (08:45), the Meixido (12:00), Finisterre (13:11), Toriñana (14:53) and Villano (16:22), then for Sisarga (20:41) as the wind veers west; noon by observation 42° 42′ N, the account 1.2 miles from the truth; the land about Sisarga at three miles at 21:32 (the account 0.4 miles out); the Tower of Hercules's light raised at 23:24 bearing E by S at some ten miles (the account 2.5 miles east of the truth, the light's first bearing setting it right); north of the Tower at 01:06, in for the harbour at 02:15, **at anchor in the harbour of Corunna in six fathoms and a half at 02:42 on the 13th**, brought up at 02:59. Thirty hours: 858 lines, digest `d0c62a036cfded4b` on the tree merged with 39d (`0031038406342073` before the merge, every event above at the same minute: the tiles' land now raised by the block's 2.5 m and not the world's level); on the tree merged with 39e too, 881 lines, digest `657fc88fa6a0a59e`: 39e's lookout estimates the distances shorter ("four leagues" for five off Salvora), so the cross bearings and the account differ by a cable or so, and she came to in the harbour of Corunna at 02:49 in seven fathoms, brought up at 03:06, the passage otherwise the same (the build machine; `tools/day_log.py data/scenarios/biscay-south.yaml --hours 30 --reckoning`); the account at the end within a cable. Two first runs, kept for the book: a waypoint off the Meixido at a mile she passed by a mile and a quarter and stood on into the Atlantic (the offshore marks now at two miles); and the course from Sisarga straight for the harbour's mouth crossed the Tower's peninsula, where she took the ground at five knots at 02:15 and lay there the forenoon (a waypoint north of the Tower now), and with the first run's southerly she could not fetch into Corunna's mouth at all (the Derrotero's winds for it are of the first and fourth quadrants: the pinned wind now veers to west-north-west). Not a gate's, not pinned.

### Found on the way (package 39c)

- **Two blocks share a row of tiles.** The bound at 42.0 N lies inside the row from 41.84 to 42.27 N, so this block and the Portuguese one (39d, built at the same time) each wrote and listed the row's tiles that hold water (two: `2/150624_-32064` and `2/150624_-33600`); the seam rule cannot see a branch not yet merged. Portugal was merged first, so at this package's merge the two are Portugal's: its files taken, this block rebuilt with `--skip-fetch`, and the check says "12 kept" (said in ChartBlocks.md).
- **A wide block's box is mostly not sea.** Of the 200 level-2 tiles over 42 to 46 N and 9.3 to 0.8 W, 59 hold no water at the datum and 57 none shallower than a thousand metres; the dry ones cost 7 MB and put the region over the tests' budget. This package's recipe key left them to the corridor, and 39d's `skip_dry_tiles`, merged first, does the same: at the merge the block took 39d's key and dropped its own (the corridor answers there as beyond the tiles; the distance field of the coastal tiles is computed over the whole block). The deep ones, 2.4 MB, were kept: a later rule could leave tiles deeper than some depth to the corridor too.
- **A feature id the Portuguese block gave too.** Both blocks named an `estelas` (the Estelas off Monteferro here, the Estelas by the Berlenga there); the merged check failed on it, and this block's is now `estelas-of-bayona`.
- **EMODnet's grid has no isles of a few hundred metres.** Santa Clara, Mouro, Santa Marina and the Estelas, forty metres high, are water in the tiles (its sixteenth of a minute interpolates the soundings over them; GEBCO's fill never comes into play, EMODnet having a value). Given as solid rocks; a land patch is a later package's.
- **A block's index is written by its build alone.** Built early to fetch, the block had an empty index; the features written after were found by id and not by the lookout or the bottom's notes until the block was rebuilt with `--skip-fetch` (the first tests failed so). Said in ChartBlocks.md.
- **TICON's UHSLC series at Vigo has every phase an hour early** (29.4° on M2, its speed in an hour): a clock off by an hour in that record (1943 to 1990); the IEO's and Puertos del Estado's series agree with each other, and the longest is taken.
- **The world's tide over the block is the Channel's blend, and late**: M2 at Santander 155° against the gauge's 95°, at Vigo 111° against 77°; the same finding as 39b's, larger here. The engine wants a gauge's own water (the lead's decision); the Iberian blocks will widen it.
- **The directions' limits were one box**, and widened to 42 N and 9.33 W it took in the bay west of 7 W from 45.9 to 47.5 N, where no area answered and the open Channel's statement would have; this package's open-bay polygon reached there, and it proposed a list of boxes. Package 39d made the list, merged first: at the merge this block's box is appended and the open bay's polygon is the block's bounds again.
- **The encyclopaedias refused every request** (429) for a quarter of an hour; the Lighthouse Directory gave the lights' years instead. It also gives Fuerte de la Galea at Bilbao "station established 1782"; the Derrotero of 1789 names the castle of la Galea and no light there, so no light is given (unverified, for the lead).
- **Tofiño's Derrotero and Atlas are the Iberian blocks' sources**: the Derrotero's volume covers Portugal to Cape Trafalgar and the Azores too, and the Atlas has plans of Cadiz's bay and of Angra (for 39d and 39e; said in ChartBlocks.md).
- **`tests/test_chart.py`'s corridor test named no shore off Finisterre** (42.9 N, 9.4 W, the corridor's): the block's mark of the town under the cape now names it, and the test says so.
- **The scratchpad is shared** between the four blocks' sessions on this machine (a script of this package's was overwritten by 39e's of the same name); this package's scratch files moved to their own folder.
- **The port test asks every port's road for its depth**; Faden gives none for the road of Royan, and the block's test says so rather than a judged depth.

## Milestone 6: the Strait block (package 39f, 2026-10-10)

Package 39f (spec M6 §26, the blocks' item 6; the brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md`; built as `docs/dev/ChartBlocks.md` says, which this package corrected where it proved wrong). The region `strait`, Cape Roche and Cape Trafalgar to Gibraltar, Ceuta and Cape Spartel; its tiles, coast, index, features and one period patch; five port files and Morocco in the nations table; the Strait's gauges read and held; seven stream areas, three of them with the constant current the stream model gained for the inset; four places of the epitome; a scenario. Built beside 39c, 39d and 39e from the same branch head; `portugal` (39d) is the one neighbour, at 36.4 N.

### The sources, fetched

EMODnet's DTM 2024 for the region (`elevation` and `elevation_max` over 35.35 to 36.80 N, 6.85 to 4.55 W, 12.3 MB each, CC BY 4.0) and GEBCO_2025's area extract (35.25 to 36.90 N, 6.95 to 4.45 W, 1.4 MB, public domain), retrieved 2026-10-10 through the proxy in seconds; their checksums in the manifest. TICON's zip (CC BY 4.0), the same file as 39a's and 39b's. Tofiño's two Derroteros (1787, 1789), Purdy 1826, Moore 1799 and Lempriere 1800 as the Internet Archive's OCR texts (public domain), Purdy's pp. 6 to 8 as page images; Tofiño's plan of the bay at full resolution through the Rumsey IIIF server (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0; the crops cached, none committed); the Spanish and English encyclopaedias' pages as wikitext, one at a time (the API answered 429). Everything fetched lies under the worktree's `.cache/` (`charts/`, `strait-texts/`, `strait-sheets/`, `strait-ticon/`, `strait-wiki/`), read by the tool and by scripts kept outside it, the Python that read it run with `-I`.

### The patch: the water about the Green Island from Tofiño 1786

Tofiño's plan of the bay, north up, its soundings in brazas of two Castilian varas, its bottoms lettered (A sand, L mud, P stone, CP shell and stone, ...); no datum stated. The modern port of Algeciras is built out over the Green Island and its chains of rock: EMODnet has no value there and GEBCO's fill, raised four metres, stands as a flat of one to six metres above the datum east of the natural slope's foot at 5.441 W, where the town's front was. Georeferenced by a similarity on three control points (the Torre del Carnero on the encyclopaedia's position of the Carnero light, 120 m; Europa's tip on the tiles', 76 m; the mouth of the Rio de la Miel on the slope's foot, 108 m), the sheet turned 1.6° at 1.53 m a pixel; checked against the tower of San García (250 m from the feature) and the Devil's Tower (683 m: its modern site uncertain, and the east side of the Rock the plan's least-sounded edge). A first fit on two points put the town's front 200 m inland, which the third point mended. Three patches: 4 brazas east of the isle (the sheet's 3 P to 9), 2 brazas before the town and inside the isle (2 to 4 close in, the 1s on the rock chains left to the isle), the isle as land ten metres high. The build printed no disagreement beyond three metres (the patch's water is the fill's land). Before: a quay of fill from 36.12 to 36.135 N; after: the isle in water, a sounding of 3.6 m between it and the town (`test_chart.py`).

### The features, the ports, the nations

88 features: Cape Roche, Conil and the Laja (5), Cape Trafalgar with its tower, its light of 1860, the Aceytera, the sand bank and the rocky flat (7), the coast to Tarifa (Barbate, Zahara, the Camarinal, Cape Plata, Bolonia, Paloma, Valdevaqueros, the Peña: 12) and its dangers (the Cabezos, Arroyo del Puerco, the rock of Valdevaqueros), Tarifa (7), the coast to Carnero (6), the Pearl, the bay of Gibraltar and Algeciras (21), the African shore from Spartel to Tetuan (25). Positions placed from the modern chart, the encyclopaedia's coordinates and Tofiño's bearings, then checked against the tiles by the file's rule (a scratch script outside the repository): 39 moved, each in `fix`; the Cabezos, the Pearl, the Aceytera and the rock of Valdevaqueros (the grid's 18 to 52 m about them) kept where Tofiño's theodolites put them; the Laja of Conil a 5.3 m shoal of the grid exactly at his bearings. **Tofiño's Camarinal is the modern Cabo de Gracia** (the Faro de Camarinal stands there) and his Cape Plata the modern Punta Camarinal: his bearings (Paloma S 72 E 4 1/2 miles from Cape Plata) fit only so. Five port files: Gibraltar British (the anchorage off the Old Mole, the King's ships under the New Mole, the yard; Reiner the pilot, Purdy's); Algeciras, Tarifa and Ceuta Spanish, hostile to a King's ship and open to a neutral; Tangier Moorish (the bay's road, buoyed cables for the weed-roots and coral; cattle for the garrison). **Morocco** in the nations table: at peace with every nation in June 1805 (no war entry), its flag the plain red, no letters of marque, `relations:` toward each nation with its source or judgement (Britain: Purdy's Jackson, the Emperor prefers the English and allows Gibraltar its cattle; Spain: peace after Muley Yazid's war of 1790 and 1791 on Ceuta, Lempriere 1800, the treaty of 1799 from memory; the United States: peace since Preble at Tangier in September 1803, the encyclopaedia; France, Portugal, Denmark, the Batavian Republic: peace, judgement).

### The stream model's constant current (the inset)

`streams.yaml`'s areas take `current: {toward_deg, kn}` and their `book:` `current: {set, kn}`. The world (`Tide.at`) adds the current to the area's tidal stream as a velocity (`StreamArea.current_toward_deg`, `current_kn`; nought for every area naming none, so no other stream moved: the test proves every other area has none). The master (`Directions`, `BookStream.current_point`, `current_rad`, `current_kn`) works it into his traverse as one more course (`_tide_between`), into his doubt with the tide's rate, into his words ("allowing the flood, two knots and a half to the W, and the current two knots to the E"), and into a shaped course as the tide and the current together (`tide_allowed`'s knots and set are the resultant where a current is given; the course's words say "the flood and the current"). A first version allowed the current in the account but not in the shaped course: the frigate steered for the tide alone and was carried past Cape Carnero to the back of the Rock (the fifth run). **The directions beyond their box**: `book_limits` was one box from the Channel to Biscay north, and widened to the Strait it would have made the open Channel's north-east stream the master's statement off Portugal; before the merge `Directions.area_at` let a polygon's statement hold within its polygon beyond the box, and at the merge with 39d (whose `book_limits` is a list of boxes) the Strait's water is its own box instead (below).

### The scenario, sailed once (`data/scenarios/strait.yaml`, seed 7)

The frigate under way five miles south-west of Cape Trafalgar at 05:00 on 12 June 1805, a westerly of thirteen knots, plain sail; the courses shaped for the Cabezos' offing (re-shaped hourly), past them at 08:03, a mile south of the Isle of Tarifa at 09:30, along the shore off the Acebuche at 10:49, off Cape Carnero east of the Pearl at 11:20 (sail shortened), up the middle of the bay and for Gibraltar road at 12:12; the lead from four miles off; **at anchor at 12:52 in six fathoms off the Old Mole**, brought up at 13:06 in six and a half with thirty-one fathoms of cable; the Gibraltar pilots' boat hailed her at 13:01, unanswered, and bore away. The noon by observation 36° 06′ N, the account kept, 0.2 miles from the truth; at the end the account on the truth. The log three and three-quarters to six and a half knots; the master's tide by his directions throughout ("in the middle of the Strait: allowing the ebb, two knots and a half to the E, and the current two knots to the E"). Ten hours: 747 lines, digest `1057826c4a32ec09` (`tools/day_log.py data/scenarios/strait.yaml --hours 10 --reckoning`, the build machine). Not a gate's, not pinned. The first runs, kept here for the book: on a single course shaped at the start the shore's flood set her north and she went on the Cabezos at 08:32, stove (the Strait's dangers bite as Tofiño said); with the waypoint south of Tarifa in the middle's current she was carried east of the Rock (Purdy's warning, p. 9); with the stream over-allowed for the bay she went on the sand under the town; with the current not allowed in the shaped course (above) past Carnero; with two hourly orders contending she wore back toward the Acebuche and grounded in Getares Bay; anchored at 0.4 miles from the road she let go in 43 fathoms (the bay falls off steeply, Tofiño p. 18: sound before you let go), so the book anchors by the lead.

**Where she starts, and "against the inset".** Cadiz bay is `portugal`'s, not in this block's manifest: she starts in the block's own water off Trafalgar, as the brief allows. The brief's "against the inset" does not fit a passage from Cadiz to Gibraltar: the inset sets east, with her; it is the passage out of the Mediterranean that has it against her.

### Found on the way (package 39f)

- **The world's tide over the Strait is Le Conquet's.** No gauge of the eleven lies within 400 miles, so the world takes the nearest alone (734 miles off): an M2 of 2.0 m where Gibraltar's is 0.31, high water two hours late, a mean level 3.98 m above a datum Gibraltar's is under a metre above; the stream's springs and neaps follow Le Conquet's range. The Strait's four gauges are read and held as the brief says; **unlike Biscay's they would move no recorded passage if blended** (every Channel and Biscay north position is more than 600 miles from them: `test_the_straits_gauges_are_read_and_held_and_would_move_no_channel_position`), and would give the Strait its own tide. What they would move: the world's tide within 400 miles of them (Portugal's south and Lisbon, 39d's water) and the far place off Lisbon (`test_tide.py`'s Le Conquet off Lisbon). The lead's decision, best taken with 39d's gauges. When they are blended this region wants a rebuild (its fill raised by 3.98 m where 0.6 would do: land three metres high, which floods nothing).
- **The seam with a neighbour built at the same time.** Two of this block's level-2 tiles (the row from 36.29 N, 6.77 to 5.92 W) meet `portugal`'s bounds and hold Cadiz bay: both branches build them, and the seam rule cannot keep them one region's until one is merged. Merge `portugal` first; this block is then rebuilt against the merged manifest (`--region strait --skip-fetch`) and those two drop out of its list (ChartBlocks.md, "the seam").
- **The directions' box**: widened to the Strait it would have made the Channel's stream the master's off Portugal. Before the merge this package let a polygon's statement hold beyond the box; 39d, merged first, made `book_limits` a list of boxes, and at the merge the Strait's is one more box (the block's bounds) and the polygon rule was dropped for it: one mechanism.
- **The weather's boxes do not cover the corridor whole**: 35 to 36 N east of 9 W (the Strait's southern half, the Moroccan Atlantic coast) lies in no box and takes the nearest, Portugal's (`Climatology.box_at`); ChartBlocks.md said the four covered it. Nothing changed; a Strait box (the Levanter and the Poniente) wants a printed table.
- **No light in the Strait in 1805.** Every light is later; the friars' lamp in the tower of Our Lady of Europe had no shrine to keep it after 1704, when the shrine ceased to be used and was taken for military use (the lamp's end JUDGEMENT from that). Tarifa's light: the encyclopaedia guesses the second half of the eighteenth century, Tofiño (1787) describes the isle's tower and no light, the first record is a plan of 1826; taken as 1826, unverified.
- **Tofiño's Camarinal is the modern Cabo de Gracia** (above), and the brief's "Pearl Rock" lies a mile and three-quarters off Carnero where EMODnet has fifty metres: the grid resolves none of the Strait's pinnacles (the Cabezos, the Pearl, the Aceytera), which stand as dangers with their heads.
- **EMODnet's `elevation_max` is empty over parts of the Strait** where `elevation` has values (the Laja of Conil): the features' check against the shoalest sounding has nothing there.
- **The ports' test holds every port to ten goods and a topmast** (`test_ports.py`), which ChartBlocks.md did not say; Tangier and Ceuta have them, judgement.
- **An apostrophe in a standing order's name** (`"the course for the Cabezos' offing"`) is refused by the dialect with a message about the condition, not the name; renamed.
- **The scratchpad directory is shared** between this machine's packages: a log written to `build1.log` there was overwritten by another package's build at the same moment. This package's scratch files live in their own folder.
- **Biscay north's held gauge Port-Tudy** gives its longitude as 1.2206 W, where TICON's file has 3.4459 W (Groix): a slip of 39b's, read by nothing while held; the lead's to correct (it is Biscay north's line, not this package's).

## Package 45: the fixes from gate m6a's first runs (2026-10-11)

The owner's notes of the first runs (`docs/playtests/2026-10-11-gate-m6a-owner-runs/`), one
package in two parts; the brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md`. Part B was cut short by
the owner's weekly limit: what was built is below with its measure, what was not is said.

### Part A: the pictures, the chart whole, the charted places, the courses by way of marks

- **The pictures that reach the model** (`tests/test_pictures.py`: Playwright on the
  pre-installed Chromium, the API door against `tests/messages_api.py` and the MCP bridge,
  the PNG decoded with Pillow and judged not blank by its spread and its dark fraction). Found
  before the fix: the ship's view was blank in truth, two faults together: the offscreen
  svg's own hiding style (`display: none` on the root) was serialised into the picture, and
  the stylesheet keyed its fills on the page's `#ship-view` id, so every fill computed to
  black on the copy; the chart picture was the page's own canvas, whatever span and size the
  player had. After: both drawn on fixed offscreen canvases with their own backgrounds (the
  chart 1200 by 900, the ship 960 by 720), the chart centred on the account at the span asked
  (harbour, coast, passage, whole, the browser's own stops), not blank on the first turn nor
  after a shelving; a shelved picture's stub says it was shown and put back.
- **The chart whole in play**: `region:` means the chart that holds it (`chart_holding`,
  `atlantic-east` for every region of the line); the browser's block carries every region (1.7
  MB), the map culls and decimates; measured in the browser test's Chromium: the whole chart
  drawn in about 20 ms on screen, 10 to 20 ms as a picture, the harbour span 3 ms. The pins
  that moved for it (tests that assumed one region) say `chart="channel-west"` instead.
- **Every charted place** (spec M6 §26, as written there): answered by reading and one sail,
  the schooner from Falmouth round Ushant to Corunna's road by the player's courses
  (`data/scenarios/falmouth-to-corunna.yaml`, four days); nothing between Falmouth and Funchal
  is unmerged; the ports outside the Channel carry no tracks and are approached by the outer
  road; the tide is one gauge beyond 45 N and the weather PROVISIONAL from Biscay south.
- **Courses by way of marks** (`via`): `shape a course for Lisbon via Ushant and Finisterre`
  and an intent's `via`; the frigate sails Falmouth to Finisterre on the whole chart in
  `tests/test_via.py` (slow). Found on the way: the straight line Ushant to Lisbon crosses
  Galicia, so the seaward side of a mark is read from the sea room about it at a league and at
  three; `Corunna` is a road and not a town on the chart (`place_of`). The owner's note 11
  of gate m6a-2 (the way turning too early at marks near the coast, cutting the corner toward
  the land), looked at once: the berth laid five miles off a land mark was "reached" by
  account two miles short of it, as an open-sea mark is, and the next course shaped from
  there; a berth (the way's `hand` names the side it is left on) is now reached within half
  a mile or passed abeam (`WAY_BERTH_REACHED_NM`). The sea-room reading that lays the berth
  and the two-mile reach of a water mark are as they were; whether that was the whole of
  what the owner saw is for his next run.

## Package 45c: package 45's tail and the fixes from gate m6a-2's runs (2026-10-16)

The brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md` (Package 45c); the owner's notes of gate m6a-2
in `docs/playtests/2026-10-13-gate-m6a-2-owner-runs/README.md`. What each item built is in
spec M6 §4, §11, §13, §14 and §23 (as built, package 45c). Measured on the build machine
(four cores) with package 43's own suites running beside mine for most of the session (a
load of five to six): no pin depends on the load; the pace tests were run alone at the end.

### The naval cruise: the finding

The brief's reading (one of package 45's three helm changes moved the cruise) did not hold.
Each undone on the package-45 tree (A, the helmsman's mark under the period's trim only; B,
full and by capped at seven points; C, the watch bracing up for the helm), the cruise ran
to 34 hours: B and C each gave the unmodified run to the digest (the cutter within hail at
91022, three wears, 1531 lines, `67ca692be24fe39e`); A met the cutter at 90936 and wore four
times; none brought back the story. Bisected over package 45's own commits instead (the
trees at `e249084`, `52ded5f`, `2a49071` and `41e6287`, the cruise run whole on each): the
first three meet the cutter at 85437, read the letter at 85497 and speak the brig at 93493
with six wears in 34 hours (`417e1dc220b442a2`); `41e6287` gives package 45's figures. The
first line to differ is the Plymouth pilot's fix at 7980 (08:13 on the 12th, the account
brought to the truth); the true track is the same to the tick until 14:00 (28800), when
the course the book shapes for the station from that truer account is a degree off the old
(SW by S, 209 degrees, against SSW, 208), and the tracks part from there by more each hour.
So nothing was wrong with the helm: the frigate reached her station on another track, the
admiral's cutter came up with her an hour and a half later (07:17 on the 13th), and the
Palinure, which the scenario puts on the sea at seven "five leagues on the frigate's bow"
where the frigate had been, was put astern of a frigate still chasing the cutter (a
stranger until her colours were made out). The chase rule then made it worse: `give chase`
kept the chase in hand (the cutter, her letter read, British) for two hours with the
Palinure in sight (item 2, below).

The mend, both halves: the chase rule (item 2), and the Palinure re-placed by the
scenario's author where his words put her, five leagues on the frigate's bow, at 10:30 on
the 13th as she stands for the station's south-west end (`data/scenarios/naval-cruise.yaml`;
48 30.6 N 5 30.3 W). With the chase rule alone and the brig at seven, the frigate turned for
the brig astern, the cutter caught her at 08:36, the brig crossed and ran NE by N, and a
stern chase of twelve hours spoke her at 20:33 with four wears in the two days. With the
brig re-placed: the cutter within hail at 07:17 (91024) and the letter read (91084), the
brig sighted on the starboard bow at 10:45 (103500) and chased at once, made out, spoken
under no colours at 11:55 (107738), lost astern at 15:23 (120180), twelve wears in the two
days, never aground; 2287 lines, `493d888d874aa358`. The two strict xfails are lifted; the
save the cruise's fixture writes moves from 08:00 to noon on the 13th, so that the brig is
spoken before it (the pins below).

### The chase (item 2)

The fault, from the station-and-stranger trial at one sample a second: at the second
bearing the chase's lead took the chaser's own way across the line of sight from her
course at that moment, so that a chase begun as she turned read her whole turn as the
brig's drift and led her across the brig's bows at the forty-five-degree cap, and the brig,
crossing at her own speed two miles off, crossed ahead of the cap and drew aft for good.
The rule as mended (`orders/navigation.py` `_chase_course`; `data/captains/kings-ship.yaml`
says it): the stranger before any sail spoken; the chaser's own way across from her own
run through the water between the two bearings (`Lookout.own_run`, pegged at each look);
the lead to seventy degrees; a bearing drawn more than forty-five degrees since the last is
a chase that has crossed, and the course is laid for her bearing again. The trial
(`trial-station-stranger`, twenty hours): before, chasing at 06:33, the stranger never
within hail and the chase given up at 10:51; after, chasing at 06:33 with the course led
seventy degrees, within hail at 06:53 (10423), on the station at 06:54 and wearing every
second hour after; minutes a sail aback, sampled each minute, 10 (4 together) before and 8
(2) after; 889 lines, `3c2aba8b08fd1f63`.

### Sail after the gale, by steps (item 3)

a sample each minute (the minutes any square sail stood aback, and the longest run of them):

|---|---|---|---|---|

### The two judgements (item 16)

- **A course shaped across the land by a model station** (note 12): left as the warning it
  is. The master's line already says it in so many words ("the line crosses the land about
  ..."), and refusing it would take from the captain a course he means to alter before the
  land, which the period's masters shaped and the rules-based captain's planner lays every
  leg past; the owner calls it an observation, and its cure is the brief's and the
  library's (`shape a course for <n> miles south of <place>`, `via`), which the models did
  not read. Not changed.
- **The officer's doubt of the tide off Torbay** (note 1), one look: the world's tide at
  Torbay is the blend of Devonport (27 miles) and Weymouth (41) by the inverse square:
  establishment 5h 32m local, spring range 3.96 metres, mean level 3.09 metres above the
  datum. The period's table says six hours (Norie and Moore alike); the Admiralty's modern
  figures for Torquay, from memory and unverified, are near Devonport's high water and a
  half hour after, a spring range near 4.2 metres. So the height is near enough, the high
  water perhaps half an hour early. The stream is the larger fault: Torbay lies in the
  `mid-channel` stream area, so the world runs the open Channel's stream inside the bay,
  1.3 knots at springs, where the bay has next to none. That is what an officer at anchor
  in Torbay would doubt. Not changed here (a stream area of its own for Torbay, with the
  passages that pass it re-pinned, is a data change for the lead).

## Package 43: other ships with captains (2026-10-16)

Package 43 (spec M6 §4, §19, §20 and §23 as built; the brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md`;
decisions 40, 43 and 45; the owner's word of 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-15: the rules-based
captain at far detail first, the director's voice and the observed world left to M7b). The
measurement first, then the brain on the far body, the crewed promotion and its guard, a
model captain of another ship kept across the switch, the director's seat hook and the live
world order. Built beside package 45c from the same head (`35d31d6`); no file of 45c's
list is touched but `captains.py` (the judgement moved into a mixin, the stimuli added at
the end of the table), `orders.py` (the `ship:` order's tails and two channels appended),
`stations.py` untouched.

### The measurement, first (item 1)

`scratchpad/p43/measure.py` (kept out of the repository): the station-stranger trial's
frigate under her captain (truth 51's form: a thousand ticks to settle, the best of three
thousands), then the same with the merchant passage's dozen ships at far detail, then with
one, three, six and twelve **fully crewed ships** beside her, each a World of her own from
one of the four files at a place in the Channel with an intent and a rules-based captain
(`make_world` + `set plain sail`), all ticked in lockstep in one process. The build machine
has four cores; package 45c's suites ran beside this package all day and no quiet window
held for the length of a run (the third run began at a load of 0.5 and 45c's four workers
were up again before its first figure), so the load is given with each figure. The
measurement is one thread and the box has four cores: the three runs agree within a tenth
at loads from 1.6 to 5, so the table is the best of the three and stands for the quiet
machine within that tenth.

| The frigate with the dozen ships at far detail | 399 (3.3) | 372 (2.5) | 411 (3.0) | **411** | 686 (3.6) |
| The frigate with one crewed ship | 190 (4.1) | 260 (2.7) | 226 (3.8) | **260** | 354 (4.2) |

The session's container was restarted twice during the package and came back the second
time on a faster machine: the last column is the merged tree there, and the tree before the
merge measured the same on it (705 alone, 718 with the dozen at far detail, 234 with three
crewed, against 667, 764 and 212 for the merged tree in the same minutes), so the gain is
the machine's and not package 45c's. The constants were chosen on the slower machine's
figures (the first five columns), which is the one the floors of truth 51 were set on.

**What costs.** A crewed ship costs what the player's frigate costs, a little under three
milliseconds a tick on this machine under load: the profile of three crewed ships (cProfile,
600 ticks) puts 82 per cent of the tick in `physics/integrate.step` → `sails.compute_sail_
forces` (four substeps a tick, 7,200 calls in 1,800 ticks), the sheets' readings and the
strain next, and the standing runtime, the captain's judgement, the reckoning and the lookout
under three per cent together. The far-detail body costs a tenth of a tick a minute (package
36's figure stands: the dozen at far detail cost a sixth of the tick, the lookout's pairwise
work, not the bodies). So twelve crewed ships at once are thirty-four ticks a second, half
the sixty times the owner plays at, as the spec's reading said, and a world with every ship in a region crewed
wants the vectorised hot loop of the risk table (the sails' forces for many hulls in one
pass), which is a later milestone's and is sized by this table.

**The strategy chosen: the horizon's range with hysteresis and a cap** (`crews.py`).

| Constant | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CREWED_NM` | 4 miles | promoted where the tops make out her rig and read her sails' state (`ships.RIG_MADE_OUT_NM`): nearer than that the far body's words ("under plain sail") are read against a hull the viewer could draw; farther, a far body and a crewed one are the same sail to the lookout |
| `CREWED_DEMOTE_NM` | 6 miles | hysteresis of two miles, half an hour's sailing apart at four knots, so that a ship at the edge does not flap between bodies (M5 §25's two and three miles for the near-detail switch, widened) |
| `CREWED_CAP` | 3 | the frigate with three crewed ships runs 100 to 114 ticks a second on the build machine, near twice the sixty times the owner plays at; four would be near eighty (six run at 56), too close to the sixty for a machine with other work on it |
| `CREWED_FLOOR_TICKS_S` | 60 | the pace truth 88 with the cap full: sixty times, the owner's play speed, on the build machine (a little over half the figure measured, as truth 51's floor is half its measurement; the truth's own frigate lies hove to and its three brigs are under sail, and it passed under a load of four) |
| `DEALING_S` | a glass | a ship within hail, or chasing, investigating or evading the player, within the last glass is in dealings with him: promoted before a nearer ship that is not, and not demoted beyond six miles while the dealing lasts |
| the cap's order | the nearest first; a dealing ship within the range takes the farthest idle crewed ship's place | spec M6 §19 |
| not promoted, and demoted | at anchor, in port, running for shelter, in distress | the port's business (the pilot's boat, the market) is the player's ship's machinery and the far brain's wait; a crewed stranger in pilot water would send a cutter that steers for the player (judgement; 43b's ground) |

How the brain is made: `captains.Judgement` is the one judgement (the trend, the chase's
log, every stimulus) shared by `Captain` (the near body) and `brains.FarCaptain` (the far
body); the far captain's perception is `brains.perceive_vessel`, from the vessel's own truth
(her position, the wind at her by `Vessel._wind_at`, the chart's coast and the lee sector's
rays from where she is, the ships in sight from her masthead by the horizon formula over the
parent's vessels and the player's ship as a vessel of her file's description,
`Vessels.player_shadow`); the states resolve into plans (`brains.resolve_state`). The far
brain lives in `brains.py` and not `captains.py` because it reads the truth, and
`tests/test_captains.py` proves that `captains.py` does not: the grep proof holds unchanged.
Nothing of a far captain's mind is a line of the player's log; `FarCaptain.history` is the
record, and runs on through the near body while she is promoted (`crews.mirror`).

**The far-detail guard** (item 3): a captain's plan is the planner's (the ports' tracks and
the common tracks, a headland given an offing), and a plan that still crosses the land is
refused at her making (`ships.land_crossing`: the first and last cable of a leg not tried).
The brief read the guard as a refusal of every ship's leg across the coast at load. Measured
first (`scratchpad/p43/guard_probe.py`): six of the recorded passages' dozen scripted ships
have a goal's straight leg across a cape (the Palinure from the Raz to Brest, the Hirondelle
from the Isle of Saints to Camaret road, the Bom Jesus for the Start, the Indefatigable out
of Cawsand Bay, the Swift for Plymouth; the cruise's Diamond's square off the Raz), which no
passage ever sees (none comes within sight of those legs' land), and refusing them would
have moved every pin of every passage and trial for a sight nobody takes. So a goal's leg
across the land is a warning on the vessel, printed with the scenario's lines when the game
starts (`scenarios.guard_lines`, the author's view, never a line of the log), and the
refusal is a captain's. 43b, whose generated ships take the planner's route, closes it.

### The trials with a brain in the stranger: what the two captains made of each other

The stranger of the two stranger trials was given a brain (`intent:` at the end of her world
order; the cruiser's doctrine by her description, a brig-sloop of France). Read from the
brain's history and the player's log (`scratchpad/p43/smoke_brain.py`, `debug_trial.py`),
twenty hours at seed 7:

- **The station and a stranger** (the frigate on her station off Ushant; the Palinure put on
  the sea three leagues north at 06:00, bound south across the station). The Palinure sees the
  frigate at once, six miles off, a sail, and closes her to make her out (investigating);
  within four miles at 06:30 she is promoted, her captain the same brain in a crewed body.
  At 06:36 both make the other out: the frigate's glass makes her a brig-sloop of war under no
  colours and the frigate chases; the Palinure makes the frigate out for what she is, an
  enemy of a bigger class within two leagues, and hauls off (`overmatched`: evading). The
  frigate chases her until 09:11 (09:16 on the merged tree, under 45c's chase rule) without
  gaining a mile (the brig seven knots on a reach to the frigate's five and a half) and
  gives the chase up as stale, the station shaped for; the
  Palinure, lost to sight by 09:45, goes back on passage and is demoted at 10:30, twelve miles
  off. Standing south on her passage she raises the frigate again at noon, closes her again
  to make her out (she cannot know it is the same sail until she has), is promoted at 12:30,
  makes her out and hauls off again; the frigate, who has done with her (`given_up`), keeps
  her station. Before this package the stranger sailed her straight leg across the station
  and was chased across the frigate's bows and lost at 10:51. States: the frigate keeping
  station 300, investigating 7200, chasing 9360, keeping station 18660, (investigating and
  chasing again at 18720 and 18780 in the run before the given-up rule, and twice more); the
  Palinure on passage and investigating 7200, evading 9360, on passage 20700, investigating
  27060, evading 30000.
- **The merchant and a privateer** (the schooner bound for Falmouth; the Renard put on the sea
  within two miles at 05:00). The Renard is promoted at her making (two miles off) and her
  captain makes the schooner out at once: a smaller class, an enemy once her colours show,
  and he chases (investigating at 05:00, chasing at 05:05); the schooner evades from 05:01,
  hauling off every ten minutes under all sail. The two are matched on a reach (the brig six
  and a half knots to the schooner's seven), and after three hours without a mile gained the
  Renard gives up the chase at 08:05 and goes on her passage, demoted at 08:35 as the dealing
  lapses and she passes six miles; the schooner hauls off until the brig is out of sight
  right astern at 08:50 (twenty-three hauls; the Renard is a sail three leagues off again at
  09:38 on her passage north, never made out, lost at 13:29), and is forty miles to the
  south-westward of where the old run was by then. She raises the Lizard at 14:07, takes the
  pilot's cutter off Falmouth at 18:40, beats from 17:17 (the wind foul for the entrance by
  the evening), anchors in the outer road at 20:43 (the bower let go at 60514) and is in port
  from the road at 20:49 (13:54 before this package, when the Renard sailed on her leg and
  the schooner evaded forty minutes and lost her). Before the given-up rule the brig chased
  her for eight hours, taking the chase up again a minute after each stale giving-up, and the
  schooner evaded all the forenoon and again in the afternoon. States: the schooner on
  passage 300, evading 3660, on passage 17400, beating 47820, at anchor 60180, in port 60540;
  the Renard investigating 3600, chasing 3900, on passage 14700. On the merged tree (45c's
  pilot's conn from his station and its beating rule) the same meeting ends with the brig
  out of sight at 08:58, the schooner beating by turns and anchoring in Carrick Road on the
  evening ebb at 19:23, in port at 19:24 and aground at 21:48 (the pins and the grounding,
  below).

The promotion's part in the trials: both strangers are crewed while within four miles or in
dealings with the player (the chase), so the meetings are sailed at full detail, each brig's
sails under the physics, and the far body takes her up again when the dealing is over and
she is beyond six miles; the brain's history runs through both bodies.

### A model captain of another ship, across the switch (item 4)

`--station captain --ship <name or id>` at the MCP bridge, the local runner and the API door
(`remote.Desk` with `ship`, the seat keyed by the ship and the station; `GameClient(ship=)`
sends it with every call). `crews.station_world` finds her and makes her World in the shape
her distance gives; `CrewedWorld.shape` is "full" or "far", `far_tick` the far shape's tick
(the clock, the body mirrored into the ship and the account, the wind at her, the lookout
once a minute, the bells, the stations sampled), `submit_far` the far shape's orders
(`FAR_SHAPE_WORDS`), `shape_words` the sample's notice. The switch's lines in her log are
urgent, so that a station standing by is woken to be told its shape. The fake proves it
(`tests/test_crews.py`, truth 89): seated on the brig three miles off, his order in her log
and not the player's, the player's lookout seeing one sail, the pace rule counting her
station, demoted with the station kept, a course shaped working the far body and an order
of the deck refused in words, promoted again beneath the same station with no reseat.
**Left undone**: the player at `--seat captain --ship` (the drivers' centre, chart and prompt
follow the player's ship; a world watched from another ship is the observed world of M7b),
and a save of a game with a station on another ship replays the player's ship's stations
only (the checkpoint carries the other ship's whole).

### The seat hook and the live world order (item 5)

`world: <order>` at the console's prompt and in the browser's order box (`ui/console.py`
`live_world_order`; the server's driver the same): the owner's order to the world,
journaled with the source "the owner", saved and replayed; the bare order stays the
grammar's refusal (truth 71). `seat: <model> as captain of <ship> for <n> samples|hours`
and `unseat: <ship>[, <note>]` (`world/orders.py` `_seat`, `_unseat`): refused in words
without a consent record holding the model's yes with the drill passed (the records'
directory the drivers were started with, `world.consent_records_dir`), without an owner's
grant naming the model (the scenario's `director:` block), with the seats at once or in the
voyage spent, for a ship not on the sea or without a captain of her own; held on the World
otherwise, her World made, the budget counted once a minute (`crews.enforce_budgets`) and
the station stood down by the director when it is spent. The hook assumes no player's ship
where that costs nothing (a bare World refuses in words). **The consent brief's revision
(42b) must say**: that a model may be seated as the captain of another ship beside the
player's, with her own company, log and account, its orders the ship's and its station kept
across the far-detail switch; and that a model may be seated by a model, the director's
seat, only under the owner's grant and budget and never by a model's own word.

## Package 44: the regatta, the trims by a point of sail, the parity tests (2026-10-16)

Package 44 (spec M6 §21 and §22 as built; the brief in `docs/dev/M6-WorkPackages.md`; the
owner's note 25 of gate m6a-2, the trims by a point of sail judged at the regatta; truths
90 and 91). Built beside package 43b from the same head (`a7e5693`). No model was run: the
regatta's model doors are proved against the fake model server and the fake Messages
server, and the first table is the rules-based captain's and the scripted captain's.

### The regatta as built (item 1)

`tools/regatta.py` and the three courses of `data/regatta/` (spec §21 as built;
`docs/agents/Harness.md` section 18). Where the brief's way was taken and where another:

- **A course is a scenario file and a course file over it**, not a scenario of its own: the
  course names the recorded passage's (or the voyage's) scenario and leaves out what is the
  scenario's own captain (its book and its first orders), so that every agent starts from
  the same sea, the same weather and the same ship, and the course can never drift from
  the passage it is run on. The recorded passages' files are run, never pinned here.
- **Every agent is given plain sail at the gun.** On the first try the rules-based captain
  on the 5b passage's start, no sail set and under way off Ushant, made no sail for
  twenty-six hours (his doctrine makes sail when he weighs, and she was not at anchor): a
  flying start under plain sail is the course's, the same for every agent. The captain's
  gap is the lead's (below).
- **The model doors run in the regatta's own process** as clients of a game it hosts (the
  browser game's app served to the door as the doors' own tests serve it), rather than the
  owner starting a game and a door in two terminals: one command runs a course, the clock
  held at the gun until the station is taken and in lockstep after, run as fast as the
  machine allows between turns. The door's own flags pass through after `--`.
- **Consent on record only**: `remote.Desk.on_record_only` refuses before the gun, in words,
  a model with no record, a brief changed since its record, a re-ask or a drill due; no
  consent conversation is begun at the regatta. Every record now in `docs/agents/consent/`
  predates the brief of 42a, so every model the owner has is refused by the regatta until
  he has put the question again in a game (decision 42's re-asks, his).
- **No model is named in the repository by a run**: the log and the row put a model's
  identity, wherever the log has it, as its kind of agent ("a local model through its
  runner") before anything is written; the run's save, which holds the identity as the
  consent and the replay need it, goes to `saves/regatta/` (git ignores it).
- **The human replay** is a save of the course begun from `--start-save` (the course at the
  gun), replayed by its journal and judged as it sails (`core.replay.replay` takes an
  `on_tick` that stops it at the line); a save of another start is refused in words.
- **The judge** rounds a mark when her true track crosses the line laid from it to seaward,
  and finishes her within the radius once every mark is rounded. The finish of the second
  course is three miles about the road of Bertheaume: the pilot's track into Brest (the
  port file's `from_sea` and `in`) passes 2.3 to 2.8 miles from the road's own point, and
  the rules-based captain bound for Brest went by it inside that and into the Goulet; a
  mile would have scored him as never arriving.
- **The scripted captain** (`fake.captain_on_the_course`): the course's orders at the gun
  and at each glass, standing by until the next. Its first scripts, a course shaped for the
  port by name and trimmed each glass, put the frigate on the Manacles and the schooner on
  Keller off Ushant: `shape a course` lays the line from the account and warns of the land
  it crosses, and a script does not read the warning. The scripts in the course files now
  prick their courses clear (by way of 50 00 N 4 57 W off the Manacles, west of Ushant,
  west of Finisterre) and take a bearing and a fix each glass; even so it takes the ground
  on both Channel courses by account and is carried off on the third (below). A model
  reads the master's words; the fake is the floor of what a station without judgement makes of a course.

What the table says. **The rules-based captain** is the regatta's standard on the two

São Lourenço and Machico, on the thirteenth day; his course for Funchal road from there
was shaped across the land ("the line crosses the land about Machico"), he took the ground
on the ebb, and each flood that floated her he shaped the same course and took it again,
nine times, 9.7 miles from the road at the limit. That is the planner's open item (the
owner's reading of 2026-10-15 that `shape a course` warns of the land and does nothing
about it): a fault for the lead, and the regatta's first finding. **The scripted captain**
took the ground on both Channel courses, by account and through the master's warnings,
which a script does not read, and on the voyage to Madeira was carried far to the westward
on a leg of four hundred miles (finding 5 below) and ended 906 miles short; on the first
course trimmed for the point of sail it came in first, 21 minutes ahead of the rules-based
captain. The purse moved once, by the Brest pilot's fee (£4, paid as he left her clear of
the road). Fatigue stayed fresh throughout: no course has the crew at the braces for long
(nobody reefs; the weather is pinned fair).

### The trims by a point of sail: kept (item 2)

`trim for close hauled`, `trim for the wind abeam`, `trim for the wind large` (or `for the
wind on the quarter`) and `trim to run` (`orders/verbs.py`, `POINT_TRUE_WIND_DEG`,
`point_wind`, `course_steered_for`; the phrases in `data/vocabulary.yaml`). The brief's way
was the period's trim by level close-hauled and the yards squared by fixed steps for the
rest (the brace table's 30° and 15° from square); by the model's own rule the steps would
be wrong for its sails, whose best angle of attack is reckoned from the apparent wind (`trim sails`
puts the yards some 60° from square with the wind abeam, the apparent wind being well
forward of the beam at the frigate's speed, where the table's "up" is 30°). So the trims
were built as `trim sails` for a named wind: each point a true wind's angle off the bow
(close-hauled six points, Fincham's and what the period's trim gives the frigate full and
by; abeam eight; large twelve; a run sixteen), the apparent wind reckoned from the true
wind she has and her way now, the yards and the sheets trimmed for it by `trim sails`'s
rule (close-hauled the period's trim by level whatever her way), on the side the wind will
be on when she is on the course the helm, or a tack or a wear ordered for a course, is
steering for. The side was the first version's fault: from a run hauled up to the wind
abeam (the helm wearing her round for it) the yards were braced for the tack she happened
to be on dead before it, and she was aback for half an hour (2.0 knots against 6.7 with no
trim at all); taken from the course steered for, 7.5 knots.

**Where they gain**: when the helm and the trim are ordered in one breath, as a model's
station orders them before it stands by for a glass. `trim sails` then trims for the wind
she had. The measure (`scratchpad/p44/turns.py`, kept out of the repository): fifteen knots
from the north, the ship under plain sail trimmed on her first heading, the helm ordered to
a new one with the trim; the miles made good along the new course in the half hour after.

| S to E | 1.46 | **3.33** | 2.32 | 1.46 |
| E to ENE | 2.66 | **3.37** | 2.87 | 2.46 |
| SE to SSE | 2.85 | 2.85 | 2.86 | 2.85 |

**Against the helm's mark** (`scratchpad/p44/mark.py`): from the wind abeam, hauling her
wind full and by with the trim in the same breath, made good to windward in the hour after.
The frigate: `keep her full` with `trim sails` 1.54 miles at 4.8 knots, with `trim for close
hauled` the same (the apparent wind abeam is on a wind for her yards already: both trims
brace up by level); steered six points off by compass, 1.57 at 5.1 either way. The
schooner: full and by with `trim sails` 0.88 at 7.2 knots, with `trim for close hauled`
0.35 at 2.6 and four minutes aback; by compass six points off with `trim for close hauled`
**2.24** at 6.8, with `trim sails` 1.67.

**On the first course** (the table above): the scripted captain trimmed for the point came
in at 14 h 25 m; with `trim sails` on the cadence it took the ground a mile and a tenth
from the line at 14 h 38 m; with no trim after the gun it was aground at
21 h 55 m 2.7 miles short. The wind is free from the gun to the line on that course (SW
backing W on a northerly course), so the helm's mark never applies there, and the courses'
different landfalls are partly the account's; the turns are the measure, the course the
check.

**The judgement: kept.** They gain or hold in eleven of the twelve turns, and in the
three that matter most (bearing away, hauling up from the quarter, and coming to from a
run) by a fifth to the whole of the distance; with the helm full and by on a square-rigger
they are `trim sails`. **The case against**: the schooner hauling her wind under her
fore-and-aft sails, from the quarter to close-hauled or full and by, does worse with her
sheets hauled flat before she has come to: she gripes past her course and is aback (the
gripe the 37p notes name). The primer's chapter 4 says so: for a schooner hauling her wind,
the helm first and the trim when she is round. **The sails-lifting line** (45c's, the yards
not trimmed for the course) now names `trim for close hauled` (`physics/integrate.py`;
`tests/test_lying_to.py`); the primer's chapters 4 and 5 say the orders and the line.

### The parity tests (item 3)

`tests/test_parity.py` (spec §22 as built). The enumeration, every entry checked:

| Surface | Entries | The captain's station | Differences |
|---|---|---|---|
| The readings registry | 78 rows | every row asked at the console's prompt and by `submit_order` at the same tick gives the same words; every row a sample carries is in the `readings` tool in the registry's words | by design: the parametric rows are asked by name (the sails' states the tool's `sails`), the absent row refused alike, the pace the driver's and never carried |
| The vocabulary's verbs | 302 (the readings' verbs among them) | every verb passes the captain's domain | by design: the driver's five (`hold`, `go`, `time`, `read the standing orders from`, `muster`), refused to the ship by the grammar from both |
| The console's commands and the browser's order line | 21 | each has its road (`state`, the stores' queries, `standing orders`, the stations' sentences, `log` as `read_log`, `help` as `library`) | by design: the clock, the save and the load, reading a book from the disk, `quit`, a world order |
| The browser's snapshot | 17 blocks | each names the readings and tools that show it | none |
| The station's tools | 16 | each names the player's counterpart | by design: the journal, the stand-by, the shelf, the hand-over, the stand-down, the opt-out |

**The gap found and closed**: `muster`. The console printed the watch bill and the browser
answered it (45c), and a station asking for it was told "'muster' is a console command, not
an order to the ship". `submit_order('muster')` at any station now answers from
`api.queries.muster_lines`, as the console prints it, logged by neither. **The same orders,
the same log** (truth 91): the fake captain gives ten orders one a sample on the 5b
passage's world with the console on the same game; the console gives them at the same
ticks to a second game; the logs are the same line for line, but for whose each order's
line says it was and for the stores' answers (`the sail room`, `the booms`), which the
console prints for the one who asked and a station gets as its tool's result and a log
line: listed by design (the console's and the browser's own query of the stores never
reaches the World; a station's is a query through the order line as the player's
`show the sail room` is).

### Found on the way, for the lead

1. **The planner's course across the land** (the regatta's first finding): the rules-based

   put the scripted captain on the Manacles and on Keller. The owner's reading of
   2026-10-15 stands as the planner's open item.
2. **The rules-based captain on passage makes no sail when he starts under way with none

   poles). The courses give plain sail at the gun; the doctrine's want is the lead's.
3. **`via` a land mark and the next leg**: a berth off Ushant "passed abeam" five miles
   north of it, the leg to the next mark laid from where she is crosses Keller (the master
   says so). The scripts prick their courses; whether the way should lay its next leg
   round the mark it has just passed is the orders review's.
4. **The schooner's gripe hauling her wind** with her sheets flat aft before she has come
   to (above).
5. **A water mark of the way passed abeam far off** (the scripted captain on the voyage to
   Madeira): the leg from west of Ushant to 42 55 N 9 50 W, 386 miles, steered with "the
   ebb, a knot and a half to the SW" allowed off Ushant, ended with the mark "passed
   abeam" when the next leg, for Funchal, was 1,562 miles: she had been carried far to the
   westward of the mark and of Finisterre (the judge never had her round it), and the
   voyage ended 906 miles short. Whether a tidal allowance laid near the land holds on a
   leg of four hundred miles, and whether a mark passed abeam at any distance is struck,

### The two hulls (item 1; `tools/gen_ships.py`, `data/ships/lugger.yaml`, `smack.yaml`)
