## Package 56: fishing, and the glass on a near ship (2026-10-18)

Spec M7b §21a to §21c; the brief's six items. Built in the worktree off `91711a0` (packages
50, 52, 53, 54 and 57 merged). New: `freesail/world/fishing.py`, `freesail/orders/fishing.py`
and `glass.py`, `data/fishing/fish.yaml`, `channel-west.yaml` and `biscay-north.yaml`, the
gear's eight evolutions (`data/evolutions/shoot_trawl.yaml`, `haul_trawl`, `shoot_nets`,
`haul_nets`, `shoot_seine`, `haul_seine`, `set_lines`, `haul_lines`), `tests/test_fishing.py`
and the primer's chapter 21.

### The sources found, and what each gave

- **Holdsworth 1874**, *Deep-Sea Fishing and Fishing Boats*, the OCR the repository holds
  (`docs/references/holdsworth/`), read for this package beyond the pages 43b cited: the
  pilchard drift fishery "begins on the Cornish coast in July, and is carried on till
  December", few pilchards "farther at sea than 10 or 12 miles ... south rather than west of
  the Land's End" (p. 130); the mackerel "towards the end of February ... into June", "May,
  June, and July are the months in which most of these fish are caught by drift-nets in the
  English Channel" (pp. 127 to 128); drift-net fishing "carried on only at night", the fish
  striking "just after sunset and before sunrise" (pp. 98 to 99), the nets shot at sunset
  before the wind over the quarter (pp. 106 to 107), a herring fleet a mile and a quarter
  and the Cornish pilchard nets "about the size of those for herrings, but with a smaller
  mesh" (pp. 110 to 111); the trawl towed with the tide "for five or six hours, under easy
  sail" at "from half a knot to a knot and a half faster than the tide" (pp. 70 to 71,
  77 to 78), the warp hove in "seldom occupying less than three-quarters of an hour, and in
  bad weather sometimes taking two or three hours" (p. 79), the deep-sea trawls of 36 to 50
  ft (p. 47), the Plymouth and Brixham grounds "only a few miles from the land" (p. 44),
  four-fifths of a trawler's take "of the inferior kinds" (p. 24); the sean worked from
  rowing boats "very near the land or in the smooth water of sheltered bays", the single
  "stop-sean or tuck-sean" where the fish are "tucked" into the boat at once (pp. 157 to
  159); the St Ives sean fishery "from September to November" (p. 188), "2500" pilchards to
  the hogshead pressed to "four hundredweight gross", "5500 hogsheads" once from one shoal,
  the curing in "alternate layers of coarse salt and fish" (pp. 193 to 194), the south
  coast's seans fewer and smaller (pp. 194 to 195); the longlines and the cod alive in the
  well (pp. 137 to 141).
- **The Encyclopaedia Britannica, 4th edition (1810), CLUPEA** (after Pennant and Borlase;
  read 2026-10-17 at jimclifford.ca's transcription): the pilchards "off the Cornish coasts
  about the middle of July, disappearing the beginning of winter"; 7,000 hogsheads enclosed
  in St Ives bay in 1767; the hogshead exported at "£1. 13s. 3d." one year with another,
  1747 to 1756. (It gives 35,000 fish to the hogshead, against Holdsworth's 2,500 of the
  pressed cask; the Britannica's figure reads as a misprint and is not used.)
- **The Breton sardine**: no period page reached. The Musée de la Pêche at Concarneau's
  text (read 2026-10-17 at artsandculture.google.com) gives the undecked boats, the half of
  France's catch in the eighteenth century, and the fish "first fished using roe (salted
  cod eggs) with different types of nets"; Duhamel du Monceau's *Traité des pêches* and
  Robin's *Pêcheurs bretons sous l'Ancien régime* are the sources to read next. The
  sardine's season (June to October) and its by-day drift are judgement on that.
- **Not reached**: a period figure for any boat's catch by the hour or the night, for the
  Brixham trawl's haul, or for the price of green fish at the quay. Every yield and price
  below is judgement, with its reasoning in the data's own comments.

### The yields (tons of fish an hour of the gear fishing, one vessel's gear)

The reasoning (judgement throughout, anchored on Holdsworth's hogshead: a ton is five
pressed hogsheads, some 12,500 pilchards):

| Gear and fish | Yield | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| tuck-sean, pilchards (Gerrans Bay July to December, St Ives Bay September to November, by day) | 3.0 t/h, an hour a shot | a small sean's fifteen hogsheads of a shoal, against the great seans' thousands (p. 194; EB 1810's 7,000) |
| tuck-sean, mackerel (Gerrans Bay June to August) | 1.0 t/h | the mackerel near the land after mid-July (p. 128), fewer |
| drift nets, pilchards (Mount's Bay, by night) | 0.2 t/h, half again at the twilight | six to eight hogsheads in a night's eight dark hours |
| drift nets, mackerel and herring | 0.12 to 0.15 t/h | a little less than the pilchards |
| drift nets, Breton sardine (Iroise, Glenan, Belle Isle, by day) | 0.12 to 0.15 t/h | as the pilchard's drift |
| trawl, soles and turbot / plaice and hake | 0.02 to 0.025 / 0.05 to 0.06 t/h, six hours a shot | half a ton a haul of five or six hours, a fifth of it prime (p. 24) |
| lines, cod / ling and conger | 0.03 to 0.05 / 0.03 to 0.04 t/h, six hours a shot | a few hundredweight a tide |
| a ground the tables do not name | trawl 0.04, lines 0.03 | the default |

The wind takes the work: full to six tenths of the gear's most (the trawl 30 knots, the
nets 27, the lines 24, the seine 16), half at the most, nothing beyond; the trawl takes
nothing outside one to four knots through the water.

### The spoilage's hours

Nothing was iced in 1805. A fish that lives in the well (cod ten days, soles and turbot
four) is alive there; one that does not (pilchards a day, herring 20 hours, sardines 18,
mackerel 16, plaice, hake, ling and conger 36) keeps cool in its running water. In the hold
unsalted: pilchards 12 hours in summer (May to September) and 30 in winter, mackerel 8 and
24, herring 12 and 30, sardines 10 and 24, the flat fish 30 and 72, plaice and hake 20 and
48, cod, ling and conger 24 and 72; salted (a third of the fish's weight of salt from the
hold), beyond any voyage. The well holds a ton of fish to three cubic metres (the
Culloden's 9.1, three tons; Chapman's sumpar's 150 lispund, about 1.3 tons, the check).
Judgement throughout, on Holdsworth's "Round-fish at all times suffer more than flat-fish"
(p. 85) and the fat herrings that "must be eaten without delay" (p. 34).

### The fish quays

Each fish a price a ton fresh and salted (`fish.yaml`), each quay a factor on it (Falmouth
1.0, Plymouth, Torbay and Weymouth 1.1, St Mary's 0.9, Brest 1.2, ...). Pilchards fresh £6
the ton: the cured hogshead's £1 13s 3d of 1747 to 1756 (EB 1810) is about £8 the ton
cured at mid-century and Falmouth's market file has £14 in 1805 from memory; the green fish
to the cellars at under half the cured, the salt, the pressing and the women's work being
the curer's. The others in proportion (soles and turbot £25, cod £12, mackerel £9, sardines
£8, herring £6, plaice and hake £7, ling and conger £8). The ports' cargo markets
(`data/ports/*.yaml`) are untouched: they deal in the cured hogshead, and a new good there
would move every price list a recorded passage brings off.

### The gear and its evolutions' times

The shots by the watch (three hands, four for the nets), the hauls all hands: the trawl
shot in a quarter of an hour and hauled in three quarters (Holdsworth p. 79); the nets half
an hour and two hours; the seine twenty minutes and an hour; the lines an hour (3,600
fathoms at four knots) and three. **The trawl's drag** on her way, 1,200 N for a metre a
second squared (`fishing.TRAWL_DRAG`), measured on the smack at seed 7 under plain sail on a
beam reach: 5.3 knots without it, 2.2 with it in fourteen knots of wind, 6.7 and 3.1 in
twenty (2,400 N gave 1.5 to 2.1, too slow for Holdsworth's "a knot and a half faster than
the tide").

### The doctrine, and the fishermen promoted

The fisherman's doctrine needed nothing in its tables: the gear's rule is the fishing
module's, one for both bodies (`far_work` at far detail, `captain_work` at full, from
`Captain._station`). What it needed in code: a fishing trip's mark is the ground itself
(`Planner.legs_for` and `FarCaptain._station_mark`), not a station a league off, which put
a bay's station on the land (the Gerrans ground's station fell at 4° 59' W, ashore); and a
ground pricked at a position is an intent's place (`captains._place_id`).

### The glass's tiers

Two miles for a look (her state, her tack, tacking or wearing, running, sail set or
shortening), eight cables for her work (reefing, sail made or taken in, a boat, the anchor
coming up, the hands at the gear), four cables for the evolution's own words; each bounded
by the visibility, a tier less at the twilight; by night within a mile only a light, and a
fishing vessel at her gear the only ship that shows one. Judgement on the period's day glass
and the brief's reading. The lookout says it unasked when a sail comes within the tiers and
when her state, her work or her light changes, never for her point of sailing alone (a far
ship's moves with every course shaped) nor for the steps of one piece of work (the first
run said "tacking" three times in three minutes as the tack's steps went by), nor for a
boat under oars.

### Found on the way

- The `station_off` rule for a station's mark rounds the room to a league and then prefers
  the west: in a bay every bearing has under a league of room, and the west won, on the
  land. Fishing no longer uses it; a cruiser's station in a bay would meet it still.
- A smack hove to has the heave-to's four hands tending her sheets (`heave_to.yaml`
  `keep_hands`), most of a smack's watch: the crewed fisherman's haul of the seine waited
  for all hands and went slowly (an hour and a half for the hour's work). The hauls are
  all hands for that reason; the heave-to's hands are the frigate's figure, and a small
  vessel's would want its own.
- The far fisherman's way home to Falmouth from Gerrans Bay is the port's track from the
  sea, out round to 49° 52' N before turning in: twenty miles for seven. Hauled at 11:00 she
  was in at 22:14, her hold's pilchards with three quarters of an hour to spare before they
  turned (truth 106 compares the catch at the haul and the tons landed, sold or spoiled, so
  that a slower passage home does not fail it).

### Pins

**The fishing moved no pin.** The business is off in every recorded passage and no
recorded ship carries gear (a ship with none has no fishery: `world.fishery` is None, and
no line, reading or draw of hers changes); lifting the never-crewed rule changes nothing
where no fisherman is drawn. **The glass and the sightings' words moved ten tests' pins,
against the brief's "no pin moves"**: every recorded passage or trial in which a sail
comes within two miles by day (the pilot cutters of Falmouth and Plymouth, the strangers
of the trials) now has the lookout's glass lines, and every made-out line her bearing and
course. Item 5 asks for exactly these lines, so they cannot be had without moving a digest;
the head rule's re-measure was taken, the old figure beside each, and the move proved to be

## Package 59: the harbour (2026-10-18)

The launcher, the scenario maker and the settings (spec M7b §21d to §21f; the owner, 2026-10-17;
`docs/dev/M7b-WorkPackages.md`, "Package 59"). Built on `06015d3` beside package 62. No
simulation figure was tuned: the package is a page, a writer of files and a settings file.

### What was built, and the reading taken

- **`py -m freesail`** (`freesail/__main__.py`) takes the server's whole command line, the
  settings giving its defaults, and serves the harbour at `/harbour` in the same server.

- **The doors** are the modules' own command lines run by the server (`sys.executable -m
  freesail.agents.api` or `.local`); their stdin is a line in the pane, which is where the

  `--store-key` (package 42), and the harbour says only whether the store holds one. A form

## Package 62: the director's hand (2026-10-18)

Spec M7b §3 ("The director's hand", the owner's proposal of 2026-10-18); decisions 46 and 50;
the brief's four items, the third (the director seated in a ship) not built. Built in the
worktree off `06015d3`, beside 59. No new module: the hand is `crews.hand` (with
`ask_crewed`, `captain_held_by`, `her_log`, `HAND_HOLD_S`), the `ship` channel's `order` and
`crewed` tails in `orders.py` (`_hand`, `_hand_reach`, `_doubt_hand`, `is_hand`), the hold on
both captains (`Captain.over_his_head`, `FarCaptain.over_his_head`, `take_up_again`), the far
body's short story (`Vessel.story`), and the brief's `examples`.

### What the far shape could and could not carry

The far shape's eleven orders (`crews.FAR_SHAPE_WORDS`) carry what a captain's hand on a far
ship mostly wants: `heave to` (the plan's `lie_to`, the far body drifting a knot to leeward,
her sail "lying to"), `fill away`, `shape a course for <place>`, `steer <course>`, `give
chase` and `haul off` (the nearest stranger her masthead sees), `make sail` and `shorten
sail` as a state, `come to an anchor`, `weigh`, `keep the station`. `far_order` reads only
her vessel and the parent's sea, so a far body with no World of her own is given it through
a light stand-in (`_FarBody`), and no World is made for one order (a far-shaped World costs a
ship from her file and a tick each second for as long as it is kept). What it could not
carry, answered as the game's honest "no way as said" naming the eleven:

- a sail by name (`set the fore royal`, `set the fore topgallant`), a boat lowered, a gun:
  the far body has no sails, boats or guns, only a sail state;
- a reading or a sentence of her deck (`the glass`, `you have the deck`): no order, and the
  truth reads her for the director;
- `give chase` with no sail in her horizon: the far shape's own refusal ("No sail in sight
  to chase"), which the fake director entered again with its reason and which was then
  logged as attempted, not performed (the honest road for an order performed and refused);
- a world order inside the hand (`ship "X": order port falmouth: ...`): no order of hers.

Within the promotion's range the answer adds `ship "X": crewed`: the ship made a crewed one
now when the cap has room and her state allows (not at anchor, in port, running for shelter
or in distress), refused in words beyond the range or with the cap full; the cap and its
order (dealings first, then the nearest) are untouched, and a ship crewed so is demoted by
the same switch as any other. It counts as an act of the day's budget (an act is a world
order performed); judgement, for the lead to overrule if a promotion should be free.

### How her captain takes up his plan after an order over his head

The lead's reading, kept: he holds by it a glass (`HAND_HOLD_S`, 1,800 s) or until the
director's next order to her, which sets the glass again, then his intent again; `ship "X":
order carry on` (`captain: carry on`'s word, said of another ship) gives her back sooner.

- **The far captain** (`FarCaptain.over_his_head`): before the far order touches the body,
  her plan, her saved plan and her sail order are kept (the first order's only, so that a
  second order over his head does not keep the first one's plan as his); meanwhile he does
  not judge (his tick returns before the perception, as it does under a seated station);
  the glass out, the plan, the saved plan and the sail order are laid back, the lying-to
  time cleared, a plan laid afresh if there was none, and his judgement runs that same
  minute from where she is. Her story says it: "The captain takes up his plan again (bound
  for Falmouth)."
- **The crewed captain** (`Captain.over_his_head`): his state's book is struck as at the
  player's hand (so that no standing order of his fights the heave-to), his state cleared,
  his judgements held (`commands` false); the glass out, he commands again as at `captain:
  carry on`, his legs and business cleared, and his first state is entered afresh, which
  fills away from the heave-to (`_fill_away_first`) and shapes his leg: in the trial the
  brig-sloop filled away and stood for her station within the minute.
- **Across the promotion**: promoted inside the glass, the near captain holds by it for the
  rest of it, and a far body lying to by his order heaves to at full detail by his words,
  the first line of her new log; demoted inside it, the far body lies to if the near one was
  hove to or heaving to, and the far captain keeps the hold with the plan just laid. **A
  crewed World counts its ticks from her promotion** (her clock is her own): the hold is
  kept in her World's ticks and converted at each crossing (found on the way, by the test:
  the parent's tick had held the crewed captain the longer by her age).
- A far vessel with no captain of her own (a goal and no intent) obeys and holds by it
  until the next order; nothing of hers judges.

### The doubt and the reach

A captain's order is a plausible cause of itself; the doubt bites only where the order is
implausible for her (judgements): an anchor let go deeper than thirty fathoms by the chart
(a bower's cable of a hundred to a hundred and twenty fathoms wants a scope of three or
four, and the period's roads lie in five to twenty; the business's trader in the western
approaches lay in eighty), plain sail in a wind at her over thirty-four knots (force 8), and
a chase given by a master of the merchant's, the fisherman's or the packet's doctrine.
Entered again with a reason, each is done. The rule of reach refuses outright, logged
`director.refused` and costing no act, where a model or the player holds her captain's
station (`_stations_held` of her World, kept full or in the far shape) and for the player's
own ship, by her name or "the ship". A seat the director holds for a model under the owner's
grant and not yet taken is no holder: the hand works on her until the door comes.

### What the dispatches scenario showed

The dispatches scenario (`data/scenarios/dispatches-falmouth.yaml`, seed 7, the business on)
**did not load**: Fowey has no port file, and the World stopped at its making; its intent
("carry a cargo of tin from Falmouth to Plymouth") was no intent a captain knows, so the
rules captain never commanded. Both put right (the two ports of the passage; `trade tin from
Falmouth to Plymouth`), with a test that the World is made, the director bound and the
captain reading his intent. With Falmouth and Plymouth alone the business draws no trader
(no route with a price ratio of 1.3): five fishermen for the Eddystone ground and two French
brig-sloops on their stations off the Black Rocks and the Isle of Bas. So the far trader of
the truth is the business's at seed 7 in the free-play water off the Lizard
(`test_business.world_with("on")`: the Haabet, bound for Falmouth a hundred and thirty miles
off, among four traders on passage).

With a fake director on the dispatches brief:

- **On a far trader**: `ship "Haabet": order heave to` brought her to at once, her story "By
  the captain: heaving to.", her plan `lie_to`, her sail lying to; the glass out at 10:30 she
  took up her plan (seven knots under plain sail, bound for Falmouth) and her story said so;
  `set the fore topgallant` was answered with the far shape's eleven; `come to an anchor`
  doubted (eighty fathoms); `give chase` doubted (the merchant's doctrine); `ship "Speedwell"`
  (the player's schooner) refused as the player's own ship.
- **On a crewed cruiser**: the frigate of the brief's example put on the sea twenty-three
  miles south-east of the cutter (the first place tried, fourteen miles off, doubted inside
  the horizon; "the Dodman" unknown to the chart, whose name is "the Deadman", so the
  example says that) closed with the cutter by her own doctrine (investigating a stranger)
  and was promoted at 2.4 miles; `order give chase` and `order heave to` were her captain's,
  "By the captain: giving chase." and "By the captain: heaving to." in her log under his
  rules' actor, and she lay hove to at a knot and a half; the player's log carried only the
  lookout's lines of her. In the truth's water the brig-sloop on her station did the same,
  the player's lookout saying her glass ("heaving to", "hove to on the starboard tack").
- **Against a fake captain holding her**: the same order refused, "Hazard's captain
  (Captain Reynolds) is held by a model: his orders are his holder's own, and nobody gives
  one through him; write to him instead ('message: ...')", in the director's log as refused.

### Found on the way

- The dispatches scenario could not load (above); fixed.
- A crewed World's clock counts from her promotion (above); the hold is kept in her ticks.
- **"Write to him" is not yet a road**: `message:` reaches the player's ship alone (left at a
  port for the pilot, or by a cutter to "the ship"); a letter to a model captain of another

- The director's "Done:" answer runs its two sentences together ("... then sails by his

- A far vessel's story is read by no tool yet (12b's ships' logs, package 51); it is in the

### Pins

**No pin moves.** No digest or line count in `tests/` changed (`git diff 06015d3 -- tests`
touches no `_DIGEST` or `_LINES`), and every pinned passage of the slow tier passes against

## Package 53b: things, free lines and transactions (2026-10-19)

Spec M7b §17a (the owner's question of 2026-10-19 after the dispatches test and the lead's
answer, approved "as written"); decisions 46 and 50. Built in the worktree off `53bc80a`.
Two new modules, `freesail/world/things.py` (the thing, its where in words, its reach, made
from words) and `freesail/orders/free.py` (the free lines); the rest is the `aboard:`
channel's thing and transaction forms in `freesail/world/orders.py`, the ledgers on
`Purse` and `Hold`, the scenario's `things:`, the readings, the director's brief.

### What was built, and the readings taken

- **Item 1, a thing.** The lead's reading kept: a `Thing` in a small `things.py`, the
  `People` registry holding the things beside the people (`People.things`), the keeping
  read from the keeper wherever he is, so that the people's machinery moves a thing with no
  code of its own (the boat, the landing, `go to the counting house`, the pilot put off).
  The rule of reach for a held person's keeping is applied as the person's rule is, for
  every source of the order (the owner's too); the scenario's `things:` are its own word
  and are not checked by it.
- **Item 2, the free lines.** Nine verbs of the vocabulary's object `free`, the class named
  in a `free_lines` list with `hand`, `eat` and `drink`. Every station's, with the deck or
  without; the director's refused (no hands aboard). Reach for a thing and a person is the
  place's (`things.same_place`: his place aboard or §14's earshot, his place of the port).
  The past tense of the verb leads the line ("gave", "took", "threw") and the words after
  it are kept as said, case and all.
- **Item 3, transactions.** Four forms, each a line of the purse's or the hold's own
  ledger, a notable line of the play log in the purser's or the manifest's words, and the
  director's act; doubted by the table in spec §17a's as-built; a payment below nothing
  and a freight beyond the hold's room refused.
- **Item 4.** The dispatches scenario carries `things: [a sealed packet, in the captain's
  keeping, from the Custom House]`; its brief's examples gain `aboard: twenty guineas paid
  into the purse by Mr Veale`, `aboard: ten tons of wool freighted by Mr Veale at the quay
  for Falmouth` and a letter left on the cabin table. `data/people/` untouched.
- **Item 5.** Truths 7b-114 to 7b-116 (`tests/test_known_truths.py`) and the tests in
  `test_people.py`, `test_world_orders.py`, `test_business.py`, `test_director.py`.

**Taken another way** (spec §17a's as-built says each with its reason): a freight the hold
cannot stow is refused, not doubted (the hold's tons are the game's; no reason makes room);
"a sum beyond a port's means by the business's figures" is made of the figures the
business has, there being no figure of a port's money (below); the class `free` is the
verbs' object beside a `free_lines` list, since `hand` is the sail's word already and the
needs keep their object; `show`, `open` and `read` are "as said" whatever they name; a
hidden thing carries no flag, and every station reads what lies in a place until package 65
decides who perceives what.

### The figures (judgement)

- **A port's means** (`business.port_means_pounds`): the business's largest cargo
  (`cargo_tons`' upper figure, 120 tons) at the dearest price of the port's market as of
  the day, a whole trader's lading bought outright: Falmouth £36,000 on 12 June 1805 at seed
  7. A sum beyond it in one payment is doubted. A port whose market deals in nothing bounds
  no sum. The price is read without settling the market (a doubt changes nothing).
- **The guinea** at twenty-one shillings (£1 1s); a crown five shillings. The sum's words:
  "£30", "£6 10s", "£6 10s 6d", a number in figures or words before pounds, guineas,
  crowns, shillings or pence ("thirty pounds ten shillings").
- **A freight** comes off by the market's lighter job at the market's own times (an hour
  ashore, three minutes a ton, the pull to the ship), at no price; struck down at once where
  the freighter is aboard. Doubted with no lighter (she lies in no port and the freighter is
  not aboard).
- **Reach**: the payer, payee or freighter aboard, in the boat, or ashore at a port within
  `BOAT_REACH_NM` (six miles) of where she lies, 52's figure for a man brought off.

### What the dispatches scenario shows, the packet as a thing

A short scripted run at seed 7 on the scenario as committed (its mate and its copper ore
included; the player at the prompt as her master, the lead at the director's door as the
seat gives its orders; the script and its output in the lead's report, not in the
repository): the people's words open "Mr Bowen, master: in command, on the quarterdeck, a
sealed packet in his keeping. Mr Pearce, mate: on the quarterdeck. ...", the mate holding
the officer of the watch's station. The cutter anchors in Carrick Road and her rules captain
buys forty-two tons of copper ore by the boat, the whole of her hold. The director makes Mr
Veale, a clerk of the Custom House, ashore at Falmouth (at the counting house by his role),
and a letter for the port admiral on the cabin table (the places' reading: "In the cabin: a
letter for the port admiral on the table."); `aboard: a letter for Mr Veale, in the
captain's keeping` is refused by the rule of reach (the master held by the player at the
prompt); `aboard: ten tons of wool freighted by Mr Veale at the quay for Plymouth` is
answered "there is room in the hold for 0 tons and no more (42 tons bought are coming off)"
(with an empty hold, in the run before the intent was changed, it was freighted, written up
in the manifest with its cause, and came off by the lighter in two hours). From the
quarterdeck `give the packet to Mr Veale` is "as said; nothing of the ship's changed (Mr
Veale is ashore at Falmouth, at the counting house, out of your reach)"; landed by the boat
and at the counting house it moves, "By the captain, ashore at Falmouth, at the counting
house: gave the packet to Mr Veale; the sealed packet is in Mr Veale's keeping.", and the
people's words say it of him; `give the guineas to the boatman` is "as said"; `aboard:
twenty guineas paid into the purse by Mr Veale` is undoubted at his port, "Paid into the
purse by Mr Veale, twenty guineas (£21); the purse £43." in the play log and the purse's
ledger, the act in the director's log. The packet the test found handed over in words is now
handed over, and the guineas are in the purse.

### Found on the way

- **The dispatches had no company** (fixed, it blocked item 4): a scenario whose director
  brief binds the station in the World's making (`set_brief` in `World.__init__`) read the
  stations, which read the wardroom, which built the people **before the crew was mustered**;
  so they were built as a ship with no company's, the captain and the master alone, and
  stayed so. The dispatches' cutter had no mate, no boatswain, no boy, and her officer of the
  watch's station was bound to nobody: the test's finding 8 ("the officer of the watch is
  bound to nobody in this scenario") is this, not the scenario's people. `People.wardroom`
  now reads the file without building the people while the company is not yet mustered;
  built afterwards they are the muster's (Mr Pearce the mate holds the officer's station).
  An old save of a director's scenario replays with the company now, so its log is not the
  log it was; no pinned passage has a director.
- **A person's own needs were refused without the deck** (fixed with the free lines, which
  needed the same exemption): `eat`, `drink`, `sleep` and `how am I`, every station's by its
  domain since 54, were refused at a station with a domain that has not the deck ("The
  officer of the watch has not the deck ..."). `tools.own_order` exempts them and the free
  lines from the deck's check. `the glass on <ship>` (56) is refused so too and is left (it
  did not block; the lead's).
- **A free line at the prompt made the rules captain stand aside** (fixed): the player's
  hand on an intent scenario (40c) took any order of his but a station's sentence or a
  reading; a free line is no order of the ship's and is left out of it.
- **The rules captain sailed with his master ashore** (not fixed; the lead's): in the
  dispatches run the master's `go ashore` came in the minute the rules captain's `in port`
  book began to get her under way; he stood aside at the order, but the weighing evolution
  went on, and the cutter weighed and stood out with her master landed at the quay. The
  stand-aside should belay what his book had in hand, or the master who commands should not
  be landed while his ship is getting under way.
- **A freight's room** (mine, fixed): the first build checked the hold's room alone, and
  in the dispatches run the wool was freighted beside the master's whole lading of copper
  ore still in the boat, which then came off to lie on deck. The room is now what is left
  after the purchases in the boat and the lighter (`orders._tons_coming`). The market's own
  `buy` checks the hold's room alone too; a second bargain is refused while the boat is
  away, but a purchase in person at the market beside one in the boat is not (the lead's).
- **The coordinator's two additions to the dispatches scenario** (2026-10-19, made with
  the packet so that the file is edited once): a mate in its `people:` and the intent
  `trade copper ore from Falmouth to Plymouth` (Plymouth's market has no tin, the test's

- **The director's "Done:" answer** still runs its two sentences together ("... ashore at

## Package 66: the station's line and the stand-by (2026-10-19)

The harness after the dispatches test (`docs/playtests/2026-10-18-dispatches-director-test/`,
findings 2, 4, 9, 17, 18, 19, 22 and 25, and the captain's debrief); spec M7b §3, §5 and §14
"as built (package 66)"; truths 7b-117 to 7b-119. Built in a worktree off `6f272b9`, beside
53b. One new module, `freesail/world/hearing.py` (who heard a word, and where), kept apart
from the people's registry, which 53b is building on.

### Each item against its intent

1. **The line: built.** `readings.station_line` (one function, as the lead read it) from
   `People.effective_place` and the port's place ashore, the stations held (where the deck
   is kept) and the needs (`NeedsKeeper.showing`, `hours`); `Sample.you`, first in the
   sample's data; the director's `director_line` (the budget and every station whose open
   sample holds the clock). `how am I` answers with the same line, then its hours. *Taken
   another way, in part*: the "since" is the harness's (`Harness._place_since`), kept when the
   person's place changes, looked at after every order, once a minute and at each sample,
   and read back from the log's last line that moved him: a person has no "since" of his
   own, and adding one to `Person` would have been 53b's registry. The deck reads *yours*,
   *Mr Pearce's*, *the captain's*, *the captain's book's* or *nobody's*.
2. **A model's own order ends its stand-by: built** (`remote.Desk._own_act`): a reply out
   of turn that acts ends the stand-by at its own word (the log's line as 52 had it for
   words), opens the turn, and is taken in it; recorded as the model's own word (`door_act`
   "speak", by "its own order") and the reply after it, so that the replay is the same
   (truth 7b-118 replays to the same digest). *Wider than asked*: it holds for the wait for
   the turn as well as for a stand-by, as words of its own did already. The director's
   `truth` (and `read_journal`, which the meanwhile words named and the door did not run)
   join the meanwhile reads; the chart was one already as a picture tool.
3. **A wake carries a line: built** (`Harness._reaches`), in the stand-by's event and
   severity matches, the urgent line and (*wider than asked*) the cadence's notable lines,
   so that a word out of hearing neither wakes nor samples a station. The 15:44 case is
   truth 7b-118's second half.
4. **Who heard, and until when: built**, in the result and never the log's line (so that no
   recorded passage moves; the brief's alternative of keeping the pinned line's words and
   adding the hearers after them would still have moved the digest): `hearing.said_tail`
   for a `say` and a hail at `submit_order`, the console (printed under the order) and the
   browser (an unlogged line); `heard_words` in the director's `say as` result; the question
   to a person nobody holds says until when it waits.
5. **The hand's hold named: built** (`crews.hold_of`, `hold_event_came`): `for a watch`,
   `for two glasses`, `for an hour`, `until a sail within hail`, `a sail in sight`, `a
   landfall`, `hove to`, `at anchor`; the event read from her truth as her far captain
   perceives it, whichever body moves her; a day at most (judgement); across promotion and
   demotion. The dispatches brief's examples gain `give chase until a sail within hail`.
6. **`say as` by station or trade: built** (`orders.Voice`, `_by_station_or_voice`): the
   people first as before, then a station's person, then the lookout at the masthead (his
   hail heard on the open deck and aloft) and the hands, then the muster's trades. The rule
   of reach refuses a held lookout. The cutter has no carpenter in her muster and says so.
7. **Merchant words: built** (`agent.merchant_ship`, `MERCHANT_OFFICER`): the wardroom
   file's binding of the captain's station to a master is the test (a point world with no
   file keeps the lieutenant, as every recorded passage of it did).
8. **Truths and records: built**: truths 7b-117 to 7b-119; spec §3, §5 and §14 as built; the
   Harness's §19 and a §21a; the primer's chapter 20. *Taken another way*: chapter 6 does not
   tell the stand-by (it is the watch and the log); a model's stand-by is told in chapter 19
   (the wardroom), so the line, the stand-by's end, the wake, who heard and the mate went
   there, in a section of their own.

### What moved

### Decisions for the lead and the owner

- The hold until an event is bounded at a day; a forgotten order otherwise keeps her for
  ever. Judgement.
- Who heard names every named person in earshot (the stations held first, four at most and
  the rest counted); on a frigate's quarterdeck that is a crowd. Stations only would be
  shorter and say less.
- An order out of turn opens the turn whether the model stood by or only waited for its turn.
- The player at the prompt has no sample; his line is `how am I`. A status line in the
  browser is not built.

may find aboard. The table had four, and their effects were four branches of
`orders._aboard_found`, one effect a thing, one condition of `plausible_when` read (the
first), and a slot for a spar alone. Widened, without a package of its own:

  sheet anchor`) and `{good}` (a good in the hold); one slot a thing, every form naming it
  where an effect falls on it, said at the table's load.

  `chronometer_stopped` (the chronometer's new `stopped` words in its reading, cleared by

- **Conditions** (`orders._PLAUSIBLE`), every one named held together: `days_since_watered`

## The hull's repair, a hotfix (2026-10-21; the owner's ask, between packages)

The cutter grounded off Horta in the Western Islands run (soft sand, struck at five knots:
a leak of about 0.08 m an hour while she lay aground, the carpenter's "strained on the
ground and making water"), and nothing in the game could stop the leak or empty the well:
the pumps and the carpenter's work are milestone 7's (taking on water). Two things are added to the
director's table (`data/director/aboard.yaml`, under "the hull's repair") until then:

- `leak_stopped` (`the leak stopped`, `the leak found and stopped`, `the leak fothered`,
  `her strained seams caulked`): the effect `leak_stopped` sets `ship.extra["leak_m_per_h"]`
  to nought, so `world.ground`'s well gains no more, aground or afloat; doubted by the new
  condition `leaking` when she is making no water.
- `well_pumped` (`the well pumped out`, `the well pumped dry`, `she is pumped out`,
  `the ship pumped out`): the effect `well_pumped` empties `hull.water_in_well_m` and has
  the carpenter count the feet afresh (`Ground._feet_said`, `_waterlogged_said`); doubted by
  the new condition `well_above` (metres) when the well is dry.

What the code shows of the grounding as it stands, for the milestone: the leak runs only
while she is aground (`Ground.tick` calls `_leak` only then), so a ship floated off makes no
more water and keeps what is in the well; and the well's water is read by nothing but the
carpenter's lines (no displacement, trim or handling), so the hotfix is the story's beat and
the well's word, not the ship's behaviour. At five knots the blow of the strike (a ratio of
0.69) is under the strain's decay ratio and the masts are untouched.

Twenty-four things in all. **Pins:** none moved; no recorded passage gives either order.
`tests/test_ground.py`'s
`test_the_director_stops_the_leak_and_pumps_her_out_and_the_well_stays_dry` (the frigate on
the Manacles: doubted before the strike, done after, the well held then emptied, the same
after a replay), and the table's counts in `tests/test_aboard_found.py` and
`tests/test_director.py`.

## The kedging off (2026-10-21; the owner's ask, between packages)

The same grounding off Horta: the captain ordered `lay out a kedge` aground and it was
refused, "she is aground". That was the guard `LayOutKedgeScript.check` kept with the
anchor work's others, though carrying out a kedge is the remedy for a ship on the ground.
Behind the refusal, a kedge could not have helped: aground, `physics/integrate.py` holds
her position and swing whatever the cable pulls, and only the tide's foot under her keel
(`AFLOAT_MARGIN_M`) floated her. The owner's ruling: the honest and conservative way, as
an option, not a quick way off.

- **The kedge laid out aground**: the guard is gone; the boat, the depth and the hawse
  checks stand as they were.
- **The capstan's pull on a ship the ground holds** (`physics/anchor.py`): a cable hove in
  aground no longer has the heaving's exemption from dragging, so past what its anchor
  holds the anchor comes home along the ground, as an anchor's does when she rides by it.
  Without this the scope came in on a ship that could not move and the tension rose
  without limit.
- **The ground's grip and the heave off** (`world/ground.py`, `Ground._heave_off`): each
  tick she is held, the pull of her taut cables (each no more than `min(tension, what its
  anchor holds)`, their directions summed) against `grip_kn`: friction
  (`GRIP_FRICTION_SOFT` 0.4 on sand, mud or shell; `GRIP_FRICTION_ROCK` 0.8 on a rock) times
  the weight the bottom bears, the sea's weight over her waterplane
  (`WATERPLANE_COEFFICIENT` 0.75 of length by beam) to the depth of water she lacks under
  her keel at her own draught, capped at her displacement's weight. Within the afloat
  margin she lacks none, and any strain heaves her off. When the pull is the greater and
  the water `HEAVE_OFF_STEP_FRACTION` (a quarter) of her length along it is deep enough for
  her draught (the tiles and the charted dangers), she is moved there and afloat: "She is
  hove off by the kedge, and afloat again[ on the flood]." (`ship.afloat`, data
  `kedged: true`). Else she lies as she is; the kedge coming home (its distance from her
  lessening while she is held) is said once a grounding, `ground.kedge_home`.

All judgement. **What it does** on Falmouth bank (the frigate, two fathoms and a half,
taken on the ebb, her 300 kg kedge laid out to the east and hove in to twenty fathoms): at
low water the kedge holds 8.6 kN against a grip of 617 kN and comes home; on the flood she
is hove off at tick 28020, 21 minutes before the tide alone floats her at 29280. A ship
riding by a taut bower to seaward when she grounds is helped the same way, as she would
be. Lightening her (starting the water, the guns overboard) is not modelled.

**Pins:** none moved. `test_director.py`'s starter-brief test asked for the briefs folder
to hold exactly the five starters, and failed on the owner's own
`interesting-passage-nobudget.yaml` (2026-10-19) before its useful checks ran; it now
asks that the five be among them, and checks every brief the same. `tests/test_ground.py`'s
`test_a_kedge_laid_out_aground_and_hove_taut_heaves_her_off_before_the_flood_alone`.

## Open, for the lead: found in the Western Islands run (2026-10-21; not fixed)

Found while directing the owner's run off Horta, after the work above, and left for the
lead by the owner's word:

- **The swing at the turn of the tide logs over and over.** `core/world.py` `_tick_tide`
  records `ship.swung` ("The cable slack at the turn; she swings to the flood/ebb.")
  whenever `TideState.flood` differs from `_tide_was_flood`. `flood` is `None` only when
  the stream is under a tenth of the rate (`world/tide.py`, `slack`); just above that, and
  where a constant `current_kn` is added, the stream's direction wobbles about the axis's
  perpendicular and the flag flips minute to minute, so a ship at anchor at the turn
  logs the swing to flood and to ebb a dozen times. It is not only the turn: at Horta it
  ran from 21:18 through the middle watch, every minute at first and then a pair (ebb,
  then flood a minute later) every five or six minutes for hours, so look too at whether
  the stream is read at her position as she sheers about 240 fathoms of cable, and the
  position moves across a place where the stream's direction changes. A fix: hold the new flood or ebb some
  minutes (ten, say) before the line and before `_tide_was_flood` moves, the counter a
  class-level default so a checkpoint-restored world does not crash (as `Ground` needed
  for `_anchor_dist`). It will move the pins of any anchored passage that spans a turn.
- **Weighing a kedge aground is refused** (`WeighAnchorScript` still checks `aground`;
  `LayOutKedgeScript` no longer does).
- **"Man the pumps" is refused in stale words**, now that the well is a reading.
- **Sail's thrust aground is not modelled**: only the cable heaves her off.
- **"Brought up" is logged while she is aground.**
- **The officer of the watch's words are labelled "The captain to the captain"** in the
  log (02:27 and 02:29 at Horta, with the captain back aboard), and "(nobody holds the
  station ...)" is added, though the officer answered him.
- **A thing cannot pass from an unheld person to a held one.** Mr Pearce's `take a sealed
  letter for Falmouth` from Senhor Bettencourt logged "took ..., as said; nothing of the
  ship's changed" and left it in Bettencourt's keeping, and the director may not put it
  in a held person's keeping either (`_aboard_reach`). The way round was to lay it on the
  desk ashore for him to pick up. Wanted: an unheld person's `give` by the director, or a
  held person's `take` from someone within earshot who offers it.
- **A name said in full is refused in the wrong words.** Ashore, Mr Pearce's "Say to Mr
  Josiah Hale ..." was refused twice with "The officer of the watch has not the deck";
  "Say to Mr Hale ..." went through. The full name should match, or the refusal say the
  name was not known.
- **The director cannot put stores aboard.** The `aboard:` table only takes water and
  provisions away (`water_tons`, `provisions_days`, the shares); a merchant who sends
  provisions or water out with his lighters has no order for it. The captain's own `send
  for provisions for 8 days` (the yard's, `ports.py`) does it at the yard's price. Wanted:
  an `aboard:` form for stores received, and no form to walk an unheld person ashore from
  one place to another (`person: "<name>" goes to the quay` is refused).
- **The director's stand-by events misfire at weighing.** Standing by "under way" woke at
  23:13 when the small bower was catted, the best bower still down; standing by "the
  anchor weighed" did not wake at 00:23 when "Under way ..., the best bower catted and
  fished" was logged. And a stand-by can't be changed while it runs without `say` putting
  words in the log.
- **A thing put in the boat stays aboard.** The captain put the Madeira case in the boat;
  the boat went in with Mr Pearce and came back, and the case was still "in the boat on
  the quarterdeck".
- **Not understood or refused:** "ring the bell" and "strike the bell" (a fog signal, or to
  guide a boat in); "send a letter to ..." (but "send the boat with a letter" is taken);
  "pawl the capstan"; "send the larboard watch below";
  the "storm trysail" asked by a name the rig does not carry.

## Package 68: the review's mending (2026-10-23)

The cold review of 2026-10-22 (`docs/playtests/2026-10-18-to-22-owner-playtests-and-review/
FreeSail-M7b-Playtest-and-Hotfix-Review.md`, the register R-01 to R-63 and the fold-in's §3.3),
eighteen items, each one finding's mending; the finding's evidence bound where it and the
brief differed. Built in a worktree off `809620b`. Nothing of 58's or 67's is built; the
consent records were not touched. Spec M5 §12 and M7b §2 to §9, §14 and §17 "as built
(package 68)"; truths 7b-120 to 7b-123.

### Each item against its intent

1. **Riding means riding (R-01): built, the measure taken another way.** `lookout.riding`,
   one predicate for the master's account (`reckoning._riding`) and the lookout's land-ahead:
   aground, or an anchor down and holding (none dragging) and either brought up by it
   (`Anchor.brought_up`, said in the log) or her *headway* over the ground under
   `RIDING_WAY_KN`, half a knot. The brief's word was her speed over the ground; measured, a
   frigate riding to the tide in Carrick Road sheers at up to two knots over the ground at
   the turn and goes nowhere (so the brought-up anchor is the test once the log has said it),
   and a ship falling astern on her cable as it is veered is not under way (so the measure
   before she is brought up is her way along her head: the speed alone moved the gate 5b
   passage and the naval cruise for a ship falling astern, and the headway moves neither).
   Truth 7b-120: the cutter let go at seven knots a mile off the beach drags her bower, the
   account runs, the lookout says the land ahead at eight cables (notable) and three cables
   (urgent) before she strikes; the old rule said neither.
2. **Words to the captain (R-13, R-14): built.** The player at the prompt holds the
   captain's station for every word said to him (`stations._player_captain`, the harness's
   `held_stations`); the line is the speaker's own ("The officer of the watch (Mr Pearce), on
   the quarterdeck, to the captain: ..."), and a word kept for an empty station is kept under
   the speaker's mark; the addressee is counted and cut on one tokenisation
   (`_after_words`) and the longest naming taken (a person's name over a station's word), so
   the word after "Mr Bowen," is kept. Truth 7b-121.
3. **A person made aboard another ship (R-15): built, the refusal's half.** `person: make
   ..., aboard <another ship>` (and "on the quarterdeck of the <ship>", "the <ship>'s
   gunroom") is refused in words ("names another ship: a person is made aboard the Amazon or
   ashore, and the people of other ships are not kept ...; nothing is made"); her own name
   said with a place is taken at the place said. *Taken another way*: the other ships are far
   detail with no people of their own (the World keeps one ship's company), so there is no
   crewed World to bind him to; the brief's "or is refused in words" is the half built.
4. **The MCP door (R-25, R-27, R-30): built.** `MCP_WAIT_S` and the desktop entries'
   `--wait` fifty seconds (under the client's sixty); a reconnect within `RECONNECT_S` of a
   held call is a cut call: the held result is delivered with "reconnected", never the brief

   a reply in the chat while seated; Harness.md's "four minutes" is fifty seconds.
5. **The brig limit (R-38): built.** The brief's enemy limit ranks by `captains.size_rank_of`,
   as the tops rank a sail, so a frigate is refused under "no enemy heavier than a brig" and a

6. **The lugger gets under way as a lugger (R-45): built.** `GetUnderWayScript`'s lug branch:

   Truth 7b-122: the Éclair weighs and makes six and a half knots full and by, never aback.
7. **The chart's fathoms (R-05): built.** `FATHOM` in `client/units.js`, the sounding's
   figure by one function (`formatFathoms`), finite or "no bottom"; a test that every `U.`

8. **The director hidden (R-20): built.** The eased clock's line for the director, and every

9. **A stand-by replaced (R-28): built.** A `stand_by` sent while another runs replaces it

10. **The director's echoes and the budget (R-61): built.** The director's own `say as`,

### The rule for checkpointed classes

**Every attribute of a class that is checkpointed (pickled or saved with the World) gets a
class default**, so that an object of the earlier build, unpickled or made with `__new__`,
reads the new attribute as its default and never raises. The hotfix's checkpoint crash was a
`Ground` of the earlier build with no `_kedge` attribute; this package's new attributes keep
the rule (`Harness._own_lines = ()`, `GetUnderWayScript.lugger = False`), and the
regression test builds a `Ground` with `__new__` and ticks it aground with a taut cable.

### Item 19: the pilot's wind (found on the way, the lead's word of 2026-10-23)

`Ports._as_she_will_lie` and `_made_good_on` count how near she lies, and her course made
good, from `_wind_from_over_the_water`: the true wind less the stream's set at her, the wind
her sails feel; the wind over the ground itself where there is no stream (so that no water
without a stream moves). A test of the helper beside the Goulet's
(`test_the_pilot_reckons_how_near_she_lies_by_the_wind_over_the_water`): ten knots from NW
over the ground in a four-knot flood toward 080° is a wind from 338° over the water.

**No pin moves.** The whole slow tier on the code with the fix (the tree at `1cd9a23` with
`ports.py` of `465ad80`; 06:04 to 07:05): 3,863 passed, 11 expected failures, every pinned
passage against its figure, the merchant passage and the intent schooner through the Goulet
among them (the pilot's "as near as she will lie" never binds in them: their wind is free
of his legs). Two failed, the Goulet's two cases from the wardroom save, and there the work
stopped, on the lead's word ("if it still fails after the fix, say exactly where she goes
and stop there"):

- **From 113000** (the replay's history moved by item 1): the pilot cons her NE and NE by N
  for his first mark (48° 19.53' N, 4° 37.8' W), passes it at 114480 (land ahead, nine
  cables, to larboard), takes up the leg for 48° 19.92' N, 4° 36.36' W at NE by E to E by N,
  is warned of the Mingan a mile on the starboard bow at 115020 ("leave it to starboard"),
  and for his next aim (48° 20.27' N, 4° 35.76' W) steers NE by E and then ENE "as near as
  she will lie" in the wind over the water; she keeps her way now (4.4 knots, no sails
  lifting, where the wind over the ground had her at 1.8), but the flood of 3.9 knots toward
  080° sets her bodily east, the lookout cries the Mingan four cables ahead at 115320, and
  she strikes it at 115561 at four knots and a half.
- **From 114000** (passed before the fix): his first order is NNE, five points to port, as
  near as she will lie, and the yards still trimmed for the wind on the quarter: she is
  taken aback at 114049 and lies in irons for twenty minutes; the flood sets her east of his
  first mark; at 115800 he gives W for the mark, now astern of her, and she is put about to
  beat back to it against the flood; she works to and fro off Petit Minou for the rest of
  the 110 minutes, and at 120600 the Mingan is four cables ahead again; no berth said, no
  grounding (the test's failure: no `port.pilot_berth`). With the old pilot's wind restored
  (`c062f89`) this case passes, so its failure is the fix's.

What is left is the pilot's conn and not his wind: with the wind over the water he finds,
rightly, that the NE legs inside Bertheaume will not be laid on this flood under this wind,
and he has no answer but to steer as near as she will lie (from 113000) or to go back for a
mark set astern (from 114000). A pilot's answers would be to wait for the slack in the road,
to work the north shore's eddy, or to anchor; and his first turn should trim before it puts
her five points nearer the wind.

**A debt, not a fix.** On the lead's word (2026-10-23) the wind over the water is kept, and
the pilot's conn in a strong flood is booked as package 58b's item 6, the captain's sea
sense, beside the rules captain's. The two cases
(`test_ports.py::test_the_pilot_allows_for_the_set_before_his_turn_in_the_goulet_on_the_flood`,
113000 and 114000) are marked expected failures, strict, as 57's gale trial is marked,
with the account above in the marker and the comment over it: the pilot lays legs the
flood will not let her make and has no answer but to pinch (113000: onto the Mingan at
115561) or go back (114000: aback at 114049, beating back for a mark astern, no berth in
the 110 minutes). Strict, so that the suite says so the day 58b's conn brings her in, and
the marker is lifted then. The logs: the whole slow tier with the fix,
`slow19-new.log`; the courses, `g-fix.txt` (113000) and `g-fix114.txt` (114000), in the
build's scratch directory.

## Package 58a: the sample's deltas and the stand-by's instruments (2026-10-23)

The cold review of 2026-10-22 (R-26, R-31, R-04, R-39 in part, R-42; the directors' and the
lugger officer's own accounts in its §7.1 and §7.2), the owner's "delta" of 2026-10-17 and
his rulings on the brief (the dry run the director's; `ahead` every station's that has the
deck's readings, the director's by the truth; the deltas watched for forgetting, the lead's
"as before" line). Built in a worktree off `872aa61`, beside 58b and 67; spec M7b §3, §5 and
§12 "as built (package 58a)"; the Harness's §21b; the primer's chapters 6, 19 and 20; truths
7b-124 to 7b-126. Nothing of 58b's (the captain's sea sense, `captains.py`, `brains.py`,
`ports.py`, the evolutions) or 67's (the desk's seat, `harbour.py`, the `seat:` form, the
channel) is touched but where named below; `remote.py` has one line (a dry run is a read
at the desk), `core/replay.py` one guard (found on the way).

### Each item against its intent

1. **Deltas: built.** A sample after the first carries what changed since the model's last
   reply. The readings were deltas since 31c; what repeated was the rows whose words move
   with every bearing and the history around them. The sail rows (`strangers`,
   `sail_in_sight`, `stranger_in_sight`) are compared by each sail and how far she is made
   out (`Harness._delta_keys`), so the list comes when a sail came, went or was made out
   further, not each time her bearing moved; the lookout's row by who holds the masthead and
   his last hail (its sightings are `in_sight`'s); the officer's row by everything but the
   captain's words to him; the captain's word and question to the station are not given
   again in the log beside the sample's `word` (`_without_the_word`); the stand-by's notable
   lines are counted and found in the waking sample's log (`lines_in`), no longer listed
   twice. Each sample of deltas closes with `as_before` ("As before: the sails, two sail in
   sight, the book; the other readings as last told (readings gives every row).") for the
   owner's caution. The first sample of a seating (the brief resent clears it, as 31c's) and
   the first after a handover fold are whole. **"Still waiting"** lists only the lines since
   the last call of the same wait (`still_waiting(..., listed)`, the bridge's `_listed`).
   *Taken another way, in part*: the brief's reading was a per-station cursor for each part;
   the deltas compare each part's own key with the last told, which is the same thing and
   keeps nothing new in the save; and the "still waiting" cursor is the MCP bridge's, not
   the game's, since a door's poll is no act (a cursor in the game would make the samples
   depend on the polls, and a replay by the transcript does not poll). The standing orders
   reach a sample only through the `captain` row, which 31c's deltas already carry only when
   the book changes.
2. **The notable-noise rules: built.** *The swing at the turn* has its cause mended, not
   masked: `TideState.flood` is None where no stream runs (`streaming`, the area's rate
   nought: `NO_STREAM` beyond every area), and the riding words there are "head to wind";
   the World's turn of the tide (`_tick_tide`) passes over a None as it passes over slack, so
   a ship sheering across an area's edge says her swing at the channel's own turns. The
   Horta night, from the filed save's own scenario, ship, berth and evening: **110 swing
   lines in six hours under the old cause, one now** (truth 7b-125). *A recurring line* of
   `RECURRING_KINDS` (`evolution.waiting`, `sounding`, `aboard.found`, `well.sounded`)
   whose words equal the last of its kind is routine (`World.record`; urgent never); the
   first, and any whose words changed, keep their severity. *Light airs* take the hysteresis
   of a point and two knots held ten minutes: they fall light when the mean has stood under
   the floor (four knots) `WIND_LIGHT_HOLD_S`, ten minutes (it was a minute), and settle when
   it has stood `WIND_SETTLE_BAND_KN` (two knots) above the floor, its direction within a
   point of where the settling began, `WIND_SETTLE_S`, ten minutes (it was five minutes at
   the floor, whatever the direction did). A breeze going between three and five knots every
   twenty minutes for four hours now says "Light and variable airs." once, where it said it
   six times with five settlings between (`test_log_lines`).
3. **Tripwires: built** (`freesail/agents/tripwires.py`). `her way settled` (her speed
   within a quarter of a knot and her head within a quarter of a point for two minutes,
   measured afresh at every order given: after "steer N" from a southerly course the frigate
   settled eight minutes on, at 7.3 knots); `depth under <n> fathoms` (the chart at her
   account, or the lead's cast); `speed under <n> knots`, `speed over <n> knots`; `the wind
   over <n> knots` (the true wind); `a point of interest within <n> miles` (the chart's
   places, marks, lights, dangers and anchorages, and the world's `mark:`s, new within the
   miles of her account; the wake names it). The dialect's conditions underneath are the
   book's (`parse_condition`), the two of her own way are the module's; each joins the others
   with *or*, and the refusal of a stand-by it cannot read lists them.
4. **`ahead` and the cost of thinking: built.** `ahead` is a row of the registry
   (`readings.ahead_words`), every station's that has the deck's readings: the land, a
   charted danger within two cables of her track with too little water for her draught, the
   depth by the chart where it shoals under ten fathoms or changes by a third, a sail within
   two points of her head; from her account, her head and the log's speed; nothing at
   anchor, aground or with no way on. A millisecond to read. The director's is the truth's
   (the player's ship's entry in `truth`, "by the truth"). The station's line and the
   director's close with "<n> minutes of the ship's time since your last reply"
   (`Harness._replied_tick`, a class default for checkpoints).
5. **The forms reference, the dry run and the lookups: built.** `director.WORLD_ORDER_FORMS`
   is one table of every form, its words, what it does and examples; the library's grammar
   topic's fourth part, "the world orders", is written from it, and so are the station
   brief's examples (`_q`) and the starter briefs' (a test holds each starter's examples to
   the table). Every example is dry-run on the sea it is meant for (a fresh one, one with her
   ship far off, one with her ships and people near) and is performed or doubted with what
   it would do, but eight the test's seas cannot do as they stand, each with the game's
   honest word about the situation (the seat's consent, the starters' own ships not on the
   test's sea, "carry on" with no order standing, "fill away" when she is not hove to, "haul
   off" with no sail in sight of her, a payment from an empty purse). **The dry run**
   (`world_order(text, dry_run=true)`, `director.dry_run`) answers in the channel's order
   (the budget read without renewing it, the rule of reach, the brief, the form, the doubt)
   and reads what the order would do by performing it on a copy of the world (the
   checkpoint's own pickling), let go; it writes nothing anywhere and spends no act, it is
   counted among the reads, and at the desk it is a meanwhile read through which a stand-by
   goes on. *Taken another way*: the doubt a dry run shows is not "shown" for 68's rule of
   the first reason (that reads the director's log, and a dry run writes nothing, so that
   it replays alike by the transcript and by the acts): the dry run says to enter the order
   once and then with its reason. **The lookups**: `truth(ports=)`, `truth(grounds=)`,
   `truth(systems=true)`, `truth(at=)`, each a small read. **The page** "the world" (the
   library's, `director.world_page`): the systems (they add; they grow in), ships put on the
   sea and their companies, what each order logs and to whom, the doubt's figures, every
   figure formatted from the constant the code uses and a test checking each.
6. **Weather, the small part: built.** An appended system grows in from nothing at the
   order's tick to its anomaly over `APPEND_RAMP_S` (an hour) at the least, or until its
   first point's time when that is later (`System.ramp_from`, `ramp_until`, class defaults);
   a waypoint appended to a track that had ended runs from where the system stands at the
   order's tick, reached an hour on at the soonest, the result saying so, and its speed is
   doubted from there; a high is doubted like a low, above the season's ceiling (the month's
   background with its strongest high and `HIGH_CEILING_MARGIN_HPA`, four hPa, over;
   judgement) or `LOW_DEEP_HPA` strong within `LOW_NEAR_KM` out of a glass not rising. A
   990 hPa low appended over the ship for three hours on now takes the glass down two hPa a
   quarter hour (1012.6 at the order, 1010.4 a quarter hour on), where it stepped 27 hPa at
   the order (1012.6 to 985.6, measured on `872aa61`). Kept out, as briefed: the summed
   field's bound and the climatology's drift onto Iberia.
7. **Truths and records: built.** Truth 124 (the second sample with no sail line and the
   strangers' list only when a sail was made out further, "still waiting" with only the new
   lines, the waking sample's lines counted in its log); 125 (the Horta night's swing once a
   turn); 126 (a dry run of a doubted order returns the doubt and what it would do, the
   log's digest, the inputs, the marks and the director's log the same, no act spent; then
   entered, doubted on the record, entered again with its reason, performed and counted).

### What moved

## Package 67: the director's seat made real, and the channel between the player and the director (2026-10-23)

Built on `872aa61` (after 68's merge) beside 58a and 58b, on the brief as the owner approved
it: the desk reads a held seat; the game starts the director's API door; the seat's cost
said and counted; the form widened to every station of a ship, the player's own on by
default, and to a person's voice; the channel at the prompt and in a small browser pane;
the seated door's fold at two fifths of the context. A new module keeps the seats
(`freesail/world/seats.py`), so that `orders.py`, where 58a works on the dry run, carries
only `_seat` and `_unseat` as doors into it.

### Each item against its intent

1. **The desk reads the seat.** Built. `Desk.station` asks `seats.match` for a seat held at
   that station (on that ship, or the player's own) for that model; a door that has one is
   admitted under its budget, the admission an input (`seat_admitted`) after the seating
   so that a replay counts from the same point, the samples counted from the station's
   samples at the admission (a station held before does not bring its old samples), the
   hours from the admission's tick; the door note, the first answer and the director's log
   say so. Any other door is admitted as before (a seat held for one model does not keep
   the station from another, as the brief says). The seat kept once a minute by the World
   itself (`World.tick` calls `crews.enforce_budgets`, now `seats.enforce`, whenever seats
   are held: 43's call came only while a ship with a captain of her own was about): spent,
   stood down with the reason; its station released after the admission, the seat ends
   with it; no door within its `within`, it lapses; each in the director's log
   (`director.seat`). The voyage's end ends it with the game (nothing outlives the World).
2. **The game starts the director's door.** Built, the lead's reading taken as written:
   `Harbour.start_door(..., seat=, seat_model=, by="the director")`, called by
   `Harbour.tend_seats`, which the driver's clock calls every tenth of a second
   (`Driver.on_tend`), running or not. The door's command line is `door_argv`'s with the
   seat's model, its dialect from the settings, the station, `--ship` and `--budget-tokens`
   where the settings name one; the key is read by the door's process, never the game's;
   the pane is in the doors tab beside the owner's, marked *The director's seat's API
   door* (`Door.by`, a class on the pane). A seat gone (unseat, spent, lapsed, a new game)
   stops its door if it was never admitted; one stood down lets the door end of itself
   (*its station was released*), stopped only after a grace of twenty seconds (the first
   build stopped it at once and raced the door's own exit: *stopped from the harbour* and a
   KeyboardInterrupt in the pane). **The models the settings can call** are
   `settings.callable_models`: the API door's model and `doors.api.models` (names, or
   `{name, dialect}`). A seat for another is refused **before the World**, at the
   director's door (`director.direct`) and at the owner's `world:` in the browser
   (`Driver.submit`), *Refused: the settings call no model by that name; the API door's
   model is <x>*: refused in the World it would have put the settings in the log (truth
   7b-110) and made the replay depend on the settings. The director's log keeps the
   refusal without the name. Without a harbour (the console), the seat is a record, and
   its result says how its door is started by hand; its words are the same either way, so
   that a replay writes the same line.
3. **The seat's cost said, and counted.** Built. The brief's paragraph
   (`director.SEAT_AND_CHANNEL_BRIEF`, kept apart from the forms reference 58a works on,
   after the fixed part and before the player's brief); `seat:`'s result repeats the
   budget and the cost's shape; the day's budget line (`director.budget_words`, the
   director's notice every sample) names the seats held and their spending. R-34's list:
   the seated door's fold at two fifths of the context (`remote.SEAT_BUDGET_SHARE`), the
   settings' `seat_budget_tokens` naming another figure (tokens, or a share: `0.4`, `40%`,
   `2/5`), sent by the door as `--budget-tokens`, which every API door now takes; a fold
   after a double cut-off (the desk folds on the door's words, `CUT_FOLD_NOTE`, at every
   door whose words say *was cut off again*, the local runner's too); the conversation's
   size said at the API door's terminal at each fold; the reseat line naming the captain's
   grants that lapsed with the leaving (`Harness._lapsed`, said only where there were
   some).
4. **The form widened.** Built, both halves; the person's seat as the honest smaller
   version the lead's reading names, well inside the day. Every station of a ship
   (captain, officer of the watch, master, lookout, passenger; a station a wardroom names
   otherwise too), the player's own by no `of` or her name, on by default, the grant's
   `seats_on_the_players_ship: false` keeping the seats off her (a person aboard her
   among them); the rule of reach through `orders.held_stations`. A person bound to a
   station is seated at it; a person nobody holds, aboard or ashore, is **his voice**: a
   station of the passenger's kind bound to him under his name (the binding quiet, the
   order being the input; its lines carry the director's actor and are for the record),
   his own brief (`seats.VOICE_BRIEF`, built by `voice_station` since the passenger's
   factory reads the passenger's binding, not the name it is made under), heard where he
   stands, `say as` him refused while held. **Taken another way: a person aboard another
   ship** is refused in words; no other ship has a World of people (68 refuses one made
   there), so there is nobody to bind. Booked onward with what was learned: the seat at a
   person on another ship wants 68's person aboard another ship first; and a voice
   station is listed among `the stations` while it is bound (*the mr veale, a passenger's
   (Mr Veale)*), which a dedicated kind would hide.
5. **The channel.** Built. `director: <words>` (any line after `director:` but `brief`,
   `budget` and nothing, `console.director_word`) is `director.player_word`: an input
   (`player_word`), the director's log (`director.player`), a word in its next sample
   (*The player, apart from the game: ...*, which wakes a stand-by), the drivers'
   listeners (`director.listen`, beside the World in a weak map, never on it). The answer,
   `answer the player: <words>`, through `world_order` (before any world order is read, no
   act counted), or opening a reply's text or an `answer` (`director.thought`, two lines in
   `Harness._say` and `answer`); to the director's log (`director.answered`) and the
   listeners: the console prints it as its own line, the browser's server sends it to a
   small pane in the corner (`#channel-panel`), and `GET /api/director/channel` reads it.
   The play log, and its replay's, carry neither; `two stories` shows both. R-21's words:
   the desk and the MCP bridge answer the director's own words as its log's. `tell the
   director` stays refused, its words naming the channel.
6. **Truths and records.** Truths 7b-130 to 7b-132 as briefed; §2a and §6 as built; the
   Harness's §19b (with §17, §19 and §22 pointing to it); the primer's chapters 6 and 20.

### The seat's cost on the fake Messages API

The API door in a thread against the game (`tests/messages_api.py`'s server reporting
200,000 tokens of context and, as its usage, each request's own body at four characters a
token), the officer of the watch's station, every reply a word and `stand_by` until a
glass, and the handover note written when it is asked:

| The door | samples | requests | the fold counted from | folds | prompt tokens sent | the largest request | the last |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seated (the default) | 48 | 48 | 80,000 | 0 | 958,466 | 28,088 | 28,088 |
| not seated | 48 | 48 | 200,000 | 0 | 956,402 | 28,045 | 28,045 |
| seated (the default) | 132 | 133 | 80,000 | 1 | 4,112,334 | 56,792 | 18,490 |
| not seated | 132 | 132 | 200,000 | 0 | 4,702,405 | 61,958 | 61,958 |

A quiet seat grows about 380 tokens a sample (a glass's sample and a short reply): a day of
glasses stays under the fold, and the first fold came at the 56,000 the default asks
(80,000 less its reserve), after two and a half days, the conversation going back to about
18,000. By the 132nd sample the seated door sent 13 per cent fewer tokens and its requests
were a third the size; the difference grows with the square of the seat's length, and far
faster with a seat whose samples are big (R-34's two seats sent sixteen million tokens in
two hours, a sample's readings and log many times these). These are the requests' sizes,
not their price: the door caches the brief and the conversation, so most of each request is
read from the cache. (The 160 samples asked of the script gave 132: the loop's wait under
three other builders' suites let some glasses pass in one tick; both runs alike.)

### Found on the way

- **Mended, since it blocked the admission's replay:** a seat held under consent records
  kept elsewhere (`--consent-records`, as the lead's playtests keep them) was refused in the

  A replay now reads a seat's consent from the world orders' outcomes in play
  (`replay.replay` sets `World.replayed_orders`; `seats.hold` takes "done" as the consent
  then read). A seat refused in play for a consent the replaying machine has would still
  be held in the replay; not mended (the reason is not kept).
- **Not mended:** a reply a door delivers at the tick another station is seated, after its
  seating, is replayed before it (two lines of the same tick change places); seen with two
  doors stationed at tick 0 and a reply between, without any seat. The test seats them a
  minute apart.
- **Not mended:** the rule of reach's refusal for a voice reads *Mr Pentreath is the mr
  pentreath's, held by a model* (the station's name is the person's); the words are
  `orders.reach`'s.

### Pins

No pin moved, and none is expected to: every new path is entered only where a seat is
held, the channel is used or a station is taken again after the captain's grants lapsed,
and no recorded passage seats a model, speaks to the director or reseats a station with
grants. `World.tick` calls the seats' keeping only while `director_seats` holds one; the
brief's new paragraph is in no log; the director's free text is a thought as before unless
it opens with `answer the player:`; `budget_words` is as before with no seat. The slow tier
below re-ran every pinned passage against its figure.

### Decisions for the lead and the owner

- **The seat at a person on another ship**: booked, after 68's person aboard another ship.
- **A voice listed among the stations** while bound: keep, or a kind of its own hidden
  from `the stations`?
- **A seat whose station is released ends with it** (the model's own stand-down, the
  owner's word, the door stopped): the director seats again if it wants the station held;
  the alternative, the seat waiting for another door, risked the harbour starting doors in
  a loop.
- **The seated door's terminal** says the fold at the whole context in its first line (the
  door cannot know it will be seated) and the true figure in the game's answer after it.
- **The settings' "account"** is read as the dialect; the game does not read the
  credential store to see that a key is there (the key is the door's process's alone), so
  a missing key is said in the door's pane when it starts.
- **A harbour with no API model in its settings** refuses every director's seat on that
  server (the brief's "the models the settings can call"); a seat for a door the owner
  means to start by hand through the desktop client is then given at the console or with
  the settings naming the model.
