## Package 58b: the captain's sea sense, third pass (2026-10-23)

The rules captain's and the pilot's half of package 58 (58a, the deltas and the stand-by, is
its own builder's). Built in a worktree off `872aa61`. The physics of the wind across the
stern is not changed (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-23); nothing of 58a's or 67's files is
touched; the consent records were not touched. Spec M6 §4 and M7b §24 "as built (package
58b)"; the primer's chapters 7 and 11; truths 7b-127 to 7b-129.

### Each item against its intent

1. **A leg laid again as the stream changes: built.** `Captain._stream_changed`, on passage
   and running for shelter: the master's tide turns (his `reckoning.tide` line with `turn`,
   kept till answered and answered ten minutes after a laying at the soonest,
   `RELAY_TURN_LEAST_S`), or the stream the master allows now, against the one the course
   was laid allowing, would carry her more than a cable (`RELAY_OFF_LINE_NM`) off the line
   in the next glass (`RELAY_GLASS_H`), a glass between such layings (`RELAY_LEAST_S`). The
   laying is the captain's "shape a course for" with the reason said ("the tide has turned,
   the ebb making"; "the stream changed since the leg was laid: a knot and a quarter SW
   now"). The leg as laid is read off every `helm.set` of "shape a course for", his own or
   his book's hourly "the leg". The perception carries the master's tide
   (`Perception.tide_allowed`). Truth 7b-127: the Éclair's leg laid at 05:30 allowing the
   flood in the channel of Bas is laid again at the master's turn to the ebb, within ten
   minutes of it, and she clears the channel.
2. **Casts on a long leg: built, the bringing-to taken another way.** `Captain._casts`; the
   five doctrines' thresholds `cast_glass_fathoms` 20, `cast_hour_fathoms` 100,
   `cast_inshore_nm` 15 and `cast_bring_to_hours` 4. The hand lead every glass where the
   chart has under twenty fathoms at the account (`Perception.chart_fathoms`); the deep-sea
   lead every hour inside the hundred-fathom line inshore (the land in sight, or the coast
   within five leagues by his account). Under four knots she casts as she goes. *Taken
   another way*: over four knots the deep-sea lead wants her brought to, and brought to
   every hour she never reached Brest in the intent scenario (eight bring-tos in the
   Channel's approaches, the stream setting her back at each), and brought to near the land
   in the lee-shore trial she was set onto it; so she is brought to for it once a watch at
   most, only on passage or running for shelter (never beating), never in a blow (the wind
   at the shorten-sail line), never with land under her lee within her sea room, and filled
   away at the sounding or after a quarter of an hour; the other hours the cast waits. Not
   in pilot water nor with the pilot aboard (the book's own lead has that). The first cast
   comes a glass or an hour into the leg, not at its laying: cast at once, the deep-sea
   lead held the hands of the King's brig-sloop from the director's heave-to for her
   station (truth 7b-113 failed on the fast tier; mended, item 2's by bisection).
3. **The wind across the stern: built as the ruling has it.** The physics unchanged; no
   evolution ordered by a helm order. `orders.navigation.watch_the_stern`, called each tick
   by the evolutions' runner beside `keep_course_pending` (the runner is outside the files
   listed; it is the one place every ship's tick passes with her evolutions known): when
   the wind has come a point (`STERN_CROSSED_DEG`, 11.25°) past dead astern onto the other
   quarter, with a dipping lug set against its mast or a square yard braced for the old
   tack, one notable line, `sail.across_the_stern`:
   "The wind has come across the stern to the larboard quarter: the foresail and the
   mainsail are against their masts; dip them when you will." (and "; and the yards are
   braced for the starboard tack, by the lee; brace them round when you will"), once a
   crossing, nothing done. A manoeuvre's own crossing (wearing, gybing, heaving to) is its
   own and says nothing (as is a crossing aground). The line's data name the boom sails,
   which gybe as 37m built them. The rules captain answers it as his next orders
   (`Captain._across_the_stern`: "dip the foresail", "dip the mainsail"; `trim sails` for
   the yards; `trim the sheets` where only booms crossed), not hove to nor in distress.
   Truth 7b-128.
4. **The course given when she gathers way: built.** `orders.navigation.gathering_way`
   (`GATHERED_WAY_KN`, a knot): from the anchor aweigh (the weighing evolutions'
   `WEIGHING_PHASES`) until she has a knot of headway with no sail aback and a sail set,
   a course given her is held (`Judgement("pending", ..., crossing="way")`): "SE is held
   till she has gathered way: the anchor is aweigh and she has not a knot of way on her
   yet; it is given when she has, her sails drawing", and steered then by
   `keep_course_pending` ("She has gathered way, 1.1 knots, her sails drawing: ...",
   `helm.course_given`, data `held_for: way`). The rules captain shapes his leg again at that
   line ("she has gathered way"), so its allowance is worked with way on. The starter book
   says so in a comment and the primer's chapter 11 has the lugger's two lines.
5. **The gale book's mending (57's debt): built, the judgement waiting for the lead's
   playtest.** A head sail straining at its bolt-ropes (`strain.warning` with "bolt-ropes")
   in a wind over the shorten-sail line is taken in before it blows out
   (`_head_sails_straining`, storm canvas excepted, once in ten minutes); filling away from
   lying to with the wind still over that line the close-reefed topsails are set "to claw
   off the land under her lee" or "to give her way, the wind still strong"
   (`_sail_to_fill_away`); a lugger lies to under her own storm canvas: "shift the mainsail
   for the storm lug" (the taille-vent), "shift the jib for the storm jib", "set the storm
   jib", and "heave to" when it is set (`_lugger_storm_lug`; probe: hove to at 3420 under
   them, never aback, 2.2 knots). *Taken another way*: **the band under the reefs**, a
   good full by compass a point free of the helm's full and by, was built and withdrawn:
   under it the frigate was aback every two minutes and a half in both trials, worse than
   the helm's own band (`hull.full_for_way`), which is kept. Truth 7b-129: the station
   gale's frigate lies a-try four hours under the book (243 minutes in the probe), never
   aback, nothing lost, under two knots on the mean.
6. **The pilot's conn in a stream (68's debt): built.** `world/ports.py`: each leg of his
   track ahead judged before he stands into it (`_leg_made`, `_foul_leg`, `_legs_judged`)
   with the stream at the time she comes to it (`world.tide.at`) and the wind over that
   water, at `PILOT_JUDGE_WAY_KN`; a leg she lies, or sags off by under a point, serves; one
   that sags more serves only if her sagged track has water under her keel and passes no
   danger (`chart.dangers_ahead` within a cable abeam), the next leg judged from where it
   leaves her. One that will not serve: he brings her up where she is in
   `PILOT_WAIT_MOST_FATHOMS` (25) or less, saying so and when he looks for the stream to
   serve; looks again every five minutes once she rides (not dragging, not anchoring);
   weighs when the legs will serve by the time she is under way (`PILOT_WEIGH_AHEAD_S`);
   takes up his track again from where she lies (`_joined_track`) on the tack toward his
   mark (`_as_she_will_lie` takes the other tack when her own lies more than eight points
   from it); and, weighed, does not bring her up again for three quarters of an hour
   (`PILOT_COMMITTED_S`). Deeper than 25 fathoms he says he cannot bring her up and cons
   her on as near as she will lie. He gives no course over a tack or wear in hand (cast the
   wrong way from her anchor she was given a new course each minute of the wear and worn
   by turns). His own turn of two points and more onto a course within eight points of the
   wind and a point nearer it is trimmed for first ("The pilot: trim for close hauled,
   before I put her head to NNE") and the helm put over a minute later
   (`PILOT_TRIM_FIRST_S`). The two Goulet cases (113000, 114000) are lifted, the wait
   asserted. **Found on the way and mended** (the captain's half): with the conn given by
   the officer (`let the pilot take her in`), the captain's 'on passage' book written again
   at the weigh after the wait carried "the leg", which shaped her back out of the Goulet
   for the outer mark under the pilot's feet and set her onto the Fillettes; the book now
   leaves "the leg" out whenever the pilot has the conn, by whoever's word
   (`Captain._pilot_has_conn`). Two more from the intent schooner's passage: a course of
   his held by the helm till she has way for it is not given again over itself (given each
   minute, it was held again each minute and she never came round), and a weigh of his
   refused (her boat away for the prices) is asked again each half hour, not at every look
   (`PILOT_WAIT_REFUSED_S`). *Tried and withdrawn*: a rule bringing her up when she had
   been "as near as she will lie" for his mark in hand ten minutes without closing it, and
   judging that leg before weighing again. It brought the intent schooner up in the
   Goulet's mouth before she was set ashore, but from 114000 it brought the merchantman up
   three times after weighing where she would have fetched (she berths at 126960 without
   it) and the case failed; withdrawn, and the intent schooner pinned as below. The open
   water to his mark in hand is hers to work as she can, as before.
7. **Truths and records: built.** Truths 7b-127, 7b-128, 7b-129; the records as listed
   above.

### 43b's against-the-mast fraction, checked

`LUG_AGAINST_MAST_AREA` is two thirds (`physics/sails.py`, 43b). Measured on the Éclair of
the lugger-roscoff scenario, wind 12.3 knots, the mean speed through the water over minutes
3 to 13 after the turn, lugs left against the masts against the same turn with them dipped,
the same seed (`fraction.py` in the scratch directory):

| Course | Apparent wind | Against the masts | Dipped | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NE, running (through the stern) | ~142° | 3.87 kn | 4.28 kn | 0.90 |
| NNW, on a wind | ~64° | 4.23 kn | 4.59 kn | 0.92 |

**The old figure is kept** (2/3; no new figure): a lug against its mast costs her a tenth of
her way, which the line now says and the captain answers. For the lead: the period's
complaint of a lug left against the mast is worst on a wind (the sail bellied round the
mast, the luff hard to set), and a stronger penalty on a wind than off it would say so; that
is a physics change, which this package was told not to make.

### Decisions for the lead and the owner

- **The intent schooner unsold** (items 1, 2 and 6): her passage moved by the leg's layings
  and the casts brings her to the Iroise as the flood runs hard into the Goulet against a
  north-westerly, and the pilot brings her up in the road to wait where the old pilot put
  her on the Mingan; the captain's boat for the prices (45's rule, in port from the road)
  then keeps her from weighing at the slack. A captain who held his boat while the pilot
  waits was tried (her pilot then weighed at 113940, was set onto the north shore of the
  Goulet's mouth pinching for his mark, and she took the ground at 126044), and withdrawn
  with the pinching rule above. For the lead: whether the captain's business waits for the
  pilot, and the pilot's answer to the open water to his mark in hand when it will not be
  fetched.
- **The gale trials**: the book is mended and lies her to without being taken aback; the
  grounding among the Molène islands is the offing's tack, for the lead's playtest.

### The gale book judged (the lead, 2026-10-24), from the trials' logs and no live play

The owner ruled that a live play at a station was not needed to judge the book, since
the judgement is of the ship's behaviour and the trials' logs hold it; the two trials were
run on the merged tree with 70 (`trial()` of the test file, twenty hours each) and read.

**The lee shore** (Ushant five miles under her lee, a westerly gale coming on): 58b's
figures exactly, 1597 lines and `ed48ca3d61e52f20`; hove to for weather at 9720, 15060
and 41940, on passage and beating from 51480, the station at 71340; **never aground**; 29
minutes aback in the twenty hours (the first hours' spells before she lies to, and the
filled-away hour from 39817, where 57's book lay aback every three minutes under the storm
canvas alone). The book does what 58b said: she lies to under the close-reefed main
topsail and the storm staysails without being taken aback, fills away with the
close-reefed topsails set and has way. **Judged right; the expected failure lifted and the
pins set to these figures** (the test's states list, lines and digest; the old beside the
new in the test).

**The station gale** (the frigate keeping her station off Ushant): on the merged tree 998
lines, `809ab25ae0c6dea8`, hove to at 16164, in distress at 42420 and **aground at 42394**
among the islands of the Molène passage, beating for her station in the dark, as 57's
trial did at 44332 and 58b's own tree at 41415. The same figures on the tree before 70
(`5fb193e`, run in a worktree), so 70 moved nothing here; the move from 58b's 864 lines
and `4cb58e9ec1ab55c0` came with 58b's merge over 58a, 67 and 68 (the recurring-lines
rule and the riding rule touch this passage; not bisected, the trial being an expected
failure whose cause is known). The book's part is right (hove to once, never aback lying
to, the staysail taken in before it blows out); the grounding is the offing's tack among
islands with no way to wear (57's finding), the captain's and not the book's. **Stays an
expected failure, its reason naming the merged tree's figures and the true cause, for the
next captain's pass** (booked with 71's brief as the captain's helm in action, item 8,
and the offing's tack beside it).

### The lead at the merge (2026-10-23): the one whole suite, and the regatta's finish

Merged over 58a and 67 (the last of the three); the four passages that both 58a's recurring
rule and this package move were re-measured on the merged tree (the merchant passage
`6abbbff4d7fa1a57`, the fake captain `1c9a985bfd5dce0f`, the trade trial with the stranger
`48b205b4f587256c`, the intent schooner `585c52675f10e590`; every line count and state
figure as above). **The one whole suite on the merged tree of 68, 58a, 67 and 58b**
(`--slow -n 4 -m "not pace"`, the lead's machine, nothing else running, 68 minutes): 3,914
passed, 12 expected failures (the eleven known and the lee-shore trial, above), 2 skipped,
**one failed: truth 90, the regatta's first course**, the rules-based captain not finished
in thirty hours. The pace tests alone, after it: 6 passed.

**The regatta's miss, and whose it is.** The course's finish is "within the radius of the
outer road", a mile (package 44's judgement). Before this package the frigate from off
Ushant raised the Falmouth cutter at 51960 making under eight knots, the pilot came aboard
at once, and she stood on to anchor at 52800 within the mile (finished at 53076, 14 h 44 m).
Now she comes to the pilot at eight knots (55920), the cutter cannot put him aboard and asks
her to heave to (the rule is 44's, not this package's), she heaves to at 56521 and takes him
at 56580, and at 56760 the captain, with the tide not serving to enter and the road's leg
reached (a mile and a half, `Planner._port_track`), brings her up where she lies: the best
bower in ten fathoms and a half at 57142, **1.2 miles from the road's centre, in port by
the game's rule (the port's reach, 45) and not finished by the course's.** By bisection on
this package's tree alone (`_casts` and `_stream_changed` each turned off, then both): both
off gives the old finish at 53076 to the tick; either alone gives the miss (the casts off:
the pilot's fix at 52800, hove to for him at 52932, anchored 53705, 1.3 miles off; the
layings off: hove to for casts at 4173 and 38181, the pilot's fix at 55980, anchored 56833,
1.3 miles off). So it is not one item's but the approach's: either item brings her to the
pilot with way on, and a captain hove to for his pilot with the tide foul anchors in the
road where he is, which is right. The builder did not see it because the whole slow tier
was stood down on the lead's word (above).

**Taken: the course's radius is the game's own reach for a road.** `data/regatta/
ushant-to-falmouth.yaml` `radius_nm` 1.0 to 1.5, the reason in the file; the captain's
road leg has been reached at a mile and a half since 45 and the course's mile was a
judgement made before it. With it she finishes at **56711 (15 h 45 m; was 53076, 14 h
44 m), no grounding, no damage**, the replay to the same digest; the twelve regatta tests
pass. Not taken: a captain who stands on to the road's centre after taking his pilot (he
would be sailing a mile into a tide he has just said does not serve), or a course that
counts "in port" (the regatta judges by the truth). For the owner: the frigate of the
regatta now heaves to for a cast of the deep-sea lead a quarter of an hour into her passage
and loses most of that quarter; a captain bound for Falmouth, not racing, would; whether
the rules captain should cast on a leg he has just laid from a known departure is item 2's
figure (`cast_hour_fathoms`, the first cast an hour into the leg) and his to tune.
- **The fraction**: kept at two thirds; a stronger penalty on a wind is a physics change.
- Taken another way: **the deep-sea lead's bring-to** once a watch and only off a lee
  shore and not beating; **the band under the reefs** withdrawn; the stern's line said
  from the evolutions' runner (outside the files listed, one call).

## Package 70: the combat core (2026-10-24)

The first package of milestone 7, built in a worktree off `5fb193e`. Spec M7 Part 7-ii (§7
to §12) "as built (package 70)"; `docs/agents/Harness.md` §21c; the primer's chapter 22;
truths 7-133 to 7-142; the first action's scenario. The physics of the hull, the sails and
the sea is read by the hit model and not changed; no ship file was touched by hand (every
figure through `tools/gen_ships.py` with its source beside it); the consent records were not
touched; no recorded passage moved (the sailing truths and the pinned passages ran green
with the package in: an action package should move no sailing passage, and this one did not,
which the whole fast tier and the slow tier of the touched files say below).

### Item 1's design, as built

`docs/design/Design-WorkInAction.md`, written before anything else. The reading that held:
the quarter bill is a second assignment of the same men (`Sailor.quarters`; `Sailor.at` the
gun's key while he is at it), beaten by `crew/quarters.py` and stood down by `secure the
guns` or `pipe down`; a gun's service is a cycle the battery steps each tick while hands and
powder last (`combat/guns.py`, not an evolution: every phase an evolution would have queued
the player's orders behind it); `engage her to starboard`, `load with chain`, `aim at her
rigging`, `fire as they bear` are standing intentions kept until changed, and the broadside
at the word, a gun by name, `cease firing` and the strike ride over them; sail work at
quarters takes the trimmers and then the guns by the bill's priority (`Runner._rob_the_guns`
after `hands.request`), the line saying from where, and the hands go back to their guns
each tick (`Quarters.tick` from `Runner.step`). Morale is the ship's one figure (the
reason in `combat/morale.py`'s head). Taken another way from the lead's reading: the beat to
quarters is a crew order beside `call all hands` and not an evolution, because an all-hands
evolution queues behind the tack or the heave-to in hand and the drum must not (the first
smoke had a crewed cutter wait ten minutes for her drum while her heave-to failed); and
casting loose and securing, though evolutions for their time, take their hands from the
crews at the guns and not the runner's pool (a frigate's company is minutes coming up the
hatchways, and the first measure had her guns never come loose).

### Each item against its intent

1. **The quarter bill and work in action: built**, as above. Found on the way: the beat and
   the cast loose as the design first had them (all-hands evolutions) queued and starved;
   both changed with the reason written in their files.
2. **Guns as parts: built**, the cutter's two fits, the frigate, the brig, the merchant
   brig; the schooner, the lugger and the smack left to 75 with their shape settled (the
   generator's `armament`/`quarter_bill` builders take any ship). `GunSpec`, `FitSpec`,
   `ArmamentSpec`, `QuarterBillSpec` in the schema; `Gun(Part)` with its load state;
   `Magazine` as a store from the fit's figures. A dismounted gun is out of the bill.
3. **The gunnery's cycle: built**, the four evolutions and the gun deck's orders
   (`orders/gunnery.py`, object `gunnery`); the rates fall out of the muster (below).
4. **Shot and the hit model: built** (`combat/shot.py`): point blank 250 yd for a long gun
   and 230 for a carronade, random shot 1,200 and 800 (the 3-pounder and the 12-pounder
   carronade; by the log of the calibre), the bands 0.9 at a quarter of point blank, 0.5
   at point blank, 0.2 at twice; heel and the lee port, the roll and the sea's scatter.
5. **Damage as state: built** (`combat/hits.py`): a line shot away by the strain model's
   own parting (`how="shot away"`), a spar by its wrecking, a sail's area cut
   (`Sail.holed_m2`), a gun dismounted, a boat stove, the helm lost (`extra["helm_lost"]`:
   the rudder held where it is), the shot hole written with its place against the
   waterline for 73's well (no water flows: the first water was not cheap, since the well
   is 73's own reading), the men at the part struck killed and wounded in the muster.
6. **The fighting instructions, the engaging and morale: built**: the doctrine as data in
   every role's file, the privateer's new file, the fighting book, the strike by rule.
   *Morale is the ship's one figure*, decided so because the colours are one decision for
   the whole company and a division's temper has nothing to act on until 73's fight on
   deck. The strike wants a shot that told as well as fire (found on the way: the merchant
   brig struck to shot that missed).
7. **Recognition before fire: the least of it, built**: a shot at a sail not made out as an
   enemy is told once (`action.unrecognised`) and the ship carries `extra["outlaw"]` for
   the ports' stance; 71 will find the hook at `combat.action._recognition` (the lookout's
   nation and `shows_colours`) and the colours as a state (`extra["colours"]`, the shadow's
   `struck`).
8. **The stations in action: built**: the readings in every sample and their deltas, the
   events and the tripwire, the director's two things and `say as` a gun captain, the truth's
   guns and damage. The cost of thinking against the cycle: a frigate's broadside comes
   every 104 s, a cutter's carronade every 60 or so; a model whose reply takes a minute of
   the ship's time at the usual pace misses a broadside, which the station's line says in
   its minutes-since clause; nothing in the sample grew for the action but the rows that
   changed.
9. **The first action, the pace and the far fight: built** and measured (below).
10. **The records: this section**, the spec, the Harness, the primer, the director's
    library (the forms' examples are the library's), the suite as run.

### The figures and their sources

- The guns (`tools/gen_ships.py`): the cutter's 12-pounder carronades of 6 cwt (the
  Admiralty's fit of the 1790s), her long 3-pounders of 7 cwt with eight half-pounder
  swivels (the hired and revenue cutters' fit; the Establishments and Lavery, *Arming and
  Fitting*, from memory and marked UNVERIFIED in the file); the frigate's 26 long
  18-pounders of 42 cwt, 8 and 2 32-pounder carronades of 17 cwt, 2 long 9-pounder chasers
  (Winfield's *Amazon* class, from memory, UNVERIFIED); the brig's 16 32-pounder carronades
  and 2 long 6-pounders; the merchant brig's 4 6-pounders. Gun crews by weight (a long gun
  2 + cwt/5, a carronade 3 + cwt/8; Douglas 1820 and the quarter bills' usage). The rounds
  per gun: 60 round, 6 grape, 6 chain for a King's ship (the Ordnance's allowance; UNVERIFIED
  figure), 40 for a hired cutter, 20 for a merchantman.
- The exercise (`combat/guns.py` `PHASES`): a long gun's seven phases 85 s nominal, a
  carronade's 60 s, a swivel's 35 s (Douglas 1820, part II, the words of command; the
  seconds judgement, pinned by truth 7-135); a light long gun worked faster with its
  weight to a floor of 0.65; the crew factor the numbers (squared, `NUMBERS_POWER`), the
  rating against the ordinary seaman's, the fatigue, the seaway and the weather's factor.
- The ballistics (`combat/shot.py`): point blank and random by the log of the calibre;
  elevation 10° and depression 4° for a long gun, 11° and 5° for a carronade; the heel
  added to or taken from the quoin by the side; a port shut within a foot (`PORT_SHUT_M`).
- The hit's allotment (`combat/hits.py`): at the hull 55/25/20 hull/deck/rigging, at the
  rigging 12/13/75, between wind and water 65/20/15 (judgement after Douglas on where
  shot fired low and high tell); shot holes below the waterline 12 per cent, 25 more at
  fifteen degrees of heel with the bottom presented, 30 more under "between wind and
  water"; men hurt per hit 1.5 at the hull, 1.0 on deck, 0.15 aloft for an 18-pound shot
  at close range, scaled by the calibre, halved when spent, trebled by grape toward the
  men (the butcher's bills of 1805, judgement); killed three in ten of the hurt.
- Dismounting: the chance half the shot's weight over the gun's weight in hundredweight,
  capped at 0.85 and floored at 0.03, on a third of the deck's hits (Douglas on heavy shot
  dismounting and light seldom); the first figures (half the gun's weight, three fifths of
  the deck's hits) dismounted two carronades by 3-pounder shot in ten minutes.
- Morale (`combat/morale.py`): the losses' weight 2.0 (a fifth hurt takes two fifths), the
  guns dismounted 0.25, a lower mast gone 0.3, the odds up to 0.25 by the log of the
  broadside weights while under fire; the start and the line by role (a King's ship 0.9 and
  0.1, a cruiser 0.85 and 0.15, a privateer 0.7 and 0.35, a packet 0.6 and 0.3, a merchant
  0.5 and 0.4, a fisherman 0.4 and 0.4), each with its source in the role's file.
- The doctrine's distances: engaged within a mile (a King's ship), a mile and a half (a
  privateer), three cables (a merchant: she fights when caught), nought (a fisherman);
  the fire opened at two cables (the British close) or three (the privateer), the French
  habit doubling it (`NATION_HABITS`); broken off at two to three miles for ten minutes.
- The clearing: a frigate's quarter of an hour and a cutter's five minutes by her length
  between the two (spec M7 §8), the drum a minute and a half, the cast loose a minute
  with the crews at the guns, the securing two.

| The merchant brig under a privateer's fire (7-137) | engaged 10:06, chased down and fired on at a cable 10:14, struck 10:15 at the first shot that told, by the odds (0.37 under 0.4) |
| The far fight at two cables (7-139) | seven rounds of three minutes; the long-gun cutter struck with four hurt and three holes |
| The pace, two crewed cutters in action (7-138) | 538 ticks a second (best of three thousands), against the crewed floor of 60 and the owner's 95 with twelve crewed ships |

The far fight against the near: at two cables the far tables end the two cutters' fight in
twenty-one minutes; the near fight ends in three at a cable and in near two hours at long
shot, so the far fight's range is the figure that decides it, and that is the far brain's
choice, which is 74's. 74 should give the far brains the engaging transition with a range
law (the doctrine's `engage_range_cables` under the nation's habit) and resolve rounds by
`combat.far.fight` with the damage summed into `Vessel.damage`.

### What moved, and the pins

No sailing passage moved: the changes to shared code are read-only to the sailing (the
runner's quarters tick and the robbing act only `at_quarters`; the captain's new states and
stimuli fire only with an enemy in sight; the readings' new rows read state that is empty on
a ship with no guns; the hull's steer reads `helm_lost` only when set; the action's random
stream opens at the first shot, so the strain's list of streams is as it was). **One
captain's trial moved, and it is a finding, not a sailing passage:** the trade-stranger
trial (`tests/test_captain_trials.py`, a British schooner chased by a French brig-sloop),
because the brig, crewed while she chases, now takes the cruiser's `chasing → engaging`
within a mile and chases on in action; the first form of the engaging work kept her at the
beam and she steered across the chase (the schooner ran clear thirty minutes sooner and,
on the earlier tide, took the ground going into Falmouth), so a weaker mark (a smaller
class, or a merchantman) is chased by the navigation's own `give chase` and closed to pistol
shot, the beam law kept for an equal. Proof by bisection: the engaging transition alone
turned off gives every old figure; with it on, the brig runs her down, opens at seven
cables at 17362 and puts two shot through her side, the schooner runs clear at 18300 (17880
at 58b), beats from 19020 and from 45600, anchors at 51240 (the bower at 51849; 53669 at
58b) and is in port at 51900 (53700), waiting in the road for the wind as at 58b; 1248
lines (1407) and the digest 0a480f7a4b7f321a
(48b205b4f587256c). The old figures stand beside the new in the test.

### Found on the way

- A promoted ship took her file's name, so two cutters in one log were both "Sherbourne";
  she takes her vessel's name now (`crews.py`).
- The lookout calls a King's cutter and a trader both "a cutter": a privateer cannot tell
  one from the other by sight, which is honest (the record has privateers mistaking revenue
  cutters), and `man of war near` reads only what the words give ("of war", "frigate",
  "sloop", "revenue").
- The size ranks called a merchant brig (hull class 2) a bigger class than a cutter: a
  merchantman is never an overmatch now; and the player's merchant brig's shadow read as
  "a ship" (class 3) in another ship's lookout, since no far description sails her file;
  `SHADOW_FILES` gives her a trader's words.
- The standing book's conflict rule read `aim at her rigging` and `fire as they bear` as
  contrary orders on the ship; each gun-deck intention is its own thing to it now.
- The bare verbs `run out` and `run in` are the running bowsprit's; the guns' are `run out
  the guns` and `run in the guns`.
- `say as` draws a gun captain by his gun under "Mr", as it addresses any role it does not
  know; a petty officer would be addressed by his plain name (`people._address`), a small
  thing for whoever next touches the people's forms.
- Renard's crewed captain stays a minute in `engaging` after his mark has struck: his
  judgement is once a minute (truth 7-137 waits for it).
- A ship with no guns took the merchant's `evading → engaging` row when caught within
  three cables (the trial's schooner): a ship with no guns never engages now; she runs.
- The gunnery's random stream was opened every tick on any ship with guns, firing or not,
  and the strain's determinism test pins the sailing's list of streams: it opens at the
  first shot now.
- The samples: the eight action rows in every sample grew a frigate's officer's first
  sample past his handover's fold by thirty tokens; the rows ride only while something is
  afoot (at quarters, damaged, hurt, a mark engaged, the colours struck), the readings tool
  still gives every row, and a row's first appearance is itself the delta.

### Decisions for the lead and the owner

- The nation's habit over the role's figures (`NATION_HABITS`) is a judgement from the
  period's commonplaces; the owner may prefer it in the nations' files.
- The privateer's fear of a man of war reads the lookout's words; 71's colours and the
  hail will give it more to read.
- The far fight is measured and not wired; 74 builds it from `combat/far.py`.
- The merchant's `strike_below` of 0.4 under a start of 0.5 means one broadside that tells
  brings her colours down by the odds alone; the record supports it for a privateer's
  prize, the owner may want it softer for an armed Indiaman (a role of her own, 75's).

### The suite, as run

See the report; the fast tier whole (two slices, the fingerprint test re-run alone on a
quiet tree), the slow tier of the touched files, the whole slow tier once, the pace tests
alone and last.

## Package 71: signals and the voice between ships (2026-10-24)

The second package of milestone 7, built in a worktree off `bca885c`. Spec M7 Part 7-i
(§1 to §6) "as built (package 71)" and the §10 line for the habits moved;
`docs/design/Design-Signals.md` (the data shape, written first); `docs/agents/Harness.md`
§21d; the primer's chapter 23; truths 7-143 to 7-151; the encounter and the convoy
scenarios. The physics is read and not changed; no ship file was touched; the consent
records were not touched; no model identifier anywhere.

### The data shape's design

`docs/design/Design-Signals.md`, written before anything else: one root a directory under
`data/signals/`, the same six files in each (`book.yaml` the declaration, `numerary.yaml`
the day signals mapped to what a commanded captain does, `telegraphic.yaml` the dictionary,
`night_fog.yaml`, `convoy.yaml`, `private.yaml` the private table's form), a nation naming
its root and its system in `data/nations.yaml`, `basic` the foundation every nation stands
on; colours a state of both bodies with the nation shown read by every lookout; a signal a
thing hoisted by an evolution and read a minute after it is seen by whoever holds the book;
`under the orders of` the least relation; the hail's three bodies by table. What was
rejected is in the note (one file a nation; signals by number as the form; the hoist as an
instantaneous state; every captain obeying every signal; the squadron's work; the true
nation in the reading; a bell line per far ship per fog; the table in the save; the whole
dictionary). The shape held through the build; the note's postscript says the two places
it grew (the least captain for a brainless vessel; the goal `in company with the ship`).

### Each item against its intent

1. **Colours as state: built.** `signals.Colours` (shown, none, false, struck, distress)
   on the far vessel's and the crewed ship's one `Locker`, the player's shadow his; the

   the truth the director's; the orders of `orders/signals.py`; the scenario's `colours:
   British` on a French ship false colours; the lookout's `colours.changed` line; the
   privateer's doctrine (`false_colours`, `true_colours_cables: 4`,
   `bluff_private_signal`); every rules captain's true colours before his first shot;

   the witnesses' `pirates` set; the recognition completed in `action._recognition`
   (the colours against the wars, the private signal, the hail, the shot) with 70's
   `unrecognised` the exception; the vocabulary's refusal gone. Taken another way: `haul
   down the colours` under fire is the strike (the custom; the spec's `haul down` and
   `strike` are one act in action and two out of it).
2. **The private signal: built.** The table a pure function of the seed, the nation, the
   year and the month from the root's form (the real tables are lost; the game's made and

### The books' sources and what was made

Howe's signal book of 1790 and the Admiralty's *Signal Book for the Ships of War* of 1799
(the meanings; the numbers 1, 13, 16, 63, 72 and 76 remembered, the rest made and marked);
Popham's *Telegraphic Signals or Marine Vocabulary*, 1800 and 1803 (the telegraph flag, the
alphabet of twenty-five with J wanting and V before U as the hoist of 21 October 1805
spells 'duty', the eight numbers of that hoist: do 220, England 253, every 261, expects
269, his 370, man 471, that 863, will 958; every other number made between them in the
book's alphabetical order); the night and fog signals bound with the 1799 book (the form:
lights in number and place, false fires, rockets, guns; guns, muskets, the bell and the
drum in fog; every hoist made); the *Signals and Instructions for Ships under Convoy* (the
form and the meanings; the numbers made); the *Regulations and Instructions* of 1806 (the
private signals' custody; the lights of ships in company; the fog signals' intervals from
memory); du Pavillon's tabular signals of 1776 and the Republic's *Code de signaux* of the
1790s (the French meanings in their own phrases where remembered: *virer de bord vent devant
par la contre-marche*, *combattre de plus près*, *branle-bas de combat*; every number made);
Falconer (HAIL, SIGNAL) and Luce 1884 ch. XX for the hail's custom. All from memory and
said so in every file; no page of these is in `docs/references/`; 76 builds the books out
against the printed editions.

### The hail's tables

`data/captains/hail.yaml`: eight question kinds matched in the words (what ship, whence,
whither, cargo, news, the captain, the days out, heave to); the answers by role (a King's
ship, a cruiser, a commodore name themselves by the nation's style, "His Majesty's",
"the French national", "His Catholic Majesty's"; a merchant, a packet, a fisherman, a
privateer; and `lie`, the merchant's table under false colours); the home ports and the
lie's names by nation; the cargo by the description's words (deep laden, a cargo; else in
ballast). The words are the builder's in the period's form and marked made.

So the helm's law alone takes the half hour aback out of the King's cutter's circle (the

### Found on the way

- 70's `NATION_HABITS` keyed `netherlands` where the table says `batavian-republic`: the
  Dutch fought by the default (fixed by the move to data).
- The privateer's doctrine had no row from `keeping station` on `stranger near`, so a
  privateer on her cruising ground sat still until an enemy came within her engaging
  distance (the cruiser has the row); given it, with the bisection above.
- A hoist created with its breaking-out minute at the order was read by the other ship
  before the hands had run it up when the evolution queued behind a wear; the script sets
  the moment now (`NOT_YET` until then), and a hoist never run up comes down after a glass.
- The private signal's wait counted from the order; it counts from the flags' breaking out.
- The frigate's captain took a British merchant brig's silence to the private signal for
  the tell and engaged her; a trader's rig is a stranger to be spoken.
- A commodore challenged his own merchantmen; a ship under his orders is no stranger.
- The planner lays no way into Plymouth from the south-west that the land guard accepts
  (`bound for Plymouth` from off the Lizard "crosses the land on the leg to Cawsand Bay",
  via the Eddystone or the Start the same): the encounter's brig is bound for Falmouth and
  the convoy for the Start. For whoever next touches the port tracks (61's route finding).
- `_keep_company` follows the commodore's drift when he has no way (the first convoy had
  a commodore with no valid intent and the brigs' heads swung with his drift): with a
  sailing commodore it holds; a `company` leg under a stopped ship is 72's to steady.
- `role_for` never gave the commodore's role: `convoy the trade from <A> to <B>` (and
  `escort the convoy to <place>`) is a passage intent that does (`Intent.convoy`).
- The answering pendant of every brig was logged into every other brig's story; only read
  signals are, now.
- The far body's `far_order` had no words for the colours or a signal; `signals.far_order_words`
  gives them for the director's hand.
- 70's `extra["colours"] = "struck"` string, set in two places and read by none, is the
  locker's state now.
- **The hoist flew from the book's minute, not the hands' finishing**: `MakeSignalScript.begin`
  set `breaks_out` at the start tick plus the book's `hoist_s`, but the phase runs at the
  hands' factor (the convoy brig's three hands took two minutes), so the readers saw and
  read flags not yet up and the "signal is up" line came a minute after they had obeyed
  it. The script sets `breaks_out` at the first phase's end and `complete_at` at the last
  (`NOT_YET` until then), and the convoy's and the encounter's pins moved by a minute
  (above).
- **A telegraphic sentence could not be read**: `Locker.tidy` gave a telegraphic hoist two
  minutes of life from its breaking out, while a sentence of n words completes n minutes
  after it and is read a minute later; every sentence of more than two words was hauled
  down before any reader could read it. Its life runs from `done_at` now (the completion),
  `NOT_YET` while the words are going up.
- **The chase went after the wrong sail**: the captain's bare `give chase` left the sail to
  the order, whose pool (45c) counts a sail under our own colours no stranger, so the
  encounter's frigate, having judged the cutter under British colours an enemy by the
  private signal, gave chase to the merchant brig two miles off while the privateer ran.
  Three mends: the captain names his stranger's rig when the lookout has it
  (`Captain._chase_order`, "chase the cutter"); a sail the captain holds an enemy
  (`recognised[..].enemy`, `pirates`) is a stranger to the bare order whatever she shows
  (the books' standing orders `keep her bearing` and `more of her` give the bare order
  every glass); and `the cutter` was a *sail word* of the lookout's (35's pilot cutter, the
  one sail in sight) that named the nearest sail of any rig, so even the named order chased
  the brig: `cutter`, `lugger` and `sloop` are rig words now, the nearest-sail reading kept

## Package 72: the naval system (2026-10-24)

The third package of milestone 7, built in a worktree off `356e7ba`. Spec M7 Part 7-vi
(§21 to §23) "as built (package 72)" and the §3 and §6 lines for the succession and the
least relation; `docs/design/Design-Squadrons.md` (the design, written first, with its "As
built" postscript); `docs/agents/Harness.md` §21e; the primer's chapter 24; truths 7-152 to
7-160; the three scenarios `convoy-six.yaml`, `blockade.yaml`, `squadron.yaml`. The physics
of the hull, the sails and the sea is read and not changed; no ship file was touched; the
consent records were not touched; no model identifier anywhere.

### The set's design, in a paragraph

A squadron is a genuine set (`Squadron` in `freesail/world/squadrons.py`, the registry on
the World): members in the order of sailing, a commander, a kind, a formation whose slots
are laid in the commander's frame with the leeward side by the wind, an interval, a book.
The set writes 71's least relation on every member and clears it when she leaves, so one
hoist still works the whole; it moves as one brain at far detail, every other member on the
plan leg `("station", set)` laid every minute at the set's pace, which is the slowest
member's and a cap on the commander's far body; it is ticked once a minute after the brains
and before the bodies, and that minute is the stragglers, the pace, the commander's reading
of the signals flying and his book. A promoted member's captain is `in company` and keeps
station by the near order; the commander's book runs on whichever rules captain holds the
commodore's station and falls silent under a model. The regimes are data; the business
draws by them and follows the player's ship.

### Each item against its intent

1. **The set: built.** `Squadron`, `Squadrons`, `sets_from_scenario`; join, leave, set the
   commander, detach and recall a division, split; the readings and the director's forms.
2. **One brain at far detail and the promotion in station: built, measured.** The station
   leg, the pace cap, `in company` for the promoted captain, the far brain's `resolve_state`
   laying the leg; the promotion keeps the line (7-155). The pace figures below.
3. **Formations and station keeping as a standing-order kind; the wake: built.** The four
   formations; `keep station` as a held order of the navigation (`freesail/orders/station.py`)
   given by the `in company` book every two minutes and by the player; the succession by the
   wake within a set, 71's three minutes outside one (`signalling._succession`).
4. **The book, the commodore's and escort's doctrine, the model at the flagship: built.**
   `data/squadrons/*.yaml` with sources; the commodore's chasing rows and `chase_stale_hours`;
   the escort's cover (`COVER_NM`) and the cut-out withheld within it; the model commands by
   `make the signal` and the book says nothing under him.
5. **Regimes in data with the nations' knobs: built the shape and the first of each**
   (`data/regimes.yaml`, `naval:` in `data/nations.yaml`, `regimes.py` for in ordinary and the
   sortie, the intent `blockade <port>`); 79 builds them out.
6. **The business's convoys and squadrons, and the player followed: built.** `_convoy`,
   `_blockades`, `_in_ordinary`, `_follow`, `_carried_over`; `population.convoys: 1`,
   `carry_over_nm: 30` (judgement: a convoy half an hour's sail from the edge is still the
   player's weather).
7. **The weather's seasonal bound (R-39): built under a switch, off.** `Weather.bound`, a
   soft scale on the systems' summed anomaly and their wind (`bound_at`), on by the
   scenario's `weather_bound: seasonal`; the unit test holds the glass to June's ceiling
   (1046 hPa: the background with the strongest high and the four-hectopascal margin) where
   two highs would give 1057; truth 7-158 keeps it off in every recorded scenario. Taken only
   this far: the blockade's gale is a scripted low and wants no bound; the recorded passages
   are not re-measured because nothing moves with the switch off. Iberia's drift (the cold
   review's finding) is 79's.
8. **The planner across the land (61): left to 78, with the reason.** The convoys sail the
   Channel's open water and the Brest blockade works from seaward; what the convoys did want
   was Plymouth's track to sea moved off the land (`data/ports/plymouth.yaml`: by Cawsand Bay
   and the Rame), which was data and is done; 61's graph is not.
9. **Readings, events, forms, truth, harness: built.** `the squadron`, `the convoy`, `the
   order of sailing`, `the station`; the events listed in Harness §21e; the forms
   `squadron.new`, `squadron.act`, `convoy`, `ship.regime` after `WORLD_ORDER_FORMS`; the
   channels `squadron` and `convoy`; the director's truth with every ship's set and regime.
10. **Scenarios, truths, records: built.** Below.

### The three days at seed 7

- **The convoy of six and the privateer** (`convoy-six.yaml`): the Friendship a mile astern
  (a dull sailer, `sailing_factor: 0.85`) is a straggler by the book's ten minutes; No. 20
  ordered at 2760, up at 2866 (the hands slow at it behind a wear), answered at 3000; back in
  her station at 5280; every ship within 165 m of her station from 7200 on (the far leg holds
  at the tolerance's edge, half a cable, and the commodore's own turns add the rest). The
  privateer schooner investigates from 600 and evades at 3600 at two miles from the
  commodore (`man_of_war_nm: 2.5`), twenty miles off by 10800. The owner's cut-out needs
  an uncovered straggler: the escort in company covers the six, and the unit test has the
  cut-out with a merchantman alone.
- **The blockade of Brest blown off** (`blockade.yaml`): the scripted low (978 hPa passing
  490 km north of the start, the gale day's radius) gives 34 knots from 226° at T+3h, 38 at
  the height, under 28 by T+10h, under 22 by T+11h; the inshore squadron's far commodore
  stands off the land in the rising southerly (his station book's offing) and is blown off
  by the book at 11400; the goal restored at 37920; the lights at 38640; the Hortense out at
  43200, an hour after the wind fell under the fresh breeze. The player's frigate on the
  Ushant station is hove to from T+3h to T+8h30 and keeping her station after, by her book.
- **The squadron promoting in station** (`squadron.yaml`): at far detail the two members
  within a cable of their stations at 3600 (about 40 m while the commodore steers steady);
  under the default cap all three crewed by 600 and within a cable and a half at 7200,
  their captains in company. The first build of the near order lost the line (below).

### The pace

`py tools/pace.py squadrons` on the build machine, quiet (load 0.3 to 0.7), each the best of
three thousands after the scenario's first ten minutes:

| The convoy of six and the privateer | ticks a second |
|---|---|
| at far detail alone (the player's brig crewed; seven far bodies, two with brains) | 551 |
| under the default cap (the privateer promoted; the merchantmen brainless and far) | 328 |
| under a cap of twelve | 311 |

The far-detail figure of the scenario is the player's brig's: her physics and her crew's
sail-handling while her rules captain beats up Channel are four fifths of the tick (a
profile of a thousand ticks: the set's own minute is not in the first forty entries, and
the far side, six station legs with their tide, is a fifth), and it ran 483 to 551 on quiet
runs by the day's load; inside the pace set it gave 483 and failed the floor once. Truth
7-159 therefore measures the convoy at far detail in truth 51's own form, beside the
brains' frigate as the frigate with the dozen is measured (a far commodore with his brain
and the convoy's book, six brainless merchant brigs on the station leg, the set's minute,
a privateer with her brain): **581 ticks a second** (load 0.7) against `BUILD_MACHINE_FLOOR`
500; truth 7-160 keeps the scenario itself under the default cap and a cap of twelve
against the crewed floor 60 (318 to 328). The owner's baseline of 95 ticks a second with
twelve crewed ships is not touched by this package (the merchantmen without brains are
never promoted, so a convoy's cap is spent on the escort and the enemy). The tool keeps
the scenario's own figure for the owner's play. The early figure during the build, a
frigate with the dozen far ships of the merchant passage, was 491 before the set's minute
was tightened (the stations cached per tick, the slots computed once a minute). The set's
minute costs one `stations()` per set per minute and one perception per commander per
minute; a brainless member on the station leg costs a far body's tick and nothing more.

### What moved, and the pins

No recorded passage's pin moved: the weather's bound is off in every recorded scenario
(truth 7-158), the planner's graph is not built, Plymouth's track to sea is read only by a
captain bound into or out of Plymouth (no recorded passage is), and the physics is
untouched. The slow tier ran whole after the package (the counts below) with no truth
re-pinned. 71's convoy (truth 7-145, four ships under orders outside a set) keeps its three
minutes. Three mends followed the whole slow tier (below) and the three files they touch
were run again under `--slow`; nothing else changed after it but truth 7-159's form and
these notes.

### Found on the way

- **The near station order's two faults** (both mended in this package): the flag's course
  taken from her own heading when the tops had not made it out, which turned the station with
  every helm she put; and the helm put again only against the course last computed, which
  crept a few degrees a glass and never turned her. With the set's course and the ordered
  course she keeps station to a cable and a half through two hours under the default cap.
- **A promoted ship's World built the sets again** from the scenario's `squadrons:` and failed
  for want of the ships; her World carries none now.
- **The chart has two Black Rocks**: Brest's (`pierres-noires`, the plural) and Falmouth's
  drying rock (the singular); the intents read them apart.
- **`blockade Brest` on the road itself** took a frigate from the west through the Four and
  onto the Plâtresses in twenty-eight minutes; the port's blockade station is the mend.
- **The gradient-wind rule** makes a scripted low's surface wind nearly flat in strength
  across hours (24 knots for eleven hours in the first draft of the blockade's low at 400 km,
  18 at 250 km): the gale comes from the low passing at about the radius, as the gale day's
  does. Noted for whoever scripts the next gale.
- **The rules captain on a station under the land** stands off forty miles in a rising
  onshore wind (his book's offing), which emptied Brest's offing and let the sortie out
  before the gale in the first draft; the regime's wind ceiling is the mend. His keeping

- **A brainless member is never promoted** (the crews' switch promotes ships with brains);
  the squadron scenario's members carry intents for that reason.
- **YAML reads a bare `on:` key as `True`**; the books' loader normalises it.

### Decisions for the lead and the owner

- The weather's bound stays under its switch until the owner has judged it on a passage of
  days; the switch is `weather_bound: seasonal` in a scenario.
- `CUT_OUT_M` is hailing distance (four cables), the far chase's own stop; 74's far fight

## Package 73: water, damage control, health and the fight on deck (2026-10-27)

The fourth package of milestone 7, built in a worktree off `7da0c0e` (the branch
`claude/pkg-73`). Spec M7 §11, §11a, §13 to §17 "as built (package 73)" and the §9 line for
the men struck; `docs/design/Design-WaterAndHealth.md` (the design, written first, with its
"As built" postscript); `docs/agents/Harness.md` §21f; the primer's chapter 25; the
director's library page's fifth section; truths 7-172 to 7-184 (the owner's local package took
7-161 to 7-171); the scenario `leak.yaml`. The physics of the hull, the sails and the sea is
read and not changed (the free surface is applied where the stability was already a figure:
`Hull.gm_m`, read by the equilibrium heel and the motion's particulars); the ship files were
regenerated through `tools/gen_ships.py` (the pumps, the shot plugs, the quarter bill's
small-arms men and boarders, the marines' two roles) with the sources beside each figure; the
consent records were not touched; no model identifier anywhere.

### The design, in a paragraph

The water in a ship is one quantity, the tons the keeper of every World sums each tick from
its sources (the shot holes by the orifice law, the ground, the seams in a seaway, the sea
shipped, the director's seams), the well's depth the tons over the bilge's floor, the pumps a
standing work of the hands' pool at Falconer's rates, the free surface a loss of metacentric
height the physics reads, foundering at half the displacement. The wounded, the sick and the
dead are states of the muster with the surgeon's queue and the courses the health keeper
works once a minute, the needs' ends among them; a station holder is a man of the muster with
his roads at parity. The marines' kit is data by nation, their fire a standing intention within
musket shot of a near deck, the fight on deck a round a minute by strengths; every repair an
evolution competing for hands. Everything is state the readings give and the log says.

### The figures and their sources (judgement marked)

| Figure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| orifice coefficient | 0.6 | the sharp-edged orifice's discharge coefficient (hydraulics' commonplace) |
| chain pump / hand pump | 80 / 15 t/h at 4 / 2 men | Falconer 1780, PUMP (a ton a minute for the chain pump) |
| the pumps' rate by numbers | numbers^1.5 × skill / (fatigue × seaway) | judgement |
| spell at the brakes | 30 min | Falconer 1780, SPELL; judgement |
| suck under | 0.05 m | judgement |
| well floor | 0.45 L B | judgement (the frigate's metre of water 220 t, the cutter's 40) |
| seams working | 0.02 t/h per 100 t × ((roll − 6°)/4)², cap 25°; ×3 for 24 h after a grounding | the "sucked the pumps dry at eight bells" of a sound ship; judgement |
| sea shipped | 2 t/h per m of sea over 3 m × L/20, unless battened | judgement |
| free surface | l b³/12 ∇, l = 0.6 L, b = B·min(1, 0.15 + depth/(0.5 T)), from 0.1 m | the free-surface correction; the breadth floor judgement |
| founder / settling | 0.5 / 0.6 of the displacement's water | judgement |
| shot plugs | frigate 40, brig 20, schooner and cutter 8, merchant brig 4, lugger 4, smack 2 | the carpenter's stores by rate; judgement |
| plug a hole | 600 s above water, 1200 s within 0.5 m under, 2400 s deeper; caulking 10800 s | Falconer 1780, LEAK; judgement |
| fother | the hole's rate less 0.3 while under 6 kn | Falconer 1780, FOTHERING; judgement |
| fish / jury | sprung under 60, fished to 70; a jury mast 0.4 of the rating, condition 40 | Luce 1884 ch. XXXI; judgement |
| the wound | killed 0.3; light / grave half and half | the actions' returns (James); judgement |
| the surgeon | light 600 s (a mate), grave 1800 s; messmates 3600 s; first come first served | Turnbull 1806; judgement |
| the courses | light 7–14 d (×1.5 untreated); grave judged at 24 h: dies 0.3 treated / 0.6 not, else invalid 40 d; sick 3–7 d | the surgeons' journals, from memory; judgement |
| the sick list | foul water 0.02/day; short allowance 0.01/day past 7 d; water out: sick 0.1/day from day 2, dead 0.05/day from day 4 | Trotter, Medicina Nautica; judgement |
| the needs' ends | thirst 72 h collapse / 96 h death; hunger 7 d / 21 d | the medical commonplaces; judgement |
| the bill | 600 s after the last shot | judgement |
| quarterdeck share | 0.2 of the shot's hits aft, 0.4 of the musketry's | spec M7 §11 (history's lesson); judgement |

| the crossing | the defenders' marines at five times the 50-yd chance; a loaded gun bearing one man each | judgement |

| the doctrine | board_odds 1.3 (King's ship, cruiser, commodore), 1.0 privateer, 0 merchant and packet; board_when her guns silent (no shot of hers for five minutes; a mark that never answered boarded after a quarter of an hour's engagement); musketry_cables 1; marines_tops kit; pumps_at_m 0.3; give_up_at_share 0.4; damage_priority the leak, the rigging, the guns | sources in each `data/captains/*.yaml` row |

### What was measured

- **The orifice law.** An 18-pounder's hole half a metre under the frigate's waterline:
  85 t/h; a 12-pounder's a third of a metre under: 50 t/h (7-172, `test_water`). The frigate's
  four pumps with twelve hands lift 190 t/h and gain; three men at a hand pump lose.
- **The carpenter.** The hole half a metre under plugged in twenty minutes, the plug counted,
  the pumps sucking after (7-173).
- **Foundering.** The cutter with three 18-pounder holes a metre under (some 300 t/h against
  her 30) founders in the hour, the lines in order: the well rising, the pumps losing, settling,
  "She is going down: the water has beaten the pumps; the pumps lost her at 10:00" (7-174).
- **The Manacles.** The frigate on the rock as the ground tests run her; the pumps gain on the
  leak and `stop the leak` is three hours, after which the ground's leak is nought (7-175).
- **The leak scenario** (`leak.yaml`, seed 7): three seams at 2 t/h in a strong westerly; the
  well shows a foot at 13:00 and the merchant doctrine's captain mans the pumps at 0.3 m
  ("manning the pumps (the well at 0.29 m)"), dry by 13:30, the hand pumps' 30 t/h kept by
  spells; with the captain aside, 0.6 m at 15:00 and `Hull.gm_m` 1.10 → 0.77 (7-184).
- **The surgeon.** Twelve hits on the frigate at seed 7: 20 hurt (4 killed, 16 wounded, 5
  dangerously); the surgeon and two mates clear the queue in three hours; the bill then "four
  killed, five wounded (five dangerously), eleven hurt and at light duty of 264"; at 24 h two
  invalided (7-176, 7-177).
- **Thirst.** The cutter's water and provisions out at seed 7: the captain at the prompt
  collapses at 72 h (day 15 10:00) and is dead at 96 h, the command passing to Mr Pearce; six
  men sick on day 3, two more on day 4, the first hand dead of thirst on day 5, buried the next
  morning (7-178).
- **The musketry.** The frigate's forty marines at thirty metres of a French frigate at seed 7:
  three volleys the first minute, one of her people fallen to a musket ball ("musketry from
  her deck; one killed" in her log); drifting apart at a foot a second the ships are out of
  musket shot in three minutes (7-179). Twenty small-arms men at will from thirty metres
  killed five and wounded seven of a frigate's company in five minutes in a probe (her
  captain's doctrine).
- **The fight on deck.** A hundred boarders against a frigate's 264 awake on deck: the
  crossing's volley costs seven, round one 17 of ours to seven of hers (strengths 50 to 110),
  repulsed, 24 lost to 7 (7-180). Against the same frigate at quarters, her gun crews at the
  guns (118 defenders), with the arms served out: six rounds, 26 of ours to 44 of hers, the
  deck carried, "The colours are struck (carried by boarding)" (7-181).
- **The pace.** The two frigates grappled and fighting ran at the crewed floor's order (the
  fight's round is a few list comprehensions a minute; the musketry a Poisson draw a tick
  within musket shot and nothing beyond); no pace truth was pinned and `K.CREWED_FLOOR_TICKS_S`
  is unchanged.

### The first action at seed 7: a pin moved, the bisection

Package 71 pinned the privateer's strike at **11:12** (3539 s after the first shot, five of
thirty hurt, seven holes). With package 73 whole she strikes at **11:43** (5399 s, four hurt,
seven holes): inside 7-133's band (three quarters of an hour to three) and the same victor,
the minute moved by thirty-one. The bisection, each item off alone and together (the first
action replayed three hours each, `FS73_BISECT` toggles removed after):

| Items off | Struck | Minutes after the first shot | Her hurt | Holes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none (package 73 whole) | 11:43 | 90 | 4 | 7 |
| the marines' and small arms' fire and the boarding (`_musketry`, `_boarding`) | 11:43 | 90 | 4 | 7 |
| the pumps, the repairs and the repel (`_damage_work`) | 11:40 | 87 | 4 | 7 |
| the small arms served out on entering the action (`_fight_ready`) | **11:12** | 59 | 5 | 7 |
| all three doctrine items | 11:12 | 59 | 5 | 7 |
| all three, and the wounds' draws on the gunnery stream | 11:03 | 50 | 4 | 7 |
| the wounds' draws on the gunnery stream alone | 11:11 | 58 | 5 | 9 |

So the water, the health and the damage control alone leave 71's minute exactly (the wounds'
draws moved to the health stream for that reason: on the gunnery's stream they shift every
shot after the first wounded man); the mover is **the small arms served out by both captains
on entering the action** (`board_odds` above nought in the King's ship's and the privateer's
doctrines): the gunner's party of six leaves the guns for five minutes at the start, and the
small-arms men fire at will within a cable thereafter, which with 70's cutters of thirty men
each slows the King's cutter's first broadsides and lengthens the action by half an hour. The
pumps and the carpenter move it three minutes more (in the runs with the small arms off her
holes were plugged at 10:50 and her pumps manned at 11:04 with the well at 0.31 m; in the
whole package's run her seven holes lie above the water and neither is wanted). The pin is re-measured in 7-183 as the band and the new lines, the
old minute beside the new here; the choice to keep the serve-out is realism's (both ships would
arm before an action) and the owner may turn it off per role by `board_odds: 0`.

records. The design and the open items are in `docs/design/Proposal-PivotGun.md`. Two

and dumb show, with every gunnery order unchanged) and

## Between packages 72 and 73: practice at the great guns, and powder and shot taken in (2026-10-25)

Built locally between packages, on `main` of a local repository on its local baseline (the
M7 folder taken from the line's `2774be3`, with the provisional pivot gun and privateer
schooner, above), nothing pushed, **for the lead to fold in**. (Package 86's fold-in: the
owner's local commits this section named are on no branch of the project; the work they
made is on the line at `5b01fdf`, on top of package 73, and the tree he measured before it
is called "the local baseline" below.) The owner's two proposals of the day (`docs/design/Proposal-PracticeFiring.md`,
`docs/design/Proposal-MagazineResupply.md`), approved and built from one design,
`docs/design/Build-PracticeAndResupply.md` (its decisions table names every
judgement call, its §8.2 the truths); the working name in the code and here is "practice and
resupply (between packages 72 and 73)". The lead's stage 0 (the scaffolding, no
behaviour change), then three builders in three worktrees, each with its own review's
fixes: Builder 1 the magazine and the gun deck, Builder 2 the supply, Builder 3 practice;
merged in that order with the merge's own edits, truths 7-161 to 7-171, and the review of
the merged tree with its fixes: ten local commits, all folded in at `5b01fdf`. Spec M7 §8
"as built (practice and resupply)"; `docs/agents/Harness.md` §21g (§21f on his tree); the primer's chapters 14
("Powder and shot") and 22 ("Practice at the great guns"); the owner's scenario
`data/scenarios/exercising-the-great-guns.yaml`. The physics is read and not changed; no
ship file was touched by hand (the five armed files regenerated through
`tools/gen_ships.py`, the topsail schooner, the lugger and the smack byte-identical); the
consent records were not touched; no model identifier anywhere; no new random draw on an
existing path (the one new stream, "practice", opens at a cask's first sighting). **The
truth numbers 7-161 to 7-171** follow 72's 7-160 and are to be agreed with package 73,
whose brief takes "the number after 72's".

### The owner's rulings (2026-10-25)

- **Stages A and B both**: the magazine by kind with the gunner's filling, and powder and
  shot taken in at a port.
- **The Ordnance's issue to a King's ship is free and vouched**; merchants and privateers
  pay.
- **Practice gives no skill**: each gun's drill is counted (`guns.Drill`: the rounds in dumb
  show and live, the timed cycles and the best, the falls at the mark) and nothing reads it
  for pace or aim. The drill counts only.
- **The galley fire out while the powder comes aboard is a state the needs read.**
- **Ship-to-ship transfer is deferred**, with powder from prizes (74's and 82's).

### What was built, and where

1. **The magazine by kind** (`ship/parts.py`: `Magazine` of layout 2, `charge_lb`,
   `fill_seconds`, `split_by_kind`, `fit_levels`, `Wanting`, `powder_words`, `gun_words`,
   `_convert_70`; `ship/schema.py`: `FIT_KEYS` with `charges`, `powder_barrels` and

   barrels' establishment, the shot by calibre and kind as before, `wanting()` what would
   complete her, the gunner's account a tuple of dated receipts. The long Tom's 55

   calibre draw one pool") is mended (truth 7-169).

### The figures and their sources

- **The charges** (`parts.CHARGE_SHARE`, written into each fit as `charges:`): a long gun a
  third of its shot's weight, a carronade a twelfth, a swivel a half, to the ounce. Falconer
  1780, CANNON (from l.4037), quoting Robins at l.4826-4831: the present allowance half the
  ball in the smaller pieces and seven sixteenths in the 32-pounders, a third "or even less"
  an advantage. **That the service charge of 1805 was a third is from memory, UNVERIFIED;
  the carronade's twelfth is from memory, UNVERIFIED** (Falconer is before the carronade);
  the swivel's half is Falconer's smaller pieces (l.4827) applied to a half-pounder,
  judgement. The Regulations' Table No. 29 (OCR l.27498-27502) has lost its figures in the
  OCR; package 75 enters them through the generator from the page image.

  | Gun | Charge | To fill one, man-seconds |
  |---|---|---|
  | long 18 | 6 lb | 210 |
  | long 12 | 4 lb | 180 |
  | long 9 | 3 lb | 165 |
  | long 6 | 2 lb | 150 |
  | long 3 | 1 lb | 135 |
  | carronade 32 | 2 lb 11 oz | 160 |
  | carronade 12 | 1 lb | 135 |
  | swivel ½ | 4 oz | 124 |

- **The barrel**: a hundred pounds (`BARREL_LB`): Falconer 1780, the French glossary, *Baril
  de poudre*, "a powder-cask, containing an hundred pounds of gun-powder" (l.22563-22564).
  The English barrel's weight is UNVERIFIED.
- **The filled allowance and the reserve**: the filled counts are package 70's (a round a
  gun of the allowance and a tenth over for the blank charges, judgement), so that nothing
  an action did before moves; the powder below at completion is half the filled powder,
  rounded up to the barrel (`RESERVE_SHARE`, judgement: the period kept most of its powder
  in the barrels). As committed:

  | Fit | Filled (kind, calibre: n) | Filled powder | `powder_barrels` | `exercise_charges` | The bill's `filling` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | frigate-36 | long 18: 2054; carronade 32: 790; long 9: 316 | 15,395 lb | 77 | 6 | 10 |
  | brig | carronade 32: 1264; long 6: 158 | 3,713 lb | 19 | 4 | 4 |
  | cutter, carronades | carronade 12: 330 | 330 lb | 2 | 1 | 1 |
  | cutter, long guns | long 3: 330; swivel ½: 352 | 418 lb | 3 | none | 1 |
  | privateer-schooner, long tom | long 12: 55; carronade 12: 220; swivel ½: 176 | 484 lb | 3 | none | 1 |
  | privateer-schooner, letter of marque | long 6: 330; swivel ½: 176 | 704 lb | 4 | none | 1 |
  | merchant-brig | long 6: 104 | 208 lb | 2 | none | 1 |

- **The filling**: 120 man-seconds a cartridge and 15 a pound of its charge (`FILL_S_BASE`,
  `FILL_S_PER_LB`, judgement), sixty man-seconds a man a minute. The party is the bill's
  `filling`, one man to every four cannon, the swivels not cannon (Falconer 1780,
  QUARTER-GUNNER, l.14283-14289; `max(1, cannon // 4)` where a bill does not say it): at
  quarters the first of them of the powder division, fit and not lent, read and never moved
  (the Regulations 1806, 1808 printing, the Gunner, Art. XVIII, l.13065-13071: he is to
  take all opportunities of filling powder during an action); out of quarters while the
  idlers are up, 06:00 to 20:00, the gunner and his crew in the filling room notionally;
  never by night out of quarters (Art. VII, l.12843-12850: the magazine not opened until the
  proper officer is in the light room; the night is judgement), never while the hoy is
  alongside (Art. V) and never after the colours are struck. The neediest kind is filled
  first (the lowest share of its level; equal shares in `GUN_KINDS` order, then the larger
  calibre); each barrel emptied is counted for the Ordnance's shilling. One man fills a
  12-pounder carronade's cartridge in 135 s, about one in two minutes and a quarter.
- **The ports and the prices** (the eleven `ordnance:` blocks): the Ordnance's storekeeper
  at Plymouth, in the Sound or Cawsand Bay only (`roads: [outer_road, anchorage]`, the
  Hamoaze the mooring; the Gunner, Art. VI, l.12833-12839: "Plymouth Sound or Cawsand Bay,
  Spithead, ..."), and at Gibraltar, anywhere in port (the storekeeper there from memory,
  UNVERIFIED); the town's merchants selling at Gibraltar and none at Plymouth (UNVERIFIED;
  the owner may flip either). The merchants of Falmouth, St Peter Port, Brest, Lorient,
  Rochefort and St Malo sell at £5 a barrel and £12 a ton of shot, those of Cadiz, Ferrol
  and Lisbon (and Gibraltar's) at £6 and £14: **every price UNVERIFIED**, the project's texts
  giving none, and the merchants' trade in powder at those ports the proposal's list,
  UNVERIFIED. The other 27 port files have no block. A sale is priced to the shilling, a
  shot of grape or chain weighed as the calibre's round shot (judgement), the ton the long
  ton of 2,240 lb. The hoy is alongside four hours after the demand at Plymouth and three
  elsewhere, the taking in at 20 barrels and 2 tons an hour and an hour at the least
  (judgement). The words: the storekeeper of the Ordnance at the port (Art. I,
  l.12722-12738), the galley fire put out and no light but in the light room (Art. V,
  l.12800-12809), the magazine secured and the keys to the captain (l.12815-12827), the
  empty barrels returned at a shilling apiece, the gunner's own (Art. IX, l.12887-12902),
  and a King's ship's purchase of the merchants only of absolute necessity (the Captain,
  Art. VII, l.6220-6252). Lisbon's `sells_in_war_to` is written in its file as a comment and
  left unset.
- **The cask** (`combat/marks.py`, `heave_mark.yaml`): an empty cask with a flag on a staff,
  from memory and UNVERIFIED against a page; hove over by two hands in a minute from the
  quarter, four points abaft the beam (135° from her head) and six tenths of her length
  from her centre (judgement); a metre long, its size term in the hit chance √(1/40), about
  0.16, where every hull under 10 m is given the floor of 0.5 (decision 18); the flag's
  staff 2 m high; made out from the masthead by day within a mile and the visibility, half
  that at twilight (`chart.TWILIGHT_FACTOR`), never by night (judgement); set by the tide's
  stream and blown to leeward at 2 per cent of the wind's base speed, once a minute
  (judgement); given up when she is three miles from it (judgement). The captain is to
  exercise the ship's company frequently at the guns (the Captain, Art. IX, l.8738-8742).
- **The notional mark** (`orders/gunnery.py`): a cutter's length, 20 m, beam-on at any
  bearing (judgement); four points on the bow (45° from her head), on the beam (90°) or on
  the quarter (135°), either side (judgement); it keeps its bearing from her head as she
  turns, and is laid from a cable to the longest random shot of the guns that bear there.
  The arcs that decide which bear are the battery's, unchanged (`combat/guns.py`): a
  broadside gun 35° either side of its beam, a chaser 25° of the bow or the stern, a swivel
  100° of its beam, the pivot 60° to 140° off the bow either side (the owner's ruling,
  above). So no broadside gun or chaser bears on the bow or the quarter, and the frigate and
  the King's cutter are refused a notional mark there; the long Tom bears on the beam and
  the quarter and not the bow. The refusals' suggested mark is four cables on the beam, or
  the whole cables her longest gun reaches when that is less (the King's cutter's 12-pounder
  carronades throw 3.95 cables: three).
- **The allowance for exercise** (`exercise_charges`, King's fits only): a charge and a
  round shot a month for a fourth of the upper deck's guns in a ship of one deck, for six
  months after the guns are received (the Gunner, Art. XXI, l.13122-13144; the Captain's
  chapter, l.8842-8879, gives a third), the first six months' figure, since the game keeps
  no commissioning date (judgement): the frigate 6 (her 26 main-deck guns, a ship of one
  deck: judgement), the brig 4, the King's cutter 1; the hired cutter's long guns, the
  privateer and the merchant brig none. Counted by the month for a King's ship of Britain
  alone; the first round beyond it said once a month and entered in the gunner's account.

### An old game

A checkpoint of packages 70 to 72 (the build design's §1.1 step 3 and §9, decision 7):

- **It has no powder reserve.** Its magazine is converted once to layout 2
  (`parts._convert_70`, logging and drawing nothing): each calibre's filled cartridges and
  rounds fired split over the fit's gun kinds of that calibre (the long Tom's 275 are 55
  and 220), no loose powder below, and the barrels' establishment the old fit's
  `powder_barrels`, which an old pickled `FitSpec` reads as its class default 0. **Until she
  takes powder in**, her establishment is the filled allowance alone: the reading says
  "Powder below: none; no barrels established.", `fill cartridges` answers "There is no
  powder below to fill: the filled cartridges are all she has.", `guns.powder_out` is never
  said, and a demand wants only what makes up the filled allowance's powder. Measured by the
  review: the first action's checkpoint written at the local baseline at tick 2437, in action, and
  resumed on the merged tree (before the review's fixes) converts both magazines with
  `powder_lb` and `reserve_lb` 0.0, the gunners fill nothing, and the game comes to the
  strike at 4320 with the same 311 lines and `a158a30ce39b345d` as the uninterrupted game
  (181 filled in the King's cutter at the strike, against a new game's 207).
- **It may say a once-said magazine line once more.** The battery's once-set for "the
  magazine is out" is now `_said_out`, keyed by gun kind and calibre and starting empty; the
  old float-keyed `_said_no_powder` is left unread (`combat/guns.py`). So "The gunner reports
  no more cartridges for the ...: the magazine is out." may be said once again in a resumed
  game for a kind it was said for before the checkpoint.
- The rest loads as it was: every new attribute on a pickled class is a plain class default
  (`Magazine`, `FitSpec`, `QuarterBillSpec`, `Battery`, `Service`, `Volley`, `Lookout`,
  `Stores`, `Port`), a `Port` reads its block from this build's file, and a `Papers` mends
  its catalogue with the gunner's account at the first miss.
